27143721.Name: Glasgow-1026
27143721.BirthLocation: Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland
27143721.bio:
== Biography ==

'''William Glasgow''' was married to [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]]. They were living in or associated with Kirknewton parish, Midlothian, Scotland, by 1682.

Their daughter [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded there on 21 April 1682, daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook.<ref name="Bessie1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, Bessie Glasgow, 1682; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch record].</ref>

William and Ann were also recorded as the parents of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]], baptised on 22 April 1705.<ref name="William1705">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, 1705; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FY9 FamilySearch record].</ref>

William's own birth, parentage and death have not yet been established from contemporary evidence.

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

This William was previously conflated with [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], who was baptised on 24 September 1671 as a son of Andro Glasgow.<ref name="William1671">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, baptised 24 September 1671, son of Andro Glasgow; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-F2B FamilySearch record].</ref>

The two men cannot reasonably be the same person. [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded as the daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook in April 1682,<ref name="Bessie1682" /> when the William baptised in September 1671 was only ten years old.

The 1671 baptism and the parentage by Andro Glasgow therefore belong to [[Glasgow-3974|William Glasgow]], not this profile.

No contemporary evidence has yet been found establishing this William's date or place of birth or identifying his parents. The former structured father [[Glasgow-1554|Walter Glasgow]] was disconnected on 26 September 2026. Walter was christened in 1649, only about eleven years before this William's estimated birth, and no cited record names Walter as his father.<ref name="Walter1649">FamilySearch, “Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” Walter Glasgow, christened 23 September 1649 in the Kirknewton/East Calder index, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-FWL record VQ4K-FWL].</ref>

=== Marriage ===

William was married to [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]].

No contemporary marriage entry for the couple has yet been identified. Their relationship is nevertheless supported by parish records naming them together as the parents of children in 1682 and 1705.<ref name="Bessie1682" /><ref name="William1705" />

Ann's currently estimated birth date should be checked separately against the 1682 record, since she was already Bessie's mother by that date.

=== Drummore and "Walter" ===

Later online genealogies describe this man as '''William Walter Glasgow''' and associate him with Drummore. No contemporary source has yet been identified establishing either the middle name "Walter" or a Drummore birthplace or residence.

These claims should remain research leads rather than established facts.

=== Ireland ===

Later pedigrees connect this family with County Tyrone, Ireland. The presently identified records do not establish when or whether William himself migrated to Ireland.

The 1759 probate-index entry for [[Glasgow-1025|James Glasgow]] places James at Drumearn, County Tyrone, but does not by itself establish James as William's son or prove a Scottish-to-Irish migration by this William.

=== Priority Research ===

* '''Priority 1 — inspect Bessie's original 1682 parish entry.'''
** Obtain the original Kirknewton Old Parish Register entry behind the FamilySearch index.
** Record the exact wording, residence, father's occupation and witnesses.
** Confirm the spelling of Ann's surname in the original record.

* '''Priority 1 — locate the marriage of William and Ann.'''
** Search Kirknewton and neighbouring Midlothian parishes before April 1682.
** Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow and Glassgow.
** Search McCook and contemporary spelling variants.
** A marriage entry could establish William's residence, parish of origin or other identifying information.

* '''Priority 1 — inspect the original 1705 baptism of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]].'''
** Confirm both parents' names in the original register.
** Compare residence and witnesses with Bessie's 1682 entry.

* '''Priority 2 — reconstruct the complete William and Ann household.'''
** Inspect every Glasgow baptism in Kirknewton and neighbouring parishes between about 1680 and 1710.
** Resolve the parentage of [[Glasgow-1546|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1544|John Glasgow]] from their original records rather than existing tree relationships.

* '''Priority 2 — investigate the County Tyrone connection.'''
** Work backwards from the earliest securely documented members of the Glasgow family in County Tyrone.
** Look specifically for records naming Scottish relatives, places of origin, executors, beneficiaries or other associates capable of linking the Irish family to William and Ann.

27153378.Name: Glasgow-1028
27153378.bio:
== Biography ==
David Glasgow was born about 1586. This date is an estimation based on the christening dates of his known children in the early 17th century.

He is recorded as the father in the christening records of at least two children in the parish of Mid Calder, Midlothian, Scotland:
* '''Elspeth Glasgow''': Christened on 2 March 1606 in Mid Calder, Midlothian.<ref name="ElspethC1606">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-22S : 12 February 2020), David Glasgow in entry for Elspeth Glasgow, christened 2 Mar 1606, Mid Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. Father's Name: David Glasgow.</ref>
* '''Issobell Glasgow''': Christened on 3 May 1612 in Mid Calder, Midlothian.<ref name="IssobellC1612">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-LR9 : 12 February 2020), David Glasgow in entry for Issobell Glasgow, christened 3 May 1612, Mid Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. Father's Name: David Glasgow.</ref>

These records confirm his presence in Mid Calder during this period. Further details about his life, such as his wife's name, his parents, occupation, or death date and place, are not provided in these specific sources and require further research.

== Research Notes ==

=== Parentage ===
[[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]] and [[Anderson-103463|Jonet Anderson]] are retained only as uncertain working parents. Andrew's 1598 testament expressly names Marioune, James, Andrew and William as his four children; David is omitted.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, Andrew Glasgow testament, CC8/8/32 (1598); printed testament index in Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Commissariot Record of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments'', p. 108, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up index entry].</ref>

David was alive and parenting children at Mid Calder in 1606 and 1612, so the testament's four-child clause weighs against placing him as Andrew's direct son. The Mid Calder and Calder geography still supports a possible connection to the wider family. David may instead have been one generation lower—possibly a son of Andrew's record-proved sons James, Andrew or William—or a collateral relative. Their ages and David's estimated birth are not secure enough to choose one, and no better exact parent has been identified.

The Mid Calder death place is retained as an uncertain locality lead based on David's documented activity there; the baptism records do not establish his death place.

27483968.bio: {{Estimated Date}} [[Category: Ayrshire, Needs Profiles Created]] == Biography == {{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}} {{Notables Sticker}} === Early Life and Education === Rev. '''John Glasgow''' earned his '''M.A.''' from the University of Glasgow.University of Glasgow Story. [https://universitystory.gla.ac.uk/people/WH6172 Biography of John Glasgow] === Ministry === In 1688, he was appointed '''Minister of Kilbirnie''' in the '''Presbytery of Irvine'''. He held this post for over three decades, serving until his death in 1721. His tenure spanned the era following the Glorious Revolution, through the formal establishment of Presbyterianism as Scotland’s national church. Hew Scott's ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'' records that he graduated M.A. at Glasgow on 16 July 1674 and was ordained at Kilbirnie on 16 August 1688, in the year the Episcopalian incumbent was removed. The record supports describing him as a Presbyterian minister of the Revolution settlement; it does not identify him as a field preacher, prisoner, or active Covenanter.Hew Scott, ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'', new ed., vol. 3 (Edinburgh: Oliver and Boyd, 1920), [https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf p. 103]. === Marriage and Family === On 14 January '''1690''', Rev. John Glasgow married '''[[Cunningham-20924|Jean Cunningham (abt.1660–)]]''',Kilbirnie Parish, Church of Scotland, "Old Parish Registers Banns and Marriages," database, National Records of Scotland ([https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk ScotlandsPeople] : accessed 2 May 2025), marriage or banns for John Glasgow and Jeane Cunynghame 14 Jan 1690; citing Ref No: 10 / 9, parish 596. citing Ref 10 / 64, parish 596. === Legacy === Following John’s death, several of his children — '''Margaret''', '''Janet''', and '''Jean''', along with their mother '''Margaret Scott''' and brother '''James Glasgow''' — were involved in a successful decree of adjudication against '''Patrick, Viscount of Garnock'''. The case involved rights to property in the new barony of Kilbirnie. A key legal document was an extract renunciation dated 21 July 1731, registered on 14 February 1733.National Records of Scotland. [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/overview.aspx?st=1&tc=y&tl=n&tn=n&tp=n&k=James+Glasgow&ko=p&r=&ro=s&df=&dt=&di=y Decree of Adjudication – Glasgow family vs. Viscount of Garnock] == Research Notes == * In 1794, Robert Glasgow, Esq. of Puddockholm, grandson of Rev. John Glasgow, minister of Kilbirnie, acquired the estate of Mountgreenan, which had previously belonged to the Cuninghame family, and later expanded the estate by purchasing the lands of Fergushill around 1800.https://www.kilwinningheritage.org.uk/office/resources/documents/history-of-the-counties-of-ayr-and-wigton-vol-3-pt-2-paterson-1863.pdf *Marriages and children listed above included 3 wives and children. **1st 'wife' [[Allison-6866|Barbara Allison /Alason / Allason (abt.1659–)]] has no source and children were born in Kilwinning. That spouse has been unlinked since she was also linked to different [[Glasgow-3375|John Glasgow (abt.1650-)]], whom children were linked with. **2nd and 3rd 'wives' have marriage sources, children are all born in Kilbirnie, and both wives are listed in ''History of Ayr'', which states that he had fourteen children, which is the same number of children listed above for those two marriages. === Parentage and the 1722 family letter === No reviewed record names John's parents. The University of Glasgow register and ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'' establish his education, ministry and approximate age, but neither gives a father or birthplace. The currently linked parents, [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]], are therefore retained only as uncertain hypotheses, not proved parentage. A letter dated 22 November 1722 from [[Glasgow-1075|Robert Glasgow]] at Paddockholm to his brother [[Glasgow-1140|James Glasgow]], then a student of divinity at Glasgow, independently confirms the sibling relationship within John's documented child group.National Records of Scotland, RH15/120/178, letter from Robert Glasgow, Paddockholm, to his brother James Glasgow, student of divinity at Glasgow, 22 November 1722, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=RH15%2F120%2F178 catalogue description]. It does not identify John's own parents or connect this family to Robert Glaskow of Larne. === Current research === John should be placed in the wider [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] descendant project, most probably in the '''Corsankell-Stevenston-Kilwinning''' branch. Calling him the root of a separate Ayrshire family was too strong. The best current route is: William Glasgow (Glasgow-1098) ? James Glasgow elder (Glasgow-1168), Corsankell -> John Glasgow (Glasgow-3193), record-proved son ? Hugh Glasgow (Glasgow-1603), Ayrshire placeholder ? John Glasgow (Glasgow-1604), Kilwinning placeholder ? Rev. John Glasgow M.A. (Glasgow-1073) Only James-1168 to his named son John is directly proved within this displayed route. Glasgow-1603 and Glasgow-1604 have only tree-derived dates and parentage. Glasgow-1604 is nevertheless the best *existing-profile candidate* for John's father by generation and place. The structured parent links remain uncertain; no alternative father should be attached as certain without a direct record. [[Glasgow-3375|John Glasgow (Glasgow-3375), about 1650, Kilwinning]] is a serious duplicate candidate for the minister, not merely another son to add under Glasgow-1604. His John-and-Barbara household has indexed Kilwinning events in 1679 and January 1689, immediately before the minister's documented January 1690 marriage. The complete OPR pages must be checked for Mr`, occupation or residence before merging. This assessment draws on the cited records and public source material.[https://archive.org/details/munimentaalmeuni03mait full register].[https://archive.org/stream/munimentaalmeuni03mait/munimentaalmeuni03mait_djvu.txt searchable text].[https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf p. 103].[https://archive.org/details/historyofcountyo02pateuoft/page/252/mode/2up pp. 252-253].[https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F5%2F59 GD39/5/59]. == Sources == * 'The County Families of the Zetland Islands' by Francis Grant, 1893 ('Gauden of Swinister and Overland', p90+) * Visitation (Gloucestershire, 1623, 'Baynham')

Stevenson, 1847-1852), Vol. II, p. 252 - 253; Internet Archive, ([https://archive.org/details/historyofcountyo02pateuoft/page/252/mode/2up Available on Archive.org] : viewed 3 December 2025)
GLASGOW OF MOUNTGREENAM.I. REV. JOHN GLASGOW, minister of Kllbirnie from 1688 to 1721, when he died. He married, first, 14th January 1690, Jean, daughter of John Cunningham of Wattieston, Chamberlain to the Laird of Glengarnock, of the family of Robertland; secondly, Margaret, daughter of Robert Scott, merchant in Beith, 19th April 1699. He had fourteen children; but there is no tradition of any of them save his son.

27484695.bio:
== Biography ==

{{Estimated Date}}
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

'''James Glasgow'''—also recorded as '''James Glascho'''—was a householder, congregational officer and later Presbyterian ruling elder associated with '''Kilwaughter, County Antrim, Ireland'''. A James Glascho was recorded there in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll; James Glasgow appears in congregational affairs by 1700, and a later session list records James Glasgow deceased in '''1726'''. This profile provisionally brings those occurrences together, but continuity across the 57-year interval has not been proved and a same-name successor remains possible. A 1727 Connor diocesan probate index entry for James Glasgow of Kilwater is a strong follow-on match, although the original probate record is lost and supplies no relatives.

His parents, birthplace and exact date of birth are not known.

=== Robert Glasgow at Larne in 1653 ===

A 1653 deposition records a '''Robert Glaskow''' as living at '''Larne, County Antrim'''.<ref>1641 Depositions Project, examination mentioning Robert Glaskow "living in Larne," 1653, [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42821.html 1641 Depositions Project, item 42821].</ref>

In evidence concerning the death of Teige O'Sheale, a witness stated that he had heard that James Browne and Robert Glaskow, then living in Larne, had found O'Sheale. The account attributes the shooting to James Browne rather than directly to Robert.

This is an important early occurrence of the Glasgow surname in Larne before James's appearance in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll.

The record does not give Robert's age, birthplace, occupation, wife, children or relationship to James Glasgow.

Robert may have belonged to the same Larne and Kilwaughter Glasgow family, and he could theoretically have been James's father, uncle or another close relative. At present no surviving evidence establishes the relationship.

=== Kilwaughter householder in 1669 ===

The 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll records '''Jo. Glascho''' and '''James Glascho''' in Kilwaughter parish.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll, T/307/A; W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf transcription of the 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll], records 5347–5348, PDF p. 36.</ref>

Their consecutive entries, shared surname and shared parish strongly suggest a close association.

The record itself gives no relationship. John may have been James's brother, father, son or another relative.

Macafee's database standardises the locality as '''Kilwaughter Demesne''', but the transmitted townland field in the transcription is '''Unnamed'''. The safest description is therefore that James and John were recorded in '''Kilwaughter parish, in the section standardised by Macafee as the Demesne'''.

Macafee's online material is several stages removed from the destroyed original rolls. The surviving database derives from earlier copies of the original records and should therefore be treated as a transcription rather than an image of the original assessment.<ref>W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/17centurydatabases.htm Seventeenth-Century Census Substitutes], discussion of the provenance and transcription history of the surviving hearth-money material.</ref>

The published transcription should not by itself be cited for a statement that James was taxed for exactly one hearth unless the number of hearths has been checked directly against PRONI T/307/A.

The form ''Glascho'' is an historical or transmitted spelling of Glasgow. It should not be described as specifically Gaelic on the evidence of the hearth roll alone.

=== Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation ===

James became a prominent member of the Presbyterian congregation serving Larne and Kilwaughter, sometimes known as the Head of the Town congregation.

Surviving extracts from the congregational records show a cluster of adult Glasgow men involved in its affairs about 1700:<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 2 (1863), pp. 409–414, [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0002unse Internet Archive]; and 3 (1864), pp. 15–19, 196–198 and 379–380, [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''John Glasgow''' — associated with Kilwaughter in arrangements concerning ploughing and repairs.
* '''James Glasgow''' — appointed to oversee building work for the Kilwaughter households.
* '''Robert Glasgow''' — associated with the south side of the water in congregational arrangements.

This demonstrates that James was not an isolated Glasgow resident. Several adult men of the surname were established within the congregation at the same period.

No surviving congregational entry, however, explicitly describes John or Robert as James's brother, father or son.

The John active about 1700 may be the '''Jo. Glascho''' recorded immediately beside James in 1669, but that identification is not directly proved.

The Robert active about 1700 should not automatically be identified with the Robert living at Larne in 1653.

=== Congregational officer in 1700 ===

In 1700 James Glasgow was appointed an overseer for the Kilwaughter district.

He participated in arrangements for work performed for the minister and supervised the construction of office-houses on behalf of the Kilwaughter households.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

His position indicates that he was a trusted and established member of the local Presbyterian community.

The surviving elder roster associated with the early ministry of William Ogilvie does '''not''' include James Glasgow.

James should therefore not be described as a proved ruling elder in 1700.

His documented position at that date was a congregational or district overseer chosen to supervise practical affairs.

=== Later ruling elder ===

James later became a member of the '''session''' of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation.

A surviving cumulative session list covering the period beginning in 1721 includes '''James Glasgow''' among the members and carries the later annotation that he was '''deceased 1726'''.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive], extracts from the Larne and Kilwaughter session records.</ref>

Membership of a Presbyterian session establishes that James served as a '''ruling elder'''.

Because the surviving session list was cumulative and the earlier session book for part of the period is missing, the exact year in which James became an elder is not known.

The evidence supports the following sequence:

* '''1669''' — householder in Kilwaughter parish.
* '''1700''' — congregational overseer for Kilwaughter, but not included in the surviving early elder roster.
* '''Between 1701 and 1726''' — became a ruling elder.
* '''1721–1726''' — included in the surviving cumulative session list.
* '''1726''' — recorded as deceased.

It is therefore safest to describe him as a Presbyterian ruling elder '''later in life''', rather than assigning that office to him from 1700.

=== Presbytery commissioner in 1722 ===

In 1722 James Glasgow was one of six men attending Presbytery as commissioners from the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation.

The same entry names '''Brice Blair''' separately as the congregation's elder for that particular meeting.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

James's participation as commissioner demonstrates his continuing importance in congregational government, but this 1722 entry alone should not be used as the primary proof that he was a ruling elder.

His status as ruling elder is independently established by his inclusion in the session list.

=== Death ===

The session list annotates James Glasgow as:

:'''deceased 1726'''

This is the best surviving evidence for his year of death.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

His death should therefore be recorded as:

* '''1726'''.
* Exact date unknown.
* Place uncertain, probably in or near Kilwaughter, County Antrim.

There is no need to use "about 1726" if the session annotation itself explicitly gives the year.

=== Probate ===

The Connor diocesan wills index contains a 1727 probate entry for:

:'''James Glasgow, Kilwater'''

The combination of surname, locality and date makes this a very strong match for the James Glasgow recorded as deceased in 1726.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, pre-1858 wills index, "Glasgow, James, Kilwater," Diocese of Connor, 1727, [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search].</ref>

The original will or administration document does not appear to survive.

The index therefore cannot presently identify his widow, children, executor, beneficiaries, brothers, other relatives or property.

The most likely reconstruction is that James died in 1726 and probate proceedings followed in 1727.

=== Associated Glasgow men ===

Several Glasgow men can be associated with the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation during James's lifetime or soon afterwards.

==== John Glasgow ====

[[Glasgow-3913|'''John Glasgow''']] appears immediately before James in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll and was involved in Kilwaughter congregational arrangements about 1700.<ref>W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll], records 5347–5348; Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

He was probably a close relative of James.

Possible relationships include:

* Brother.
* Father.
* Son.
* Another close relative.

No surviving record specifies the relationship.

A brother or close collateral relationship is plausible, but should not be presented as proved.

==== Robert Glasgow ====

A '''Robert Glasgow''' was active within the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation about 1700 on the south side of the water.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

A later '''Robert Glasgow''' also appears among the members of the session. A 1747 congregational minute records his removal from the session after he refused the required public discipline following fornication.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

It is not yet proved that the Robert active in 1700 and the later ruling elder were the same man.

Neither is proved to have been James's son.

==== Hugh Glasgow ====

A later '''Hugh Glasgow''' appears as a member of the session and was recorded as deceased on '''8 July 1767'''.<ref>Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

His membership of the same congregation and surname make him a likely member of the wider Kilwaughter Glasgow family.

No surviving record proves him to have been James's son.

=== Possible children and later generations ===

No child of James Glasgow has yet been proved by a surviving primary or near-primary record.

Several later Glasgow men associated with Kilwaughter may have been descendants or close relatives:

* '''[[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]]''' (about 1705–1767).
* '''[[Glasgow-1504|James Glasgow]]''' (about 1707– ), possibly the man who married Sara Muray in 1727.
* '''[[Glasgow-1505|William Glasgow]]''' (about 1708–about 1783).
* '''[[Glasgow-1143|Robert Glasgow]]''' (about 1710–about 1772).

Their presence demonstrates continuity of the Glasgow surname in the Kilwaughter area but does not establish parentage.

Any children attached to James should remain marked '''uncertain''' unless supported by additional evidence.

In particular, '''[[Glasgow-1469|James Glasgow]]''', reportedly born in 1736, cannot be a biological son of this James if the elder James was deceased in 1726. Either the relationship or one of the dates must be incorrect.
=== Possible son: James Glasgow of Randalstown and Duneane ===

'''[[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]]''', the ruling elder associated with Randalstown or Drummaul in 1698 and 1703 and probably Duneane in 1705, has been attached as an '''uncertain son''' of James Glasgow of Kilwaughter.

The relationship is not stated in any surviving record. It is nevertheless chronologically and geographically plausible. James of Kilwaughter was already an independent householder in 1669, while the younger James first appears as a ruling elder in 1698. A son born during the 1660s or 1670s would fit that chronology comfortably.

The 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll also makes a family connection worth considering. Macafee's transcription records only three householders standardised under the surname Glasgow: Elizabeth ''Glascho'' at Glenarm and James and Jo. ''Glascho'' at Kilwaughter. No householder standardised as Glasgow appears in Drummaul or Duneane.<ref>W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf transcription of the 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll], entries for Elizabeth, James and Jo. Glascho.</ref>

The later appearance of a James Glasgow as a Presbyterian ruling elder in western County Antrim could therefore represent a younger member of the established Kilwaughter-area Glasgow family who had moved west.

James of Kilwaughter is presently treated as the possible father because the chronology works and the repeated given name is consistent with a father-son relationship. However, '''[[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]]''', recorded beside James at Kilwaughter in 1669, or another member of the same family could also have been the younger James's father.

The parent-child relationship should therefore remain marked '''uncertain''' unless estate, congregational, probate or other evidence explicitly establishes it.

=== Identity assessment ===

The following records form a possible Kilwaughter sequence; they do not yet prove one continuous individual:

:'''1669''' — James Glascho, Kilwaughter householder.
:'''1700''' — James Glasgow, Kilwaughter congregational overseer.
:'''By 1721–1726''' — James Glasgow, member of the Larne and Kilwaughter session and therefore a ruling elder.
:'''1722''' — James Glasgow, commissioner to Presbytery.
:'''1726''' — James Glasgow recorded deceased.
:'''1727''' — James Glasgow of Kilwater, probate indexed in the Diocese of Connor.

No single surviving document explicitly states that all these records concern the same man.

Name, place and congregation support a working continuity hypothesis. However, an adult householder in 1669 surviving to 1726 would have been at least about 78. That is possible, but a same-name successor needs explicit testing in leases, rent rolls and church originals. The 1726 death and 1727 probate alignment is stronger than the unbridged 1669-to-1700 identity link.

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible Scottish identity ===

The Scottish child now represented separately by [[Glasgow-3971|James Glasgow]] was recorded in a Glasgow parish index in November 1645 as a child of '''[[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]]'''.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," FamilySearch database, James Glasgow, November 1645, parents Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunningham, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK FamilySearch record VQHK-VMK]; derived from the Glasgow Old Parish Register.</ref>

Derivative references give both '''11 November''' and '''25 November 1645'''. The original register page has not yet been examined, so it is unclear whether these represent birth, baptism, registration or an indexing difference.

Until the original page is reviewed, the safest statement concerning this Scottish child is only '''November 1645'''.

The chronology is compatible with the Kilwaughter man. If born in November 1645, he would have been about twenty-three or twenty-four when recorded as an independent householder in 1669, about fifty-five in 1700, and about eighty at his death in 1726.

Chronological compatibility is not evidence of identity.

No known record states that James of Kilwaughter:

* Was born in Glasgow.
* Was a son of Robert Glasgow.
* Was a son of Jonet Cunningham.
* Migrated from Scotland to Ireland.
* Was related to the Robert Glaskow recorded at Larne in 1653.

The proposed identification of [[Glasgow-3971|the Scottish James]] with this Kilwaughter man remains an open, low-to-moderate hypothesis. The profiles should remain separate and must not be merged without a record bridging origin, kinship or migration.

=== Parentage assessment ===

The parents of James Glasgow of Kilwaughter are presently '''unknown'''.

'''[[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]]''' should not presently be described as his probable or established parents.

They were the parents of a James Glasgow recorded in Glasgow in November 1645.<ref>"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," FamilySearch database, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK James Glasgow, November 1645], parents Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunningham.</ref>

What remains unproved is whether that child was James of Kilwaughter.

There is also a separate unproved proposition that the Scottish father Robert Glasgow was identical with the Robert Glaskow living at Larne in 1653.

The proposed pedigree therefore requires both of the following identifications to be correct:

* The Scottish James recorded in 1645 was James of Kilwaughter.
* The Scottish Robert Glasgow was Robert Glaskow of Larne in 1653.

Neither has yet been demonstrated by a record naming origins, kinship or migration.

The Scottish couple may remain in Research Notes as candidate parents, but attaching them as parents on the profile risks turning a plausible hypothesis into copied genealogical fact.

=== Current Irish reconstruction ===

The strongest current reconstruction is:

:'''Robert Glaskow''' — living at Larne in 1653; relationship to the later Kilwaughter Glasgows unknown.
:'''John Glasgow''' — Kilwaughter in 1669 and probably the John active there about 1700.
:'''James Glasgow''' — Kilwaughter in 1669; overseer in 1700; later ruling elder; died 1726.
:'''Robert Glasgow''' — active in the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation about 1700; relationship unknown.

These records establish a local Glasgow surname cluster and probable kinship network. They do '''not''' establish parent-child relationships.

=== Scottish hypothesis ===

The separate working hypothesis is:

:'''[[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]]''' married '''[[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]]'''.
:* Their son '''James Glasgow''' was recorded at Glasgow in November 1645.
:* That James may subsequently have migrated to County Antrim.
:* He may have been the James Glasgow recorded at Kilwaughter from 1669.

This remains unproved.

=== Evidence against merging with the western elder ===

The General Synod records give the following sequence:<ref>Presbyterian Church in Ireland, ''Records of the General Synod of Ulster, from 1691 to 1820'', vol. 1 (Belfast, 1890), [https://archive.org/details/recordsofgeneral01pres Internet Archive].</ref>

* '''1698''' — William Taylor / James Glasgow.
* '''1703''' — William Taylor / James Glasgow.
* '''1703''' — William Ogilvie / James Caldwell.
* '''1705''' — James Scott / James Glasgow.
* '''1705''' — William Taylor / Robert King.

William Taylor was minister of Randalstown or Drummaul.

William Ogilvie was minister of Larne and Kilwaughter.

James Scott was minister of Duneane.

The placement of James Glasgow beside Taylor in 1698 and 1703, followed by Scott in 1705, strongly favours a western-Antrim identity separate from James of Kilwaughter.

=== Not to be confused with ===

James of Kilwaughter should not presently be merged with:

* The '''James Glasgow''' who served as ruling elder for Randalstown in 1698 and 1703 and probably Duneane in 1705.
* [[Glasgow-1376|James Glasgow (bef.1657-)]], the Covenanter.
* [[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow (1640-)]].
* Other contemporary Scottish men of the name.

=== Date and place guidance ===

Recommended profile data:

* '''Birth:''' uncertain; exact date unknown.
* '''Birthplace:''' unknown.
* '''Parents:''' unknown.
* '''Residence:''' Kilwaughter parish, County Antrim, by 1669.
* '''Religion:''' Presbyterian.
* '''Occupation/status:''' householder; congregational overseer; later ruling elder.
* '''Death:''' 1726, exact date unknown.
* '''Death place:''' uncertain, probably County Antrim.
* '''Probate:''' Diocese of Connor, 1727.

If the profile requires a birth estimate, a conservative form would be:

:'''Birth before 1649, place unknown'''

This is based only on his appearance as an independent householder in 1669.

Alternatively, '''November 1645, uncertain''' could be retained only if the profile is explicitly using the proposed Scottish identity as an uncertain working hypothesis.

=== Record-loss caution ===

The surviving evidence is affected by substantial record loss.

The original Irish hearth-money rolls were destroyed in the 1922 Public Record Office fire. The surviving County Antrim material derives through earlier copies rather than the original rolls.<ref>W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/17centurydatabases.htm Seventeenth-Century Census Substitutes].</ref>

Many pre-1858 Irish wills were also destroyed.

Absence of explicit family relationships in the surviving sources therefore does not imply that such records never existed.

=== Research priorities ===

'''Kilwaughter estate papers and rentals'''

* PRONI D282.
* NRS GD154/505–534.
* Search leases, renewals, rentals and named lives involving James, John and Robert Glasgow.
* A lease identifying "James, son of Robert Glasgow" or equivalent wording would be decisive.

'''Original Larne and Kilwaughter session books'''

* PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B and associated volumes.
* Inspect the cumulative elder list and the original annotation beside James.
* Search every surviving entry from 1721 through 1727 for his admission as elder, illness, death, burial costs, mortcloth payments, widow, executor or relatives.
* Porter's articles are extracts rather than a diplomatic transcription and may omit genealogically useful details.

'''1666 County Antrim subsidy roll'''

* PRONI T/808/14889.
* Search separately for Glasgow, Glascho, Glaskow, Glass and similar forms.
* This may establish James, John or Robert in Kilwaughter before 1669.

'''1727 probate substitutes'''

* Betham abstracts.
* Crosslé manuscripts.
* Groves collection.
* Thrift abstracts.
* Surviving Connor diocesan administration material.
* Search for an executor, widow, legatees or property description.

'''Registry of Deeds'''

* Search from 1709 onward for Glasgow grantors, lessees, witnesses and memorials involving Kilwaughter or the Agnew estate.
* Particular attention should be given to deeds after James's death where a widow, son, heir or executor renewed or assigned a lease.

'''Original Glasgow Old Parish Register page'''

* Examine the original page containing the November 1645 entry.
* Determine whether 11 and 25 November represent birth and baptism.
* Record any residence, occupation or witnesses supplied.
* Search surrounding entries and siblings of the Scottish James for names later appearing in County Antrim.
* National Records of Scotland guidance: [https://www.nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/research-guides/old-parish-registers/ Old Parish Registers research guide].

'''Glasgow burgess records'''

* Examine the complete 1655 absent-burgess material, Glasgow City Archives C1/1/13.
* Evidence explicitly placing Robert Glasgow in Ireland, Larne or Carrickfergus would materially strengthen the Scottish hypothesis.
* A bare statement that he was absent would not establish migration to County Antrim.

=== Belfast namesake and possible collateral ===
[[Glasgow-3172|Captain James Glasgow of Belfast]] may have been a younger relative of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glaskow of Larne]] and a collateral of this Kilwaughter household. Belfast, Larne and Kilwaughter form a plausible north-east Antrim corridor, but no record states the relationship.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, maritime material for Captain James Glasgow or Glascow; T/828/15, will extract for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref>

The two profiles remain separate because their identity has not been established. The Belfast testamentary reference carries the year 1686, but that has not been verified as a death or probate date; a will date alone cannot exclude survival into the 1720s. Read the full Belfast extract before treating chronology as decisive evidence against identity.

=== Precise early estate targets ===

National Records of Scotland's Agnew catalogue identifies Kilwaghter tenant goods and livestock and a rental, c.1653 (GD154/514-515); rentals, c.1690 (GD154/525, two items); rent rolls and accounts, November 1692 (GD154/530, three items); and rent rolls and accounts, 1693-1708 (GD154/532, eight items). The inspected item descriptions state Open / On site. These are concrete targets for testing the 1669-to-1700 continuity and possible family succession, but their tenant names and original contents have not yet been read; the catalogue itself establishes no Glasgow occurrence or relationship.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Agnew family of Lochnaw papers, GD154/514, 515, 525, 530 and 532; item descriptions inspected 21 September 2026. [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD154%2F532&st=1&tc=y&tl=n&tn=n&tp=n GD154/532 catalogue entry].</ref>

== Biography ==
Jhone was born in 1608. He is the son of [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow (bef.1590-)]].<ref>"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-X8B : 12 February 2020), Jhone Glasgow in entry for Jhone Glasgow, 1608.</ref> 

Probably a nephew of [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow (abt.1575-)]]

 
	

'''John Glasgow''' lived in Lanarkshire, Scotland, during the seventeenth century.

His estate appears to have been recorded by the Commissary Court of Lanark, but the original testament still needs to be re-read before his residence, family relationships and exact death date can be stated confidently.

The published Lanark testament index includes separate entries for men named John Glasgow dated:

* 27 May 1650;
* 13 January 1662;
* 25 March 1685.

The 1650 entry belongs to [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow of Quothquan]]. This profile is more likely connected with either the 1662 or 1685 estate.

Further details should be added once the original records CC14/5/6 and CC14/5/12 have been transcribed.

== Research Notes ==
=== Record identification ===

The previous biography on this profile described the 1650 testament of [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow of Quothquan]], including his daughters Issobell and Jonet and the estate recorded in CC14/5/5.

Those details have been removed because they belong to the separate 1650 profile.

This profile appears to concern either:

* the John Glasgow whose estate was recorded on 13 January 1662, probably in CC14/5/6; or
* the John Glasgow whose estate was recorded on 25 March 1685, probably in CC14/5/12.

The original documents must be checked before choosing between them.

=== Attached family ===

The attached child [[Glasgow-3331|John Glasgow]] has elsewhere been associated with the 1662 estate as an executor.

That relationship should be retained only after the original wording of CC14/5/6 has been verified.

=== Death date ===

The profile has used a death year of 1685, but that date has not yet been matched securely to this individual.

Until CC14/5/12 is transcribed, the death date should remain uncertain.

=== Further research ===

* Transcribe CC14/5/6.
* Transcribe CC14/5/12.
* Identify each man’s residence and occupation.
* Identify executors, spouse, children and other relatives.
* Match the correct testament to this profile.
* Reassess the attached family once the original wording is available.

=== Supplied parish index comparison ===

The supplied Scotland’s People index records '''JHONE GLASGOW''' on '''26/06/1608''' at Mid Calder, with parent text “JHONE GLASGOW/”.<ref name="OPRBirth095">Scotland’s People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms], exact surname Glasgow through 1700, index text supplied 10 September 2026: JHONE GLASGOW, 26/06/1608, JHONE GLASGOW/, indexed gender U, Mid Calder, parish 694, reference 10 / 12. Original register image not inspected for this review.</ref>

This supplies a more precise index date than the profile’s existing birth year of 1608. The combined births and baptisms collection does not establish whether 26 June is a birthday or a baptism date. It does not connect this child to either of the later testament identities discussed above. A parent’s name alone does not uniquely identify an attached historical person, and the index does not establish an unnamed parent.

27485238.Name: Glasgow-1095
27485238.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}  
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

This page is listed with an approximate date of 1500, but it primarily serves as a placeholder for [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:John_Glasgow-1 John Glasgow (1475–1536)], who was likely born around 1450. Various records mention a John Glasgow at different times between 1475 and 1575. These entries most likely refer to at least two or three generations of John Glasgows. Given the time span and naming patterns, there could be more individuals, but it is clear that the same John could not have appeared in all these records.

This marks one of the earliest known appearances of the Glasgow surname outside of the "de Glasgu" lineage, which is documented between 1259 and 1419. A significant portion of the "de Glasgu" individuals are named John, which complicates efforts to distinguish their individual timelines. Based on common medieval generational spans—typically 25 to 30 years—there would have been roughly 11 to 12 generations between 1259 and 1575. Considering the prominence of the name "John" as a firstborn male in this period, it is likely that at least 6 distinct individuals named John Glasgow appeared in records during this time, though there could have been more.

Although no direct relationship has been definitively proven, it is highly probable that the three individuals named Glasgow, who are mentioned in the '''Protocol Books of the Town Clerks of Glasgow''', are related to the John mentioned in 1475, given the patterns of naming and the family’s prominence in local records:

* '''[[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow (b. abt. 1510)]]''' – Active between 1536 and 1575.
* '''[[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow (b. abt. 1510)]]''' – Active between 1526 and 1536.
* '''[[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow (b. abt. 1520)]]''' – Active between 1554 and 1568.

Considering the relatively small population of Glasgow in the early 1500s—estimated at between 2,500 and 3,000<ref>Lynch, Michael (2001). *Title of the Book/Article*, p. 267.</ref>—the probability of these individuals being closely related is high. The surname "Glasgow" was less common at the time, and the repeated appearance of multiple members of the Glasgow family in the same documents further suggests a shared familial connection. It was common in smaller communities for surnames to reflect familial ties, especially when the population was limited and families played prominent roles in local affairs.

The Glasgow family’s frequent mention in these historical documents points to their significance in the area during the period, and it’s possible that additional archival research could uncover further details about their relationships and activities during the 15th and 16th centuries.

== Sources ==

27485245.Name: Glasgow-1096
27485245.DeathLocation: High Street, Merchant City, Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland
27485245.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was born circa '''1520'''. He was a resident and citizen of Glasgow during the mid-16th century, active in civic life between at least 1551 and 1575. He appears in the civic records, particularly ''The Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', primarily as a witness and later as a property owner, identified by his occupation as a fisher. === Early Civic Appearances === On 21 May 1551 Robert witnessed the sale of a Glasgow tenement to [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]] and Isobell Newlands.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 1, protocol 84, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n59/mode/2up 21 May 1551, printed p. 31]. The record places Robert with Archibald but does not state their relationship. On 10 May 1554 Robert and David Mathy were named together among the ''comburgesses'' of Glasgow while witnessing the same sasines.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 1, protocols 183-184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63]. This is a direct personal association between the Glasgow and Mathie families. Protocol 266 again expressly described him as a burgess when he witnessed a property transaction on 17 February 1555/56.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocol 266, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n18/mode/2up 17 February 1555/56, printed pp. 2-3]. Robert continued to appear in the South Port and Clyde-bridge property district. He witnessed William Hall's sasine and immediate resale on 26 July 1557.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 372-373, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n51/mode/2up 26 July 1557, printed p. 35]. In November 1557, protocols 401 and 403 described a tenement bounded by Robert Glesgw's lands on the south and John Glesgw's lands on the west.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 401 and 403, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n57/mode/2up 8 and 26 November 1557, printed pp. 41-42]. Robert witnessed a further transaction in the same district on 20 February 1559/60, and three sasines of 18 April 1560 used his lands as a boundary; one of them also named John's lands on the west.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 525-526, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n93/mode/2up 20 February 1559/60, printed p. 76].Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 2, protocols 544-546, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc08scogoog/page/n98/mode/2up 18 April 1560, printed pp. 80-81]. These adjoining holdings establish a close property association with John, but the records state no kinship. === Marriage and Property Ownership === Robert married '''[[Rolland-239|Margaret Rowand]]''' (born c. 1535), likely around '''1551'''. By 1572, they were established citizens involved in property transactions. Protocols 1903 and 1904 call Robert and Margaret spouses when they sold property on '''12 February 1572/3'''.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 6, protocols 1903-1904, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01renwgoog/page/n121/mode/2up 12 February 1572/73]. The record details the transaction:
''Robert Glasgow, citizen of Glasgow, and Margaret Rowand, spouses, sold to James Rowand a tenement [...] This property, fore and back, with its pertinents, was situated on the west side of the street leading from the market cross to the South Port. It was bordered by the lands of the late Andrew Dunlop to the north, the lands of [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] to the west, the chaplainry lands of St. Roche to the south, and the street on the east. Sasine was given by Archibald Lyone, bailie, and ratified by Margaret Rowand in the absence of her husband.'' — ''12 February 1572–3, 8 a.m.''
This entry confirms Robert's marriage, his status as a property-holding citizen, and the specific location of his tenement near the market cross and South Port. It also places [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] (presumably the same fisher mentioned earlier) as the owner of the adjacent property to the west. Protocol 2125 again expressly calls Robert and Margaret Rowand spouses in a property reversion on '''7 February 1574/75'''.Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2125, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n102/mode/2up 7 February 1574/75], printed p. 86. This proves Robert was alive on that date. === Family === On '''23 October 1596''', Ninian Glasgow was admitted as a burgess as the “second son to Robert G., fisher, burgess.”James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'' (1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], 23 October 1596. This directly proves that [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] was Robert's second son and describes Robert as a fisher and burgess. Ninian's 1613 testament independently names “Johne glasgw his brother,” proving that Robert had another son named John who was alive on 10 January 1613.National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142-145, testament testamentar and inventory of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613 and confirmed 8 May 1613. That John's identity remains unresolved. [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] is attached as an uncertain candidate; he must not be conflated with [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow of Hirmanscheillis]], who died in 1576. The records do not prove that Margaret Rowand was the mother of either son. === Death === Robert's date of death is currently unknown, but he was alive on 7 February 1574/75. The 1580 Kilbride charter is a probable later appearance; if the cross-record identification is correct, he was alive on 9 February 1580. The exact date of death remains unknown. === Burgh account, 1573-1574 === The Glasgow burgh accounts for 1573-1574 record eight shillings described as outstanding and not in use of payment from "Robert Glasgow tenement."''Extracts from the Records of the Burgh of Glasgow'', accounts for 1573-1574, printed p. 453. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QHV-V3DN-P9VH-Q FamilySearch image]. This property occurrence falls between Robert and Margaret Rowand's documented tenement transaction of February 1572/73 and their property reversion of February 1574/75. The date, city and property context strongly support attribution to this Robert, although the account itself gives no occupation, spouse or relative. == Research Notes == === Probable parentage === [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] is the leading and '''probable''' father of Robert, but the relationship remains marked uncertain because no record explicitly calls Robert his son. The assessment rests on several details operating together: * William's documented son [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] and Robert repeatedly held land around the same compact South Port and Clyde-bridge property group in 1557-73. * In 1572/73 Robert and Margaret Rowand dealt with a tenement adjoining John's land, and a John Glasgow, fisher, witnessed the transaction. * Robert and John were described together as fishers in 1573.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up 19 December 1573], printed p. 36. * Robert had witnessed [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]]'s 1551 purchase of a parcel whose exact east-of-Bargill boundary was in John's hands by 1554/55.Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 1, protocol 205, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n97/mode/2up 31 January 1554/55], printed p. 69. This is stronger than a shared surname or neighbourhood alone: it combines property, occupation and a repeated three-man association. John's service as William's sole heir is consistent with male primogeniture and does not exclude younger sons who established neighbouring holdings. The principal alternative is that the later fisher John was Robert's own son rather than William's son; both generations of John were alive during part of this period. Cousinship also remains possible. Those alternatives prevent a confident relationship status. [[Brade-232|Esbell Brade]] is William's documented wife and mother of John, but no record identifies her as Robert's mother. Her attachment therefore remains uncertain. An uncited MyHeritage tree reportedly gave Robert a birth about 1502 and named William and Esbell as parents; it is a research lead only and does not override the contemporary chronology. === Family and other claims === [[Rolland-239|Margaret Rowand]] is Robert's documented spouse, although the records do not establish a marriage about 1551 or identify her parents. Her relationship to James Rowand, who acquired the couple's property, remains worth investigating. [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]] is a documented son; the record-defined son John was alive in 1613, but his identity with [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] remains uncertain. Robert's relationship to Archibald is probably close, but the witness record does not explicitly call them brothers. Earlier descendant compilations proposed wider connections through Herbison, Stewart, Howie, Cunningham, Edmonstone, Hamilton, Ivey, Johnson, Gammon and Dauge families. Those lines require their own documentary chains and cannot establish Robert's parentage. A reported "Bigger 1625" reference has not been identified and remains unusable pending a full citation. Robert's occupation as a fisher is independently supported by protocol 2002. The exact roles of Archibald Lyone, Robert Steward, Robert Herbertsone, John Woddrop, Archibald Herbertsone, Andrew Huchesone, Duncan Lennox, John Wilsone, Hugh Blair, John Maxwell of Bogtoun, Andrew Farie and Andrew Dunlop remain associate-network questions rather than kinship evidence. === Mathie–Glencairn connection === David Mathy had a documented son John in 1571. That son may be the John Mathie who appeared as a writer in 1574 and was admitted with the Earl of Glencairn’s burgess group in 1583.Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 6, protocol 1798, 25 October 1571, printed p. 70, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog digitised volume]; vol. 4, protocol 1036, 4 August 1574, printed p. 19, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07scogoog digitised volume]; James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750, [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83]. Tutory retours entered in 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother Matthew as a Glasgow burgess and name four of John’s lawful children.Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3]. The family therefore remained connected with both Glasgow burgh society and the Glencairn estate network. If [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] was Robert’s son, his 1618 marriage to [[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]] may have continued the relationship first documented between Robert and David Mathy in 1554. === Kilbride land, 1580 === On 9 February 1580 a charter of the church lands of the vicarage of Kilbride in Cunninghame, Ayrshire, named “Robertum Glasgw” among the occupiers, together with Robert Andro, Robert Boyd, Thomas Young, Robert Dunlop, Jonet Hunter, Robert Andro younger, John Wilson and John Young. The charter was confirmed under the Great Seal on 15 February 1581/82.John Maitland Thomson, ed., ''Registrum Magni Sigilli Regum Scotorum'', vol. 5, A.D. 1580–1593 (Edinburgh, 1888), no. 324, [https://archive.org/details/registrummagnisi05scot/page/104/mode/2up pp. 104–105], charter dated at Glasgow 9 February 1580 and confirmed 15 February 1581/82. The former [[Glasgow-1096]] held this Kilbride occurrence. It has been combined with this profile as the leading identity: the rare name, five-year interval after Robert and Margaret Rowand's 1575 city property act,Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2125, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n102/mode/2up printed p. 86], 7 February 1574/75. and documented Mathie–Glencairn connection support one man's move or land interest in Cunninghame. Dunlop, Wilson and Young are also surnames found in the wider associated network, but shared surnames alone do not prove kinship. The charter does not call the Kilbride occupier a fisher, burgess, husband of Margaret Rowand or former Glasgow resident, so the identification remains probable rather than directly proved. The separate profile estimated birth about 1560 solely from adult occupancy in 1580; no birth record supported that year. It is compatible with the older profile's circa 1520 estimate because both are approximate adult-status inferences. If this identification is correct, Robert lived after 9 February 1580. Seek a later deed naming both his Kilbride holding and wife, occupation or Glasgow tenement to confirm the bridge. == Sources ==

Spouses.Name: Rolland-239
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==

Margaret Rolland, also recorded as '''Rowand''', was the wife of [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]], a fisher and Glasgow burgess.

On 12 February 1572/73, James Rolland resigned a tenement to Robert Glasgow and Margaret Rolland, expressly described as spouses. The following instrument again named the couple and recorded Margaret's separate ratification.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 6, protocols 1903–1904, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc01renwgoog/page/n121/mode/2up 12 February 1572/73].</ref>

On 7 February 1574/75, Robert Glasgow and Margaret '''Rowand''', spouses, dealt with reversions concerning their South Port tenement.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 7, protocol 2125, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n102/mode/2up 7 February 1574/75].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

These instruments directly prove Margaret's marriage to Robert and her Glasgow property dealings. They do not give her birth date, parents or marriage date. The structured birth about 1535 is retained only as an uncertain estimate, and the reported 1551 marriage is unproved.

James Rolland's role in the 1573 property transaction does not establish that he was Margaret's father or brother. No such relationship should be inferred without another record.
