44280491.Name: Glasgow-3163
44280491.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date|Birth}} == Biography == '''Andrew Glasgow''' (written ''Andro Glasgw'') lived at a place read uncertainly as “Corsoun,” in the parish read as “Calder Clair” or “Calder Cleir,” within the sheriffdom of Edinburgh. His testament testamentar and inventory was made on 6 February 1597 as written (1597/8). The record says that he died the next day, 7 February, and was confirmed on 10 July 1598.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; working transcription of the original register images. See also Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. This was a ''testament testamentar'': Andrew made the will himself on the day before his death. The introductory account, inventory and debts begin on image 123; the family provisions continue on image 124. A different testament begins towards the foot of image 124 and is not part of Andrew's entry. === Family and executors === Andrew's wife was '''Elizat Stevinsoun''' (Elizabeth Stevenson). The testament expressly calls '''Robert Glasgow''' their son:
“Robart Glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff”
It also names Andrew's daughters '''Marion, Janet and Isobel'''. The dispositive clause refers to “his said sone and his said [dochter… struck through] Marione, Jonet, Isobell.” {| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;" |+ '''Household named in Andrew Glasgow's testament''' |- ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Person ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Relationship ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | What the record proves |- | Elizat Stevinsoun || Wife || Appointed with Robert to administer the movable estate; explicitly called Andrew's spouse and wife. |- | Robert Glasgow || Son || Explicitly Andrew's son by Elizat; he had not yet reached the age fixed for taking the land. |- | Marion Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the operative inheritance clause as one of Andrew's daughters. |- | Janet Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the same inheritance clause. |- | Isobel Glasgow || Daughter || Named in the same inheritance clause. |- | Unnamed possible child || Conditional only || Provided for only if Elizat was pregnant; the will does not prove a later birth. |} Andrew appointed Elizat and Robert to take charge of his goods, movable property and debts receivable, and to pay his debts. He also named advisers whose counsel they were to use. One readable adviser was '''James Stevisoun'''. The shared surname makes him a useful lead for Elizat's family, but the will does not call him her father, brother or other relative. === Estate and financial network === The inventory describes a working rural household. It appears to include three cows with calves, although the number is uncertain; two yearling cattle; two horses valued at £10 each, £20 altogether; nine sheep; eight bolls of oats in the barn and barnyard; four firlots of barley; household utensils and furnishings; and Andrew's clothing. Several quantities, individual valuations and the inventory total remain unresolved and should not be supplied from the usual form of other testaments. The debts owed to Andrew include entries for '''John Mure''', an incompletely identified widow of a deceased John, and '''James Stevisoun'''; some residences and all of the relevant sums remain uncertain. The debts Andrew owed include a payment associated with a brown horse, and less secure readings involving Bartholomew Wilson, James Lyon and John Brown, David Lyon, James Stevisoun and a laird whose designation may be Westhall. These are economic associates, not proved relatives. The account then calculated the free estate, its division into thirds and Andrew's own third, but the figures have not been securely read. === Distribution and land === Andrew directed that, once his debts had been paid, one third of the free estate should go to Elizat and another third to Robert. His own third was to go to a child if Elizat was pregnant by him. If she was not pregnant, that third was to be divided equally among Robert, Marion, Janet and Isobel. Andrew provided that Elizat was to “bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige”: she was to possess or enjoy the land until Robert reached legal age. The unclear word before ''land'' is not supplied here. This is direct evidence of intended succession within Andrew's household, but the record does not say from whom Andrew obtained the land or whether his interest was heritable or tenanted. The will also allowed for the possibility that Elizat was pregnant: “incais his said spous be with bairne to him.” That conditional wording does not establish that another child was born. Andrew further directed that, if “Elizat his spous do not hir pairt to his said bairnis,” she was to be removed from the administration, protecting the children's interests. The closing clause records execution by a notary at Andrew's direction because he could not write. The subsequent confirmation again names Elizat Stevinsoun and Robert Glasgow. A further man, Johne Sandelandis, appears in the confirmation, but the surviving reading does not establish a relationship to the family. == Research Notes == === Calendar and locality === The manuscript year is 1597 in the Scottish record, while the confirmation was in July 1598. Andrew's death should therefore be recorded as 7 February 1597/8, not 10 July 1598. The readings “Corsoun” and “Calder Clair/Cleir” remain qualified until the handwriting is independently resolved. The place has been rendered both Corsoun and Corstoun in derivative work. It has not been safely equated with a modern settlement. The profile's structured death place should reflect only the documented household locality, marked uncertain, rather than the unsupported Kirknewton value. === Corrected family reading === An earlier transcription identified a Jonet Anderson as Andrew's wife and Marion, James, Andrew and William as four children. Re-reading images 123–124 does not support that reconstruction. The secure relationships are Elizat Stevinsoun as wife; Robert as Andrew and Elizat's son; and Marion, Janet and Isobel as Andrew's daughters. Profiles [[Glasgow-4006]] and [[Glasgow-4007]] represent supposed sons Andrew and William from that reading; neither man is named as Andrew's child in the corrected testament. Their profiles should preserve the history of the mistake without treating it as evidence that either person existed. The current spouse should not be detached merely to leave an empty field before an evidenced Elizabeth profile is available, but the relationship is contradicted and must not be presented as proved. Robert, Marion, Janet and Isobel each require a new documentary profile. [[Glasgow-1156]], [[Glasgow-3062]], [[Glasgow-3917]], [[Glasgow-3183]] and [[Glasgow-3336]] were compared but do not have a direct Corsoun, Stevenson, sibling, property or succession bridge. They must not be substituted merely from name, chronology or regional compatibility. The currently attached [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1028|David Glasgow]] are not named as sons in this testament. They should remain uncertain unless another record independently connects them to Andrew. The attached spouse is now the record-defined Elizat Stevinsoun (Elizabeth Stevenson). The earlier Jonet Anderson identification is retired. The earlier model reading of the 1577 testament's second child as ''Androw'' has been superseded by the accepted Marjory (''m[ar]iory'') reading, so no comparison with this Andrew profile arises from that record. The 1577 household is associated with the place provisionally indexed as Hirmenschelis, while this testament places Andrew at Corsoun; no record bridges the two households, and this profile is not the present match for any child of [[Glasgow-3181|John Glasgow]]. === Parentage and next evidence === No parent is named. [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] remains an uncertain working father only; Andrew's evidence is in the rural Calder setting, whereas John's proved family is concentrated in Glasgow burgh records. The highest-value next search is the National Records of Scotland's Morton estate material: GD150/696–757 (Barony of Caldercleir), GD150/2027–2060 (Midlothian rentals), and GD150/320–493. An occupier succession naming Robert after Andrew could identify The proved son and clarify the nature of the landholding.National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD150 GD150, Papers of the Earls of Morton], especially GD150/696–757, GD150/2027–2060 and GD150/320–493. == Sources ==

Spouses.Name: Stevinsoun-2
Spouses.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date|Birth}} == Biography == '''Elizat Stevinsoun''' was the wife of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]]. Andrew's testament expressly calls [[Glasgow-4006|Robert Glasgow]] his son by Elizat:
“Robart Glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff”
Andrew directed that Elizat should “bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige,” giving her possession or enjoyment of the land until Robert came of age. He also made a conditional provision “incais his said spous be with bairne to him” and provided that if “Elizat his spous do not hir pairt to his said bairnis,” she was to be removed from administration.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. == Research Notes == === Birth chronology === The earlier circa-1540 birth and current circa-1560 birth are generational estimates; no reviewed record states Elizat's age. Circa 1560 better fits the age range of her directly documented son Robert, who had not yet come of age when Andrew made his testament on 6 February 1597/8. Robert's precise birth year is also unknown, and the testament's possible-pregnancy clause does not prove a later birth. === Identity === The manuscript form is '''Stevinsoun'''; Stephenson or Stevenson is the modern spelling, retained as another-surname form. [[Stevinsoune-1|Bessie Stevinsoune]] remains a compatible possible remarried identity: the Dunfermline register names her husband George Lugtoun on 25 February 1606 and their children in 1607 and 1609, but gives no prior marital status, parents or residence, so no record bridges her to Corsoun, Andrew, Robert or the land Elizat held. [[Stevenson-7398]] is excluded as Robert Blaikstone's Yorkshire wife. The testament names Andrew's daughters Marion, Janet and Isobel, but does not expressly call them Elizat's children; their maternity is not proved by this clause alone. == Sources ==

44299537.Name: Glasgow-3171

44299635.Name: Glasgow-3172
44299635.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow'''—also recorded as '''James Glasco'''—was a mariner and shipmaster associated with Belfast, County Antrim, during the later seventeenth century. His origins, parentage, date of birth, wife, and children have not been identified.

The available evidence places James in Belfast’s maritime community from at least 1667 until 1679. Although an estimated birth around 1600 has sometimes been assigned to him, no contemporary record supporting that date has been found. He was necessarily born before 1667 and was probably an adult by then.

On 29 October 1667, Belfast merchant George Macartney reported that Mr Arthur wished to ship butter from Belfast to Rouen but had been unable to obtain a vessel. Macartney therefore proposed sending the butter to Dublin aboard the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats, of which James Glasgow was master.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 29 October 1667.</ref> This record identifies James as the master of a Scottish vessel engaged in trade between Belfast and Dublin, with the cargo intended ultimately for France.

On 21 January 1669/70, James was admitted and sworn as a free commoner of the Corporation of Belfast. The entry records him as:

: “James Glasco Marriner Admitted and sworne a ffree Comoner”

A fee of ten shillings was entered beside his name.<ref>Robert Magill Young, ed., ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816'' (Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892), p. 271; entry dated 21 January 1669 [Old Style, equivalent to 21 January 1670 New Style].</ref>

Admission as a free commoner gave James formal standing within the borough. The record is also direct contemporary evidence of his occupation and presence in Belfast.

James continued to work as a shipmaster during the following decade. On 8 November 1679, George Macartney recorded that he had freighted the ''James of Belfast'', commanded by James Glasgow, to carry butter and tallow to Havre de Grâce, now Le Havre, France.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter dated 8 November 1679.</ref> Macartney referred to the arrangement again that day in correspondence with Sir Joshua Allen concerning the payment of bills.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, letter from George Macartney to Sir Joshua Allen, dated 8 November 1679.</ref>

These records show James commanding at least two vessels—the ''Blessing'' of Saltcoats in 1667 and the ''James of Belfast'' in 1679—and participating in trade linking Belfast with Dublin and French ports. The surviving evidence supports describing him as a mariner and shipmaster. It does not establish that he owned either vessel or that he held the title of captain in a military or naval sense.

A testamentary reference for a James Glasgow of Belfast carries the year 1686 in the Connor will material.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index, entry for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref> The original will has not been examined, and its contents are presently unknown. The close agreement of name, place, occupation period, and date makes it probable that the testamentary record relates to the mariner, but this identification should remain qualified until the extract or surviving copy is consulted.

The year 1686 has not been established as his death or probate date: it may be the date of the will. His last dated lifetime record presently cited is the letter of 8 November 1679, so the death field is conservatively recorded as after that date. His place of death is also unproved. No reliable evidence has yet been found identifying his wife, children, parents, or descendants.

== Research Notes ==

* The surname appears as both ''Glasgow'' and ''Glasco''.
* The Corporation record uses Old Style dating. Its “21 January 1669” corresponds to 21 January 1670 under the modern calendar because the legal year then began on 25 March.
* A birth around 1600 is not supported by the cited records. It would make James about sixty-seven when first recorded as a working shipmaster and about seventy-nine in 1679. This is possible but presently speculative.
* Belfast should be treated as James’s place of residence or occupational association, not as a proved birthplace.
* The 1686 will-index entry is probably his, but the identification is not conclusive without examining the will extract.
* No evidence currently supports the claim that he left descendants or property in Belfast.

=== Possible north-east Antrim placement ===
Captain James is a possible son or younger relative of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glaskow of Larne]] and a possible collateral of the adjacent Kilwaughter householders [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho]]. Belfast, Larne and Kilwaughter form a credible north-east Antrim maritime and estate corridor, and a shipmaster active by 1667 fits the generation after Robert's 1653 occurrence. The evidence is geographical and chronological only; no record states a relationship.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, maritime material naming Captain James Glasgow or Glascow as a Belfast-associated shipmaster in the late 1660s and 1670s.</ref>

Captain James and the Kilwaughter James represented by [[Glasgow-1081]] are retained as separate, unproved identities. A will dated 1686 does not alone exclude survival to the 1720s. Conversely, the identification of the 1669 Kilwaughter householder with the later congregational officer is itself a continuity inference; an adult householder in 1669 surviving to 1726 would be at least about 78, and a same-name successor must be considered. The complete Belfast will extract and the Kilwaughter records are needed to decide this question.<ref>Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, will extract for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686.</ref>

== Sources ==

<references />

* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, business correspondence of George Macartney, merchant, 1672–1681, including related earlier material.
* Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/828/15, Connor Will Extracts and pre-1858 wills index.
* Young, Robert Magill, ed. ''The Town Book of the Corporation of Belfast, 1613–1816''. Belfast: Marcus Ward & Co., 1892, p. 271.

44300075.Name: Glasgow-3178
44300075.bio:
[[Category:Stevenston, Ayrshire]]

== Biography ==
'''Agnes Glasgow''' was a resident of Stevenston, Ayrshire, in the early 17th century. The primary record of her life is her testament, which confirms she was married to Johnne Logane, a "trumpmaker" (a crafter of Jew's harps).

Agnes passed away in or before March 1628, as her Testament Dative and Inventory was officially recorded in the Glasgow Commissary Court on 4 March 1628.<ref name="Testament1628">''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow, Register of Testaments, 1547-1800'', Vol. 7, ed. by Francis J. Grant (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), citing the testament of Agnes Glasgw, spouse to Johnne Logane, trumpmaker in Stevinstoune, parish of Stevinstoune. National Records of Scotland, Reference CC9/7/22.</ref> A "Testament Dative" indicates she died without leaving a will, and the court appointed an executor to manage her estate.

A 1932 published index also records “Agnes Glasgow, spouse of John, in Milneburne, Stenstoun,” under its “Logan (Logane)” heading. It dates the entry 29 June 1601 and gives vol. 1, fol. 94, Ayr. This is probably the same woman because the name, husband and Stevenston locality match her later testament; the original sasine has not been read, so retain this as a probable identification only.<ref name="Sasine1601">Scottish Record Office, ''Index to Secretary's Register of Sasines for Sheriffdom of Ayr and Bailiaries of Kyle, Carrick and Cunningham, 1599–1609'' (Edinburgh: H.M. Stationery Office, 1932), p. 128; FamilySearch, “Ayrshire. Land Records 1599–1609,” item no. 007830795, image 74/120 ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CS3Q-47SZ-P?view=fullText&keywords=GLASGOW&searchForm=advanced&lang=en&groupId=M9QN-ZXH FamilySearch image]), accessed 23 September 2026. The National Records of Scotland catalogues the original as RS11/1; [catalogue record](https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=RS11). The original register has not been inspected.</ref>

=== Family and Kinship ===
Based on the record, her husband was:
* '''Johnne Logane''', a trumpmaker in Stevenston.

It is highly likely that Agnes was the sister of [[Glasgow-1494|Jonet (Glasgow) Logan (abt.1610-)]]. This strong possibility is based on Jonet Glasgow also being married to a Logan (George Logan) in the same small parish of Stevenston at the exact same time (1628). It was a common pattern for two sisters to marry two brothers.

44300090.Name: Glasgow-3179
44300090.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
'''Geillis Glasgow''' was the spouse of [[Wilson-127012|Thomas Wilson]] at
Chaplehill in Ardrossan parish. Her testament states that she died in January
1603 and was confirmed on 11 May 1603.<ref name="GeillisWill">[https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills National Records
of Scotland, wills and testaments], Glasgow Commissary Court, testament dative
and inventory of Geillis Glasgow, CC9/7/3, images 113–114; working transcription
reinspection supplied 6 September 2026.</ref>

James, Isobel and Bessie Wilson are identifiable in the executor clause. The
words between James and Isobel remain unresolved, so [[Wilson-142005|James
Wilson]] should be treated only as a possible son, not as a directly proved
lawful son.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

Geillis's estate owed money to a James Glasgow in Stevenston.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

The testament does not identify Geillis's parents or state James Glasgow's
relationship to her. [[Glasgow-3921|James Glasgow younger of Corsankell]]
remains an uncertain father candidate only.

The debts also name the lord of Eglinton and servants Robert Boyd and a Bessie
whose surname is unresolved; Robert and Bessie were owed wages. The servant
Bessie is not thereby identified with Bessie Wilson in the executor clause.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

[[Glasgow-1495|Katherine Glasgow]] also died in January 1603 in neighbouring
Stevenston parish. The common date, adjoining parishes and Stevenston creditor
justify researching them as a kin network; they do not prove sisterhood.

The published testament index and Findmypast transcript are finding aids for
The original.<ref>Findmypast, Scotland Will and Testament Index,
[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FWILLS%2F057431 transcript],
Geillis Glasgow, 11 May 1603.</ref>

The testament proves Geillis's husband and son but does not name her parents. [[Glasgow-3921|James Glasgow]] and [[Smith-374110|Margaret Smith]] remain attached as uncertain parents because they belong to the same Ayrshire record cluster; the relationship has not been established.

Two difficult entries in the debt section may name a James Glasgow in the Gorbals and a Thomas Glasgow in the Saltmarket. Those readings remain useful leads, but the handwriting is not clear enough to identify either man or claim a relationship to Geillis. [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow]] is a possible comparison for the first name. The known profiles [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow]] are too late to be the man in a 1603 account.

The official index spells her forename Geillis and describes her as the spouse of Thomas Wilson in Chaipliehill, Ardrossan parish.

44300226.Name: Glasgow-3181
44300226.bio:
==  Biography  ==

=== Uncertain father ===

The currently attached [[Glasgow-1093|John Glasgow]] is a plausible but '''uncertain''' father. A Glasgow burgh protocol dated 13 May 1563 records John Glasgow senior resigning property to “John Glasgow junior, his son,” and a second protocol dated 8 January 1570/71 names “John Glasgw, younger son of John Glasgw.”<ref name="FatherProtocols">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 3, protocol 748, 13 May 1563, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n52/mode/2up scan]; vol. 6, protocol 1722, 8 January 1570/71, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc05scogoog/page/n58/mode/2up scan].</ref> These records directly prove that John-1093 had a son John of the correct generation, but no inspected record connects that burgh son to the man at Hirmanscheillis. The relationship must therefore remain uncertain, not confident or DNA-confirmed.

This testator cannot be the brother John named in [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]'s 1613 testament. Ninian's burgess admission identifies him as a son of [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]], and Ninian left a gown to a brother John who was alive on 10 January 1613.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/24/mode/2up p. 24], 23 October 1596; National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, testament of Ninian Glasgow, made 10 January 1613.</ref> Glasgow-3181 died in November 1576, so the earlier Robert-1096/Ninian sibling identification is chronologically impossible.

⚠️ '''Palaeographic Warning'''

This profile cites the registered testament of Johne Glasgw in National Records of Scotland reference CC8/8/5. Johne's entry begins on Image 276 and continues through only the upper portion of Image 277.

The lower portion of Image 277 begins a separate testament for '''Petir Hyme, quarter maister'''. A detached strip headed '''The confirmation of the testament of andro hutchesoun''' is likewise a separate record. Neither should be used as evidence concerning Johne Glasgw or Margaret Hoghame.

The manuscript is written in late sixteenth-century Scottish Secretary Hand. Original spelling is retained in the working transcription. Letters supplied when expanding contractions are placed in square brackets; uncertain or unreadable text is marked rather than silently reconstructed.

===  Testator  ===

'''Johne Glasgw''', styled '''in Hirmanscheillis''', died in November '''1576'''.

The year '''1577''' in the National Records of Scotland catalogue and the manuscript margin is the year in which the testament was processed by the Edinburgh Commissary Court. The manuscript distinguishes the dates:

* Death: November '''j m v c lxxvj''' — 1576.
* Executors-dative decree: '''xxj day of Aprile j m v c lxxvij''' — 21 April 1577.
* Marginal date: '''quarto May 1577''' — 4 May 1577.

===  Executors and family  ===

* '''Margaret Hoghame''' is described as Johne's '''relict'''. The spelling Hoghame often maps to families later shown as Hutchison.
* She gave up the inventory '''in name & behalfe''' of the bairns. She is not described as executrix.
* The two lawful bairns were:
** '''Katherine Glasgw'''
** '''Marjorie Glasgw'''
* Katherine and Marjorie, rather than Margaret, are described as the '''executouris dative decernit''' to their late father.

===  Inventory and valuation  ===

* The total inventory is read as '''xlix li xiij s iiij d''' — '''£49 13s 4d Scots'''.
* The clearest individual entry records '''tua young nolt of tua zeir auld''' — two young cattle, two years old.
* The remaining entries appear to include further livestock, agricultural produce or grain, meal or malt, household vessels and the '''abuilzement''' of Johne's body.
* Several item names and individual marginal valuations remain provisional. They should not be presented as settled diplomatic readings without checking a higher-resolution image.

===  Debts owed to the deceased  ===

The heading '''Followis the dettis awand to the deid''' is clear.

The current working readings of the debtor and place names include:

* '''Henry Coultar his wyf in Aderstoun'''
* '''Johne Donaldsone in the Borders'''
* '''Johne Williamsone in the Bent'''
* '''Sawll Wallace in Clocherd'''
* '''Robert Manys in Taleraw'''
* '''Johne Mathie in Boxhame'''

These personal names and place names remain palaeographic working readings. Modern locations should not yet be assigned solely from this image.

The current draft reads the Johne Mathie entry as '''xliij s iiij d''' and an old account for half a boll of oats as '''xvj s'''. The marginal figures should be checked again before being treated as final.

Nothing in the testament states or implies that Johne Mathie was related to Johne Glasgw. No connection should be made to later Mathie or Glasgow profiles from this debt entry alone.

===  Debts owed by the deceased  ===

The heading '''Followis the dettis awand be the deid''' is clear.

The following portion appears to include:

* kirk duties and burial expenses;
* a kist or coffin and mortcloth;
* funeral provisions including ale, wine, candles or spice;
* arrears of maill extending over six years.

The exact wording and sums remain working readings. The account concludes by calculating the free gear remaining after deduction of the debts.

===  Confirmation on Image 277  ===

The upper portion of Image 277 continues Johne Glasgw's entry. It contains the formal court procedure by which the testament and executors were confirmed and the required caution or surety was accepted.

No new testamentary family group begins at the top of Image 277. Johne's entry ends immediately before the large new heading in the middle of the page.

The large heading beginning '''The testament dative Inventar''' in the lower portion of Image 277 belongs to '''Petir Hyme, quarter maister''', not Johne Glasgw.

===  Archival and legal context  ===

* Margin note: '''Johne glasgw quarto May 1577'''.
* The body cites an executors-dative decree dated '''the xxj day of Aprile''' 1577.
* Johne's death clause gives November 1576.
* Court: Edinburgh Commissary Court.
* National Records of Scotland reference: CC8/8/5.
* Relevant manuscript extent: Image 276 and the upper portion of Image 277 only.

===  Diplomatic Transcription and Modern Rendering  ===
{{Image|file=Glasgow-3181.png|align=c|size=xl|caption=Image 276, NRS CC8/8/5}}

'''Semi-diplomatic working transcription'''

:Margin  Johne glasgw
:Margin  quarto May 1577

:1  The testament dative Inventar of the guidis geir soumes
:2  of money & dettis pertening to vmq[uhi]le Johne Glasgw in Hirmanscheillis
:3  the tyme of his deceis quha deceissit in the moneth of November
:4  the zeir of god j m v c lxxvj zeiris Faithfullie maid & gevin vp be
:5  Margaret Hoghame his relict in name & behalfe of Kathrine
:6  & Marjorie Glasgwis thair lauchfull bairnis & executouris dative decernit
:7  to thair said vmq[uhi]le father be decreit of the commissaris of Ed[inbu]r[gh]
:8  as the samin decreit of the dait xxj day of Aprile the zeir of
:9  god j m v c lxxvij zeiris at lenth proportis
:10 In the first the said vmq[uhi]le Johne Glasgw had guidis geir soumes
:11 of money & dettis of the availl & pryces following pertening to him
:12 in the tyme of his deceis foirsaid viz tua ky [valuation indistinct]
:13 Item tua young nolt of tua zeir auld pryce [indistinct]
:14 [Further livestock entry and valuation indistinct]
:15 [Further goods or produce and valuation indistinct]
:16 [Grain, meal or malt entry partly indistinct]
:17 [Further inventory entry partly indistinct]
:18 Item the abuilzement of his body [remainder partly indistinct]
:19 Summa of the Inventar, '''xlix li xiij s iiij d'''
:20 Followis the dettis awand to the deid
:21–32 [Several named debtors, places and sums follow. See the working readings above. A complete diplomatic reading of each name and marginal sum is not yet secure.]
:33 Followis the dettis awand be the deid
:34–40 [Kirk, burial and funeral expenses and arrears of maill follow. Individual wording and sums remain partly indistinct.]
:41–Image 277 upper [The court confirmation and caution clause continues.]
:End [Johne Glasgw's entry ends before the new testament for Petir Hyme.]

'''Modern English rendering'''

:1–2  This is the court-appointed testament and inventory of the goods, property, money and debts belonging to the late John Glasgow in Hirmansheils.
:3–4  He died in November 1576.
:4–6  His widow, Margaret Hoghame, submitted the inventory in the name and on behalf of Katherine and Marjorie Glasgow.
:6–9  Katherine and Marjorie were their lawful children and had been appointed executors dative to their late father by a decree of the Commissary Court of Edinburgh dated 21 April 1577.
:10–18  The inventory then lists John Glasgow's property and the value assigned to each item. The clearest entry is two young cattle, each two years old. Other entries concern livestock, agricultural produce, household goods and his clothing.
:19  The total inventory was £49 13s 4d Scots.
:20–32  The next section lists debts and other sums owed to John by named individuals.
:33–40  The following section lists John's own unpaid debts, including burial or kirk expenses and arrears of rent.
:Image 277 upper  The Commissary Court then completed the formal confirmation of the testament and executors after the required caution or surety was provided.

==  Research notes  ==

* '''1576 and 1577 are not competing readings of the same date.''' The manuscript gives death in November 1576, followed by court proceedings in April and May 1577.
* '''Hirmanscheillis''' is retained as the testament's confirmed place form. Published Calder barony-court extracts and a University of Glasgow place-name study identify the historical Hirdmanschiels forms with Hermand in West Calder.<ref>Hardy Bertram McCall, ''The History and Antiquities of the Parish of Mid-Calder'' (1894), [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/westcalder/mid_calder.pdf barony-court extracts]; ''The Germanic Toponymicon of Southern Scotland'', University of Glasgow thesis, [https://theses.gla.ac.uk/1343/1/2003scott1phd.pdf Hermand entry].</ref>
* '''Quarter maister''' belongs to Petir Hyme's separate testament in the lower portion of Image 277. It is not Johne Glasgw's occupation.
* The debt owed by Johne Mathie does not establish a family relationship.
* All monetary amounts are Scots money unless the source expressly says otherwise.
* The inventory total is read as '''xlix li xiij s iiij d''' — £49 13s 4d Scots.
* The item-level inventory and debtor readings remain provisional where the clerk's minims, abbreviations or marginal figures are indistinct.

==  Sources  ==
<references />
* National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/5, Image 276 and upper portion of Image 277, testament dative and inventory of Johne Glasgw in Hirmanscheillis; court record dated 1577.

Spouses.Name: Hutcheson-1656
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==
'''Margaret Hutcheson''' (also recorded as ''Hochaine'') lived in the mid-16th century in or near Hermiston (sometimes written Hirmenschelis) in the Lothians or Glasgow region.  

Her surname appears in her husband’s 1577 testament as ''Hochaine'', which may be a phonetic variant of ''Hutcheson'' or ''Hutchin'', both common in west-central Scotland at that time. She may be connected to the [[Hutcheson-1651|Hutchesons of Lambhill and Gairbraid]], but her precise parentage is not yet confirmed. 
=== Testament Record ===
Margaret is named as the ''relict'' (widow) of John Glasgow, who died in November 1575.  
On 6 March 1576, the Edinburgh Commissary Court decreed that their lawful children — Katherine Glasgow and Marion Glasgow — were his executors and heirs.  
Margaret acted as administratrix for them.

> ''“Faithfullie maid & gevin up be Margaret Hochaine his relict in name & behalf of Katherine & Marionne Glasgowis lawfull bairnes & executouris decernit…”''  
> — [National Records of Scotland, CC8/8/5, Edinburgh Commissary Court, 1577]

=== Family ===
* Spouse: John Glasgow (d. 1575)
* Children:
** Katherine Glasgow
** Marion Glasgow

=== Research Notes ===
* ''Hochaine'' may be a variant of ''Hutcheson'', but more evidence is needed.  
* No birth record survives; estimated birth before 1545.
* Parish registers and sasines for Hermiston may confirm her link to the wider Hutcheson line.

== See also ==
* Margaret’s surname appears as Hochaine, which may be a variant of Hutcheson or Hutchin. While her exact parents are unproven, her testament ties her to the Glasgow family — a line closely connected to the Hutchesons.
* Compare with [[Herbison-439|Margaret Herbison (abt. 1560–)]], daughter of Sir William Herbesoun. Although they are clearly not the same person, they show how local Glasgow, Hutcheson, and Herbesoun families likely intermarried and shared property connections within the same wider kinship network.



== Sources ==
* National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court CC8/8/5, Testament of John Glasgow, 1577.
* ''Early Records of an Old Glasgow Family'' by W.H. Hill (1902)

== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

Barbara Glasgow married, or had a marriage/proclamation entry with, [[Wilson-126696|Johne Wilsoune]] at South Leith in 1611. The South Leith OPR transcription gives 20 September 1611 (692/2 90/219, FR2993), while a FamilySearch marriage index gives 26 November 1611.<ref>South Leith OPR transcription, “GLASCOW BARBARA—JOHNE WILSOUNE,” 20 September 1611, parish 692/2, reference 90/219, FR2993.</ref><ref>“Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910,” FamilySearch [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYML-ZBB XYML-ZBB], Barbara Glasgow and Johne Wilsoune, 26 November 1611.</ref>

The original register is needed to determine whether the dates represent proclamation and marriage or a transcription error. The spouse is supported, but the exact marriage date remains unresolved.

== Research Notes ==

No reviewed record identifies Barbara's parents. Her birth about 1590 is an uncertain estimate from the 1611 marriage; no birthplace is proved, and South Leith is not a documented death place.

Other adult Barbara Glasgows appear at Edinburgh in 1611 and 1616: [[Glasgow-567|Barbara Glasgow]], mother of Catharine Little, and [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara Glasgow]], wife of George Johnstoun. Either may be the same woman, but no record proves an identity. [[Glasgow-1102|Barbara Glasgow]], baptised in 1617, is a later child. Do not merge the adult profiles without an identity bridge.

=== Branch and identity assessment ===
Barbara's leading family placement is as a possible daughter or niece of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]. Ninian's probable son [[Glasgow-3075|William]] later lived at Leith, while Ninian's proved son Robert was a cordiner. Barbara's South Leith entry and the adjoining Edinburgh cluster of Glasgow women marrying cordiners and a tailor fit that household's geography and trade network, but no record names her father.

Barbara may also be the same woman as [[Glasgow-567|Barbara, mother of Catharine Little]], and [[Glasgow-3302|Barbara, wife of George Johnstoun]]. Catharine was born on 9 September 1611;<ref>FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4N-CDX baptism index for Catharine Little], Edinburgh, 29 September 1611.</ref> the Wilson entry is dated either 20 September or 26 November 1611;<ref>FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYML-ZBB Barbara Glasgow and Johne Wilsoune marriage index].</ref> and the Johnstoun marriage was in 1616. The sequence is possible because the Little baptism proves parenthood, not a marriage. This is a moderate identity hypothesis only; do not merge until the original 1611 entries and John Wilson's fate are resolved.

== Biography ==
'''Thomas Glasgow''' was born before about 1627, probably in Scotland. His
exact birth date, birthplace and parents have not been established. Edinburgh
is a reasonable uncertain location from his documented adult household there,
but not a recorded place of birth.

Thomas and '''[[Weir-3979|Catharine Weir]]''' were the parents of four children
recorded in Edinburgh:

{| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding: 5px; width:100%;"
|+ '''Children recorded at Edinburgh'''
|-

! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Date
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Register reference
|-
| [[Glasgow-1160|Margaret Glasgow]] || 27 December 1644 || Edinburgh OPR 685/1, FR1323
|-
| [[Glasgow-1161|Elizabeth Glasgow]] || 1 July 1647 || Edinburgh OPR 685/1, FR1362
|-
| [[Glasgow-1162|Catharine Glasgow]] || 16 January 1649 || Edinburgh OPR 685/1, FR1400
|-
| [[Glasgow-1163|Jeane Glasgow]] || 8 March 1650 || Edinburgh OPR 685/1, FR1426
|}<ref name="Children">Edinburgh parish register index entries preserved on
The live profiles: Margaret Glasgow, 27 December 1644, Thomas Glasgow/Catharine
Weir, OPR 685/1, FR1323; Elizabeth Glasgow, 1 July 1647, OPR 685/1, FR1362;
Catharine Glasgow, 16 January 1649, OPR 685/1, FR1400; and Jeane Glasgow, 8
March 1650, OPR 685/1, FR1426.</ref>

The first child's date shows that Thomas and Catharine were together by
December 1644. The profile's 1644 marriage date is therefore an estimate, not
an identified marriage entry.

On 2 May 1660 Thomas was admitted as a burgess and guild brother of Edinburgh,
gratis.<ref name="Burgess1660">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed.,
[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=219
''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record
Society, 1929), printed p. 209: “Glasgow, Thos., B. and G., gratis”, 2 May
1660; see also Findmypast,
[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FBURGESS%2F1009527&tab=this
SCOT/BURGESS/1009527], captured 3 September 2026.</ref> The word “gratis” means
that the entry does not supply the usual apprenticeship- or marriage-right; it
does not identify Thomas's occupation or relatives.

Thomas's death date and place have not been identified. He was alive on 2 May
1660.<ref name="Burgess1660" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

==== Identification with the burgess ====
The 1660 burgess is probably this Thomas. The exact name, city and adult
chronology continue the Edinburgh household documented between 1644 and 1650.
The admission lacks a wife, trade or kinship statement, so the identification
should remain explicitly probable.

==== Parentage ====
Thomas is attached to [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] and [[Mathie-159|Jonet
Mathie]]. No birth or baptism record inspected for Thomas names those parents.
The child records and burgess admission establish his adult Edinburgh identity
but do not prove that attachment. Preserve the relationships as uncertain
working hypotheses unless direct evidence is found.

==== Thomas M.A. ====
[[Glasgow-3413|Thomas Glasgow M.A.]] graduated from the University of Edinburgh
on 20 March 1670.<ref>[https://archive.org/details/catalogueofgr10600univuoft/page/100/mode/2up
''A Catalogue of the Graduates in the Faculties of Arts, Divinity, and Law of
The University of Edinburgh''], printed p. 100.</ref> He is attached as a son
of this household, but the university entry supplies no father and shared
city/name evidence is insufficient. Keep that relationship uncertain.

Thomas's wife [[Weir-3979|Catharine Weir]] should not be confused with
[[Glasgow-1495|Catharine Glasgow]], wife of a Thomas Weir. The broader
same-name comparison is maintained at
[https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Thomas-1 Thomas Research].

* [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Space:Thomas-1 Thomas Research]
* His wife, [[Weir-3979|Catherine (Weir) Glasgow (abt.1625-)]] is not to be confused with [[Glasgow-1495|Catherine (Glasgow) Weir (bef.1584-)]]

46166326.bio:
{{Estimated Date}} [[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] A 1610 Glasgow Commissary Court index records "Bessie, spouse to John Glasgow, in Montfoid" on 17 August 1610.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547-1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196]. This profile retains the Montfoid husband as an '''uncertain earlier same-person hypothesis''' for the John Glasgow of Quodquen whose estate was confirmed in 1650; no reviewed record bridges the two places or proves they were the same man. '''Transcription and identification note:''' This profile is based principally on the 1650 testament dative of John Glasgow in Quodquen. The document is written in seventeenth-century Scots Secretary Hand. The relationship between John and Bessie Glasgow is secure. The testament first describes Bessie as John’s “laufull sister” and later describes John as “hir brother”. A separate 1610 testament index identifies Bessie Robertson as the spouse of a John Glasgow in Montfoid. It has not been established that the John Glasgow in Montfoid was the same man as John Glasgow in Quodquen. {{Image|file=Glasgow-3296.png |align=c |size=l |caption=Testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, 1650. Lanark Commissary Court, National Records of Scotland reference CC14/5/5, images 65–66. }} == Biography == '''John Glasgow''' lived at Quodquen in Lanarkshire. He died in April 1650, and his estate was confirmed at Lanark on 27 May 1650.National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, CC14/5/5, images 65–66, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen; confirmed 27 May 1650.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy]. His testament was dative because he died intestate. It twice identifies Bessie Glasgow as his lawful sister: first when appointing her executrix dative and again when describing John as her brother. It names no parent, wife, son or daughter. Thomas Glasgow, deceased, and a William Glasgow appear in the financial account, but their relationships to John are not stated. === Residence and death === '''John Glasgow''' lived at '''Quodquen''', in Lanarkshire, Scotland.National Records of Scotland, Lanark Commissary Court, Wills and Testaments, reference CC14/5/5, testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow in Quodquen, images 65–66. He died during '''April 1650'''. His estate was confirmed at Lanark on '''27 May 1650'''.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, “Glasgow, John, in Quodquen,” 27 May 1650, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy]. The record gives Quodquen as John’s residence. It does not state his birthplace or exact place of death. === Testament and executrix === John’s estate was recorded as a '''testament dative'''. He had died intestate, and the commissary court appointed an executor to administer the estate. [[Glasgow-XXXX|Bessie Glasgow]] was appointed executrix dative. The testament expressly describes her as John’s:
“laufull sister”
The confirmation later describes John as:
“hir brother”
The relationship is therefore directly stated twice in the original record. On 27 May 1650 Bessie appeared before Master John Carmichael, commissary of Lanark, presented the inventory and was confirmed as executrix after providing the required caution. === Estate === John’s physical possessions included: * three kine, valued together at £8 Scots; * his clothing or bodily apparel, valued at £20 Scots. The physical inventory totalled '''£28 Scots'''. The testament also listed debts and sums owing to John’s estate. The clerk recorded:
“Na debtis awin be ye deid”
No debts owed by John himself were entered. The clerk also recorded:
“Na divisioun”
No formal division of the estate was entered. === Family === ==== Sister ==== * [[Glasgow-XXXX|Bessie Glasgow]] — John’s lawful sister and executrix dative. No parent, wife, son or daughter is identified in John’s 1650 testament. The absence of a wife or child from the record does not prove that John had never married or had no children. It means only that none is named in this testament. ==== Possible wife: Bessie Robertson ==== The published index to the Glasgow Commissariot Register contains the entry:
“Robertson, Bessie, spouse to John Glasgow, in Montfoid — 17 Aug. 1610”
The corresponding entry under Glasgow reads:
“Glasgow, John, in Montfoid. See Robertson, Bessie.”
This establishes that '''Bessie Robertson''' was the wife of a John Glasgow in Montfoid. The date is the testament date, not a marriage date.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'', Scottish Record Society, vol. 7 (Edinburgh, 1901), p. 426, entry for Robertson, Bessie, dated 17 August 1610, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/426/mode/2up digital copy]. It is possible that the Montfoid man was the same John who later lived at Quodquen, but this has not been proved. The two records concern different residences and commissary jurisdictions, and neither provides a distinctive identifier linking the men. Bessie Robertson should therefore remain a research possibility, not a confirmed wife. She must not be confused with John’s sister Bessie Glasgow. === Other people named in the testament === The following people appear in connection with money or debts owing to John’s estate: * Thomas Glasgow, deceased, in Quodquen; * John Miller, described as an executor; * W[illia]m Glasgow, apparently owing £8 Scots; * Isobell Fisher in Glasfurde; * James Gibson in Quodquen; * a probable William Wilsone; * Master John Carmichael, commissary of Lanark; * an unidentified cautioner for Bessie Glasgow. Thomas Glasgow and W[illia]m Glasgow may have belonged to the wider Glasgow family at Quodquen, but the testament does not state their relationship to John. == Research Notes == === Current evidence assessment === ==== Distinct records combined on this profile ==== The former profile [[Glasgow-3296]] now redirects here. That merge brought in a separate Mid Calder reconstruction. Derivative baptism indexes name a Jhone Glasgow as father of Jhone in 1608 and William in 1609.“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch ([https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-X8B record X1BL-X8B]), Jhone Glasgow, 1608, father Jhone Glasgow.“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch ([https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1B2-3LV record X1B2-3LV]), William Glasgow, baptised 24 December 1609 at Mid Calder, son of Jhone Glasgow. Those records prove a father-child pair in Mid Calder but provide no bridge to the man whose estate was confirmed at Quodquen forty-one years later. [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]] must therefore remain uncertain children of this profile. A 1610 testament index also identifies Bessie Robertson as the wife of a John Glasgow in Montfoid.Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/n435/mode/1up p. 426], Robertson, Bessie, 17 August 1610; cross-reference under Glasgow, John, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/1up p. 196]. Bessie Robertson was the wife of the Montfoid man; she was not the Bessie Glasgow identified as the Quodquen man's sister. The Montfoid, Mid Calder and Quodquen records are chronologically compatible with one life, but no residence, occupation, property, spouse or kinship evidence joins all three. Both earlier identities and the wife relationship remain uncertain. The attached [[Glasgow-1029|Stephen Glasgow]] and Margaret Graham are not identified as this John's parents by any of these records. Their links must remain uncertain pending positive relationship evidence. The testament gives Quodquen as John's residence, not his birthplace or place of death. The present Mid Calder death location came from the merged earlier reconstruction and is unsupported by a death record; it must be treated as uncertain unless a sourced replacement location is established. [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow]] of nearby Linlithgow is a duplicate candidate only. Similar name, date and region do not justify another merge without an identity bridge. === Data corrections === The cited testament shows that John: * died in April 1650, not 1649; * lived at Quodquen; * was confirmed on 27 May 1650. The record does not state that he died at Carluke. Carluke should therefore be removed as the death location unless supported by another source. === Working child relationship === No child is identified in John’s testament. The existing relationship to [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow]] (formerly Glasgow-3019) is retained as an '''uncertain working son''', not as a proved relationship. The 1650 testament neither identifies nor disproves him. The 1650 testament does not prove John as the father of: * Isobell Glasgow; * John Glasgow of Burnesyde; * any other presently identified child. === Parentage === John’s father and mother are not named in the 1650 testament. Any parent relationship should remain unsupported unless established by another record. === Further research === Useful records include: * the original 1610 testament of Bessie Robertson; * Quodquen parish and kirk-session records; * land, sasine and rental records naming John, Bessie, Thomas or William Glasgow; * records identifying John Miller and the estate for which he acted; * any record connecting John Glasgow of Montfoid with Quodquen; * evidence establishing whether Thomas Glasgow or William Glasgow was related to John and Bessie. John was born before 1590. Might be the same person as [[Glasgow-3296|John Glasgow (abt.1590-1649)]] and/or [[Glasgow-1561|John Glasgow (abt.1579-)]] == Sources == * See [[Glasgow-1086|John Glasgow (1608-)]]

== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

'''Barbara (Glasgow) Johnstoun''' was born before 1600, calculated from her 1616 marriage to [[Johnstoun-29|George Johnstoun (abt.1594–)]]. Their marriage is recorded in Scottish parish records.

=== Possible Connections ===
Early 17th-century Edinburgh-area records mention several women named Barbara Glasgow who may or may not be closely related:
* [[Glasgow-3182|Barbara (Glasgow) Wilson (abt.1590–)]] who married [[Wilson-126696|John Wilson (1590–)]] in 1611 at South Leith.
* [[Glasgow-567|Barbara (Glasgow) Little (abt.1586–)]] of Edinburgh, mother of Catharine Little (bapt. 1611).
* [[Glasgow-1102|Barbara Glasgow (b.1617)]], daughter of George Glasgow and Margaret Steuart, with older siblings Margrat (b.1610), Thomas (b.1612), and Archibald (b.1614).

Although no direct evidence ties these women together, their overlapping timelines and parishes suggest potential family connections.

=== Branch and identity assessment ===
Barbara's leading family placement is within the household or immediate collateral circle of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]. Her husband George Johnstoun was a cordiner,<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595-1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 printed p. 267], 21 November 1616.</ref> the same trade as Ninian's proved son Robert. Ninian's probable son [[Glasgow-3075|William]] later lived in Leith and William's son entered a cordiner apprenticeship. This is concrete trade and locality evidence, but no record names Barbara's father.

Barbara may be a later appearance of [[Glasgow-3182|Barbara Wilson]] and [[Glasgow-567|Barbara, mother of Catharine Little]]. The 1611 Little birth, the disputed September or November Wilson entry, and the 1616 Johnstoun marriage form a possible successive life course. Assessment: moderate identity hypothesis. Do not merge until the original 1611 entries and John Wilson's death or disappearance are resolved.

== Sources ==
<references />
* "Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910," FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMH-HZJ : 11 February 2020), Barbara Glasgow in entry for George Johnstoun, 1616.

46280224.Name: Glasgow-3322
46280224.bio:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

== Biography ==

'''Daniel Glasco''' was associated with Lower Norfolk County in the Colony of Virginia during the late seventeenth century. His date and place of birth have not been identified.

The spelling '''Glasco''' is used in the published abstract of the only contemporary record presently identified for him. The original record should be inspected before concluding that this was his consistent surname spelling.

May be a grandson of [[Glasgow-1157|Robert Glasgow II (abt.1612-abt.1690)]]

=== Marriage to Mary Gamon ===

Daniel married '''Mary Gamon''', also rendered Gammon in later accounts, before 4 October 1693.

The will of Mary's father, '''John Gamon''', was dated 4 October 1693 and proved on 15 March 1694. Its published abstract identifies Daniel Glasco as John Gamon's son-in-law and Mary as Daniel's wife. John left Daniel and Mary eighty acres of land bordering Richford Swamp.<ref name="GamonWill">Charles Fleming McIntosh, ''Brief Abstract of Lower Norfolk County and Norfolk County Wills, 1637–1710'' (Virginia: Colonial Dames of America in the State of Virginia, 1914), p. 149, abstract of the will of John Gamon, dated 4 October 1693 and proved 15 March 1694; cited and discussed in Legacy Tree Genealogists, [https://www.legacytree.com/wp-content/uploads/T1508095.CLIENTGlasgow1508.report.public.pdf ''Research Report''] (1 March 2016), p. 3.</ref>

The record directly establishes that:

* Daniel and Mary were married by 4 October 1693;
* Mary's father was John Gamon; and
* Daniel and Mary received land bordering Richford Swamp.

Richford Swamp was situated in Elizabeth River Parish, Lower Norfolk County.<ref name="LegacyReport">Legacy Tree Genealogists, [https://www.legacytree.com/wp-content/uploads/T1508095.CLIENTGlasgow1508.report.public.pdf ''Research Report''] (1 March 2016), pp. 3–4.</ref>

The will abstract does not identify Daniel's parents, birthplace, age, occupation or children.

Daniel was alive on 4 October 1693. His date and place of death have not been identified.

== Research Notes ==

=== Birth date ===

Daniel has previously been assigned a birth year of 1613.

The cited source for that date is an International Genealogical Index entry submitted by an unidentified contributor. The entry contains no supporting source information.<ref name="IGI">The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, “International Genealogical Index (IGI),” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/2:1:MDL3-HTF entry for Daniel Glasgow] (accessed 4 April 2025); submitted by user jence5408, with no source information supplied.</ref>

A submitted IGI entry records a contributor's assertion. Without an underlying baptism, Bible, will, deed or other historical record, it does not establish that Daniel was born in 1613.

Daniel's birth date and birthplace should therefore be left unknown.

For database purposes, the only certain statement is that he was born before 4 October 1693, when he was recorded as Mary's husband.

=== Unsupported Scottish parentage ===

'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' have previously been attached as Daniel's parents.

No inspected record identifies either person as his father or mother.

The will of John Gamon identifies Daniel's wife and father-in-law but does not name Daniel's parents. No Scottish baptism, marriage, testament, land record or migration record has been found connecting Daniel with Robert Glasgow or Deborah Ivey.

Both parental relationships should be removed.

Daniel should also not be attached as a child of '''[[Glasgow-3938|Robert Glasgow]]''', the cordiner who married Jonet or Janet Thomsone in Edinburgh in 1652. No evidence connects that Edinburgh household with Daniel or colonial Virginia.

=== Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson tradition ===

Many online family trees instead identify Daniel as a son of a Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson or Johnston.

A professional review of the family found that this relationship was repeated in online trees but that those trees supplied no documentary evidence supporting it.<ref name="LegacyReport" />

No contemporary record presently establishes that:

* Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson were Daniel's parents;
* Daniel was born in Scotland;
* Daniel migrated from Scotland to Virginia; or
* Daniel belonged to the Scottish Glasgow families represented by the earlier profiles.

Any attachment to Robert Glasgow and Ann Johnson should remain uncertain or be removed until a contemporary parentage record is found.

=== Possible connection with Robert Glascocke ===

A Robert Glascocke was documented in the Elizabeth River area before Daniel's known appearance there.

Robert Glascocke received:

* a patent for 200 acres in Elizabeth City County on 7 October 1635; and
* a patent for another fifty acres in Lower New Norfolk County on 10 June 1639.

A 1640 court order also referred to religious services being held at Robert Glascocke's house while a meetinghouse was being built.<ref name="LegacyReport" />

The shared locality and broadly similar surnames make Robert Glascocke a person worth investigating as a possible relative.

They do not prove that:

* Robert Glascocke was Daniel's father;
* Glascocke and Glasco were forms used by the same family;
* Robert married Ann Johnson;
* Daniel inherited Robert's land; or
* either man belonged to a Scottish Glasgow family.

Robert Glascocke should not be attached as Daniel's father without a deed, will, court record or other document connecting them.

=== Surname ===

The published abstract of John Gamon's will records Daniel's surname as '''Glasco'''.

Later records and compiled genealogies use variants including:

* Glasco;
* Glasgow;
* Glascock;
* Glasscock; and
* Glascocke.

Surname spelling was not fully standardised during this period, but similarity alone does not prove that all these records concern one family.

The original will should be inspected to establish the spelling used by the clerk. Until then, Glasco is the best-supported spelling for Daniel himself, with Glasgow retained as an alternate form where appropriate.

=== Children ===

No inspected contemporary record identifies a child of Daniel Glasco and Mary Gamon.

Later family trees attribute children and extensive descendants to the couple, but those relationships should not be treated as established solely because they appear in compiled genealogies.

Each proposed child requires separate evidence, such as:

* a baptism or parish entry;
* a deed describing the relationship;
* a will naming the child;
* a guardianship record;
* an apprenticeship record;
* a court order; or
* a documented chain of inherited land.

Any existing child attachments should remain uncertain pending review of their individual evidence.

=== The inherited property ===

John Gamon's will left Daniel and Mary eighty acres bordering Richford Swamp.

Tracing that property may be the best route for identifying Daniel's later life and possible children. Deeds involving its later sale, inheritance or division may name Daniel's heirs or establish whether he had died.

The original will, probate proceedings and subsequent land records should be obtained rather than relying solely on the published abstract.

=== Death ===

Daniel's date and place of death are unknown.

He was alive when John Gamon's will was written on 4 October 1693. The will's probate on 15 March 1694 does not necessarily prove Daniel was still living on that later date.

His death should therefore be recorded as after 4 October 1693 only if an estimated date is required. No precise death place should be assigned.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original will of John Gamon;
* the complete probate file and estate accounts;
* deeds concerning the eighty acres bordering Richford Swamp;
* Lower Norfolk County court orders;
* Elizabeth River Parish records;
* later Norfolk and Princess Anne County deeds and probate records;
* records identifying Daniel and Mary's children or heirs;
* land records concerning Robert Glascocke's patents;
* evidence establishing whether Glasco, Glasgow and Glascocke were used for the same family;
* contemporary records concerning Ann Johnson or Johnston;
* any immigration or transportation record for Daniel;
* a will or estate administration for Daniel;
* a will or estate administration for Mary; and
* the original evidence underlying the submitted IGI entry.

== Sources ==

<references />

== Acknowledgements ==

This profile was previously attached to an unsupported Scottish family and carried an unsourced birth year of 1613. It has been revised to represent Daniel Glasco, husband of Mary Gamon, documented through the 1693–1694 will of John Gamon.

46296301.bio:
'''⚠️ Paleographic Warning:'''

This profile is based on a testament written in 17th-century Secretary Hand. Due to the ornate and inconsistent handwriting style, all names, places, and relationships should be considered '''tentative''' and subject to '''revision''' pending further document comparison or corroboration. Interpretations are paleographically informed but speculative.

== Biography ==

''This profile is a placeholder for a 17th-century Glasgow individual from Lanarkshire, possibly the son of [[Glasgow-3019|John Glasgow (abt.1610–bef.1653)]], and part of an early Glasgow family line based near Biggar.''

This man was active in '''Quothquan''' parish, in the rural uplands west of '''Biggar''', on the Lanarkshire–Peeblesshire border.

He is identified in the '''13 July 1662''' testament dative of John Glasgow as his '''lawful son and executor dative'''. The estate was confirmed in the '''Lanark Commissary Court''' (CC14/5/6), where he gave oath and produced an inventory of goods. A man named '''James Glasgow''', described as John’s brother, also appeared and gave assurance.

This individual was the same '''John Glasgow''' who appears again in a separate testament dative dated '''25 March 1685''' (CC14/5/12), also in Quothquan, suggesting he survived his father by several decades and managed property in the same location.

He may have been born between '''1630 and 1635''', which would make him old enough to serve as legal executor in 1662. No spouse or children are yet confirmed.

== Sources ==
<references />
* Lanark Commissary Court Records:
** '''13 Jul 1662''' – Testament of John Glasgow, naming son as executor (CC14/5/6)
** '''25 Mar 1685''' – Testament of John Glasgow in Quothquan (CC14/5/12)
** '''27 May 1650''' – Entry for John Glasgow in Quothquan (CC14/5/5)
* Testament images and transcription via ScotlandsPeople

Elizabeth Glasgow was recorded at Polwarth, Berwickshire, on 17 August 1656. The FamilySearch index names her father as William Glasgow.<ref name="ElizabethPolwarth">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYL3-24Q : accessed 16 September 2021), Elizabeth Glasgow, Polwarth, 17 August 1656.</ref>

Other details blank; age blank; gender F. Original image not inspected.</ref>

The 1656 index names Elizabeth's father only as William Glasgow. It does not identify him with [[Glasgow-2462|William Glasgow]], whose own record is at Inveresk and whose profile supplies no documented move to Polwarth. That father link remains uncertain pending the original parish entry or another identity bridge.

The 1657 entry is a probable match, not proof that the child died on that exact day. Check the original OPR 754/10/30 entry for a parent, age or residence and for whether the date denotes death, burial or another burial-related entry. 26613954.Name: Glasgow-991
26613954.bio:
== Biography ==
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}
James Glasgow was born circa 1585, likely in Scotland. This estimate is based on the birth year of his first known child in 1605. He appears in baptismal records as a father residing in Midlothian, Scotland, between 1605 and 1618, with records showing activity in two distinct parishes: Mid Calder (OPR parish #694) and Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref>A patron submission to the LDS Church suggested a birth location of Inveresk, but this requires stronger sourcing. See Research Notes.</ref>

The mother of his children is not named in these specific records. James is recorded as the father of the following six children, with the location alternating between the two parishes:

* [[Glasgow-1082|George Glasgow]], christened 17 February 1605 in Mid Calder.<ref name="George1605">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BK-1B4), James Glasgow in entry for Gerge Glasgow, 1605.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-994|Eduard Glasgow]], born 27 February 1609 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="Eduard1609">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRF-FQX), James Glasgow in entry for Eduard Glasgow, 1609.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1083|Beatrix Glasgow]], christened 15 April 1610 in Mid Calder.<ref name="Beatrix1610">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-L51), James Glasgow in entry for Beatrix Glasgow, 1610.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-992|William Glasgow]], born 10 July 1614 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="William1614">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRN-WMS), James Glasgow in entry for William Glasgow, 1614.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-1084|John Glasgow]], christened 18 February 1616 in Mid Calder.<ref name="John1616">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-JXY), James Glasgow in entry for John Glasgow, 1616.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-993|Agnes Glasgow]], born 22 February 1618 in Inveresk with Musselburgh.<ref name="Agnes1618">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTRJ-SZX), James Glasgow in entry for Agnes Glasgow, 1618.</ref>

The pattern of baptisms/births alternating between Mid Calder and Inveresk with Musselburgh (parishes roughly 15-18 miles apart) suggests James and his family had significant ties, possibly residency or work, in both locations within Midlothian during this period.

The date and location of James Glasgow's death are currently unknown.

=== Research Notes ===

* '''Dual Locations:''' The records confirm activity in Mid Calder (Parish 694) and Inveresk with Musselburgh, Midlothian. Further research into land, kirk session, or court records might clarify the family's presence in both parishes.
* '''Single Identity Assumption:''' This profile currently assumes these records pertain to one James Glasgow, based on the consistent name and plausible timeframe/geography. However, the possibility of two contemporaries named James Glasgow cannot be entirely ruled out without further evidence (e.g., marriage, death, or conflicting records).
* '''Inveresk Birth Claim:''' A citation noted "Place of birth is listed as Inveresk<ref name="PatronSub">Patron submission record, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints ''(Note: Source details are vague in original text; treat with caution unless specific record identified).''</ref>". This is generally considered weak evidence unless corroborated by primary sources.
* '''Possible Earlier Record (Speculative):''' A record from Perth dated 19 January 1575 mentions the baptism of a James '''Glas''', son of '''Alexander Glas''' (Perth OPR 387/10/172).<ref name="Perth1575">OPR entry: “GLAS JAMES / ALEXR. GLAS/ M 19/01/1575 387 10 / 172 Perth”. Also cited via FamilySearch profile LZGY-NSY (https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/details/LZGY-NSY) accessed [Insert Date].</ref> Any connection between this Perth record and the James Glasgow of Midlothian (born c. 1585) is unconfirmed and requires significant further research. It may relate to a different individual or family line.
* '''Mother Unknown:''' The mother of the children listed above is not identified in these baptism/birth records.
* '''Excluded Information:''' Information regarding a wife named Christina Bie, later generations potentially linked via Geneanet, or specific GEDmatch references previously in comments have been excluded from this biography pending reliable sources confirming their connection to *this* James Glasgow.



=== Connection to Father ===
Placement under Andrew Glasgow (bef.1540–1598) fits the alternating parish pattern between Mid Calder and Inveresk/Musselburgh from 1605 to 1618. Andrew’s branch anchors the Caldercleir/Mid-Lothian corridor and expands toward the east-coast parishes. Andrew’s testament names sons James and John; this James matches that statement and geography. No record on this page states his father.

* '''Next Step:''' Compare sponsors and witnesses across the 1605–1618 baptisms with Andrew’s testament and nearby sasines for overlapping names.

=== Possible older daughter ===
[[Glasgow-3183|Jonet Glasgow, wife of Martin Ramsy]], is James's leading possible older daughter. James is the only identified same-generation Glasgow repeatedly recorded as a father at Mid Calder, where children attributed to him were baptised in 1605, 1610 and 1616; Jonet married there in 1624.<ref>FamilySearch indexes: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BK-1BW George Glasgow, 1605], [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BJ-L51 Beatrix Glasgow, 1610], [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X1BL-JXY John Glasgow, 1616], and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9X-4PR Jonet Glasgow and Martin Ramsy, 1624].</ref>

The placement also resolves a conflict in Jonet's current genealogy: Andrew of Corstoun's 1598 testament names exactly four operative children and excludes her.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32; printed index in ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514-1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref> James is now attached as Jonet's uncertain working father. The relationship remains a moderate-to-strong placement rather than direct proof, and Jonet's mother is unidentified.
