46507815.Name: Glasgow-3375
46507815.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' was born before about 1661, probably in Scotland. His exact date and place of birth are unknown.

The estimated birth date is based on John being old enough to have a child baptised in July 1679. He may have been born considerably earlier.

John was living in, or otherwise associated with, the parish of Kilwinning, Ayrshire, Scotland, between 1679 and 1689.

He had at least two known children:

* '''Jon Glasgow''', baptised on 6 July 1679 in Kilwinning, recorded as the son of Jon Glasgow and Barbara Alason.<ref name="Jon1679">Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 44, baptism of Jon Glasgow, 6 July 1679, son of Jon Glasgow and Barbara Alason.</ref>
* '''Jannet Glasgow''', baptised on 1 February 1689 in Kilwinning, recorded as the daughter of John Glasgow and a woman recorded by the surname Allason.<ref name="Jannet1689">Kilwinning Old Parish Register, parish 599, frame 75, baptism of Jannet Glasgow, 1 February 1689, daughter of John Glasgow and Allason.</ref>

The woman surnamed Allason in Jannet's baptism was probably the same Barbara Alason named in Jon's baptism. The surviving indexed entry does not give her forename.

Her surname may appear in records under several spellings, including Alason, Allason, Alison and Allison.

No marriage or proclamation record for John Glasgow and Barbara Alason has yet been identified. Barbara should therefore be described as John's probable wife or partner rather than as a proven legal spouse.

John was alive, or was at least named as the father, when Jannet was baptised in February 1689.

His date and place of death are unknown.

=== Children ===

John Glasgow and probably Barbara Alason had the following known children:

# '''Jon Glasgow''', baptised 6 July 1679 at Kilwinning, Ayrshire.<ref name="Jon1679" />

# '''Jannet Glasgow''', baptised 1 February 1689 at Kilwinning, Ayrshire.<ref name="Jannet1689" />

There may have been other children whose baptisms were not recorded, whose records have not survived, or whose entries have not yet been identified.

== Possible Parentage ==

John's parents have not been established.

Five Scottish baptism records have been identified for men named John or Johne Glasgow who were born within, or close to, a plausible period for the father of a child baptised in 1679.

None of these records currently provides a direct connection to Kilwinning, Barbara Alason, or the children Jon and Jannet Glasgow.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 27 April 1656 in South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone.<ref name="John1656">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 27 April 1656, South Leith, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 23 years old when Jon Glasgow was baptised in 1679 and about 32 when Jannet was baptised in 1689.

He is a strong chronological candidate among the currently identified records.

However, South Leith is in Midlothian, while John's known children were baptised in Kilwinning, Ayrshire. No evidence has yet been found showing that this Johne moved to Ayrshire or was associated with Barbara Alason.

Archbald Glasgow and Agnes Watsone should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Johne Glasgow ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 22 April 1649 in Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of another Johne Glasgow.<ref name="John1649">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 22 April 1649, Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Johne Glasgow. The indexed record does not name his mother.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 30 years old in 1679 and about 40 in 1689.

He is chronologically plausible, but no evidence currently links him or his father with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

The elder Johne Glasgow should not presently be attached as John's father.

=== John Glasgow, son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse ===

A John Glasgow was baptised on 25 February 1644 in Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse.<ref name="John1644">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," John Glasgow, baptised 25 February 1644, Linlithgow, Linlithgowshire, Scotland, son of Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse.</ref>

This John would have been about 35 years old in 1679 and about 45 in 1689.

He is chronologically plausible, but no evidence has yet been found connecting him or his parents with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

Thomas Glasgow and Hellin Bryse should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 4 April 1639 in Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman.<ref name="John1639">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 4 April 1639, Duddingston, Midlothian, Scotland, son of Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman.</ref>

This Johne would have been about 40 years old in 1679 and about 50 in 1689.

He is chronologically possible, but no record currently links him with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

Johne Glasgow and Margaret Sluman should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Johne Glasgow, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan ===

A Johne Glasgow was baptised on 30 August 1661 in Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland. He was recorded as the son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.<ref name="John1661">FamilySearch, "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," Johne Glasgow, baptised 30 August 1661, Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>

This Johne would have been approximately 17 years and 10 months old when Jon Glasgow was baptised on 6 July 1679. He would probably have been about 17 when the child was conceived.

He cannot be excluded entirely, but he is a less likely candidate because of his young age. His baptism also falls slightly later than John's estimated birth date of before about 1661.

No evidence has been found connecting him with Kilwinning or Barbara Alason.

James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan should not presently be attached as John's parents.

=== Parentage Assessment ===

The candidates may be ranked by chronological plausibility as follows:

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1656 at South Leith — about 23 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1649 at Kirknewton and East Calder — about 30 years old in 1679.

# '''John Glasgow''', baptised in 1644 at Linlithgow — about 35 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1639 at Duddingston — about 40 years old in 1679.

# '''Johne Glasgow''', baptised in 1661 at Edinburgh — about 17 years old in 1679.

This ranking concerns age only. It is not evidence that the higher-ranked candidates were more closely connected to the Kilwinning family.

All five men were baptised in Midlothian or Linlithgowshire. The John Glasgow represented by this profile is currently known only from the baptism records of his children in Kilwinning, Ayrshire.

No candidate has yet been shown to have:

* lived in Kilwinning or elsewhere in Ayrshire;
* married or formed a household with Barbara Alason;
* fathered Jon Glasgow or Jannet Glasgow;
* used an occupation or territorial designation matching the Kilwinning records;
* shared relatives, witnesses, neighbours or associates with the Kilwinning family.

The absence of a matching Ayrshire baptism does not prove that John was born elsewhere. Scottish Old Parish Registers are incomplete, and some baptisms were never recorded or have not survived.

John's parents should remain unknown until additional evidence links one of these baptism records to the Kilwinning family.

== Research Notes ==

=== Original Kilwinning Records ===

The original images of the Kilwinning baptism entries should be examined rather than relying only on abbreviated index entries.

The images may contain information omitted from the index, including:

* John's occupation;
* a farm, village or residence;
* the mother's full name;
* witnesses or sponsors;
* whether the child was described as lawful or natural;
* marginal notes.

=== Marriage Search ===

A marriage or proclamation record should be sought for John Glasgow and Barbara Alason before July 1679.

Relevant parishes include:

* Kilwinning;
* Irvine;
* Stevenston;
* Kilbirnie;
* Dalry;
* Beith;
* Ardrossan;
* other nearby Ayrshire parishes.

Searches should include variants such as:

* John Glasgow;
* Johne Glasgow;
* Jon Glasgow;
* John Glasgo;
* Barbara Alason;
* Barbara Allason;
* Barbara Alison;
* Barbara Allison.

=== Kirk Session Records ===

Kilwinning kirk-session records may contain references to John Glasgow or Barbara Alason.

These records may be useful if:

* the couple married irregularly;
* a child was born outside a formally recorded marriage;
* the family received parish assistance;
* either parent was disciplined by the kirk session;
* the family moved into or out of the parish.

=== Other Records to Search ===

Potentially useful sources include:

* testaments and inventories;
* sasines;
* land and tenancy records;
* tax rolls;
* hearth-tax records;
* poll-tax records;
* communion rolls;
* kirk-session minutes;
* burial registers;
* mortcloth accounts.

Records involving Archbald Glasgow, Agnes Watsone, Thomas Glasgow, Hellin Bryse, Margaret Sluman, James Glasgow, Agnes Duncan or the elder Johne Glasgow should be checked for later appearances in Ayrshire.

== Identity and duplicate assessment ==
This Kilwinning John is a serious same-person candidate for [[Glasgow-1073|Rev. John Glasgow M.A.]]: the name and estimated generation agree, Kilwinning and Kilbirnie are neighbouring Ayrshire parishes, and the last indexed Barbara-family event in February 1689 preceded the minister's January 1690 marriage to Jean Cunningham. The chronology permits the identification but does not prove it.

Neither ''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'' nor Paterson's county history mentions Barbara Alason, and the available index extracts do not give this John a title, occupation or residence that would identify him as the minister.<ref>''Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae'', vol. 3, p. 103, [https://electricscotland.com/bible/fastiecclesiaesc03scot.pdf PDF]; James Paterson, ''History of the County of Ayr'', pp. 252-253, [https://archive.org/details/historyofcountyo02pateuoft/page/252/mode/2up scan].</ref> Glasgow-3375 and Glasgow-1073 must therefore remain separate unless the full Kilwinning OPR pages or another identifying record supplies a bridge.

The attached father [[Glasgow-1604|John Glasgow]] and the links to [[Glasgow-1434|John Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1433|Jannet Glasgow]] are retained as uncertain. [[Glasgow-3288|William Glasgow]] should not be moved between adult family groups without direct evidence.

46569783.Name: Glasgow-3539
46569783.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}
== Biography ==
'''Mary Glasgow''' was the wife of [[Montgomerie-601|James Montgomerie]], who
was described as a sailor in Saltcoats in the parish of Ardrossan. The printed
index to the Glasgow Commissary testament registers lists Mary in that capacity
under 24 October 1677.<ref name="Mary1677">Francis J. Grant, ed.,
[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/page/196/mode/2up?q=Glasgow%2C
''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800'']
(Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1901), p. 196: “Mary, spouse to James
Montgomerie, sailor in Saltcoats, par. of Ardrossan,” 24 October 1677.</ref>

The index directly supports Mary's marriage to James and identifies his
occupation and place. The date is the testament-register entry date; the index
does not state Mary's exact date of death.<ref name="Mary1677" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Birth and parentage ===

Mary's existing birth year of about 1613 is an estimate for which no supporting
record has yet been identified. Saltcoats is relevant because the 1677 index
describes her husband there, but it does not expressly state that Mary was born
there. The populated date and location should be retained as uncertain while
better evidence is sought.

[[Glasgow-1557|Edward Glasgow]] and [[Hamilton-31734|Catherine Hamilton]] are
attached as Mary's parents. The 1677 index does not name either parent, and no
inspected source presently proves those relationships. The links should remain
uncertain unless a record establishes specific replacement parents; they
should not simply be removed and left blank.

=== Distinct 1637 household ===

The testament dative and inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, is a
different record. It names Isobell Gray as John's widow and Katherine and
Agnes Glasgow as his lawful children. It does not name Mary or Marie and gives
no basis for attaching this profile to that household.<ref>National Records of
Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, testament dative and inventory of John
Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats, NRS CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480; death in
December 1636 and court proceedings in April 1637; original register re-read
September 2026; locate by reference through the
[https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills
Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The full 1677 testament should be inspected before inferring Mary's age,
parentage, children, property or exact death date from the short printed index.

46690455.Name: Glasgow-3556
46690455.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
The date and place of birth of '''Thomas Glasgow''' are unknown. Because he was recorded as an adult in January 1684 and styled an esquire by 1689, he was probably born before about 1671. Lifford may be retained in the structured birth-place field as uncertain because it is his earliest stated locality, but the record does not prove that he was born there. No inspected record identifies his wife, children or parents.

On 22 January 1684 Thomas Glasgow was indexed as defendant in an Exchequer proceeding brought by a Bryson or Brison described as “of Raphoe.”<ref name="Exch1684">National Archives of Ireland, Equity Exchequer Bill Book 1684–1686, vol. 5, p. 102, 22 January 1684; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F007635147%2F00191&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001584141 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001584141&tab=this transcript].</ref>

In 1689 a printed list associated with the Irish attainder legislation named “Thomas Glasgow of Lifford, in the County of Donnegal, Esq.” among Protestants regarded as absent from Ireland or adherents of William of Orange.<ref name="King">''The State of the Protestants of Ireland under the Late King James's Government'', list of persons named in the attainder legislation, [https://quod.lib.umich.edu/e/eebo/a47446.0001.001/1%3A6 p. 275].</ref> This establishes his Lifford association and designation, not his birthplace or ownership of every property later named.

On 2 March 1692 Thomas was a defendant in a Chancery proceeding in which Abraham Creighton was a plaintiff or petitioner.<ref name="Chan1692">National Archives of Ireland, Court of Chancery Bill Book 1692–1696, vol. 11, p. 36, 2 March 1692; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F007635177%2F00507&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F0000106395 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FCHANCERY%2F0000106395&tab=this transcript].</ref>

On 23 December 1692 Thomas entered into a counterpart deed of partition with Colonel Abraham Creighton of Crom, County Fermanagh, and Abraham's son James Creighton concerning Donegal lands.<ref name="Partition1692">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/8/1, counterpart deed of partition, 23 December 1692.</ref>

On 25–26 May 1693 Thomas was described as “of Ballindroight” in a lease and release with Colonel Abraham Creighton concerning lands including Drumloane, Glencosh and Shannon in the Barony of Raphoe.<ref name="Lease1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/1/3, lease and release between Thomas Glasgow, or Glascow, of Ballindroight and Colonel Abraham Creighton, 25–26 May 1693.</ref>

On 26 May 1693 Thomas executed a performance bond and deed of defeasance for £4,000 in favour of Abraham Creighton.<ref name="Bond1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/3/25, bond and deed of defeasance, 26 May 1693.</ref> A counterpart release that day, for £400, concerned lands including Teroneal, Drumlane, Glancosh and Shannon in the Barony of Raphoe.<ref name="Release1693">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/7/1, counterpart release, 26 May 1693.</ref>

On 26 May 1694 Thomas was described as “of Shannon” when he issued a copy bond for performance of covenants in a release to Abraham Creighton.<ref name="Bond1694">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/11/16, copy bond for performance of covenant, 26 May 1694.</ref>

On 25 November 1695 Thomas appeared in a letter and memorandum concerning a joint bond of £6,000 with Hugh Hamill, Abraham Creighton, John Hamilton and John Johnston, all described as esquires.<ref name="Memo1695">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, D1939/18/3/25, letter and memorandum, 25 November 1695.</ref>

On 15 May 1701 Thomas Glasgow, Esquire, was indexed as plaintiff in an Exchequer bill against John Moffett, William Humphrys, Archibald Sinclair and Margaret Sinclair.<ref name="Exch1701">National Archives of Ireland, Equity Exchequer Bill Book 1700–1701, vol. 12, p. 121, 15 May 1701; [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F007635145%2F00152&parentid=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001527519 image] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=IRE%2FCOURT%2FEXCHEQUER%2F0001527519&tab=this transcript]. The page includes June 1701 procedural annotations.</ref>

The rare surname, Esquire designation, exact Raphoe reference and repeated Abraham Creighton association strongly identify the court litigant with the man of Lifford, Ballindroight and Shannon. Thomas was alive after 15 May 1701. His death date and place remain unknown.

{| class="wikitable" style="padding:5px; width:100%;"
|+ '''Evidence summary'''
|-
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Point
! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Assessment
|-
| Same Thomas in the 1684–1701 court and deed sequence
| High confidence from rare name, Esquire title, Raphoe locality and Abraham Creighton association
|-
| Birth before about 1671; death after 15 May 1701
| Uncertain bounds inferred from adult status and the latest dated proceeding
|-
| Relationship to Archibald, Nathaniel or George
| Unproved; retain existing links only as uncertain
|}

== Identity and Status ==

The references to Thomas Glasgow of '''Lifford''', '''Ballindroight''' and '''Shannon''' almost certainly concern the same man.

The surname was uncommon, the locations were within the same Donegal and Raphoe property network, and the records form a continuous sequence of transactions involving Abraham and James Creighton between 1692 and 1695.

No inspected record explicitly states that the Thomas of Lifford was the same person as the Thomas of Ballindroight or Shannon. The identification is nevertheless strongly supported by the chronology, geography and repeated association with the Creightons.

Thomas was styled '''esquire''' and participated in substantial legal and financial transactions. The bonds, considerations and lands involved show that he was a significant actor in the Donegal property network.

The surviving catalogue descriptions do not establish his precise role in every transaction. Depending upon the instrument, he may have acted as:

* owner;
* purchaser;
* vendor;
* mortgagee;
* trustee;
* tenant;
* surety; or
* another party with a legal interest.

He should therefore be described as an esquire and legal or property actor. The records do not by themselves prove that he beneficially owned every estate or parcel named.

== Family and Relationship Research ==

The available records name Thomas Glasgow, Abraham Creighton, James Creighton and several other parties to the transactions.

They do not identify Thomas’s:

* father or mother;
* wife;
* sons or daughters;
* brothers or sisters;
* heirs;
* executors; or
* other stated relatives.

No family relationship between Thomas and the Creightons is given. Their repeated appearance together establishes a continuing legal and financial association, not kinship.

No inspected record proves that Thomas was a son, brother, nephew or other relative of [[Glasgow-1101|Archibald Glasgow M.A. (1614–bef.1677)]].

The chronology and geography allow Thomas to have been a son or younger relative of the Archibald Glasgow who served as a clergyman in County Donegal and whose will was proved in 1677. That remains a research hypothesis only.

No inspected record proves that Thomas was the father of [[Glasgow-1136|Nathaniel Glasgow M.A. (died 1743)]].

The proposed line:

Archibald Glasgow
|
?
|
Thomas Glasgow of Lifford, Ballindroight and Shannon
|
?
|
Nathaniel Glasgow

remains unsupported by direct kinship evidence. Each question mark represents a missing documentary link.

A '''James Glasgow''' appearing in Killybegs account material in 1728 may belong to an adjacent generation of the Donegal family. The entry does not identify James as Thomas’s son or other relative.

No spouse or child should be attached to Thomas from chronology, geography, naming patterns or unsourced family trees alone.

== Distinction from Other Men Named Thomas Glasgow ==

Thomas should not be identified with [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow]], the child baptised in Scotland in 1612, without evidence connecting that person to Lifford or County Donegal.

A man baptised in 1612 would have been approximately 77 years old in 1689 and over 80 during the property transactions of 1692–1695. That identity is chronologically possible but unlikely and is unsupported by any inspected cross-channel record.

The two profiles should remain separate unless a deed, will, migration record or other contemporary source establishes that they were the same person.

== Death ==

Thomas’s date and place of death are unknown.

He was alive on '''25 November 1695''', when he was named in the memorandum concerning the £6,000 joint bond.

No will, administration, burial entry or record naming his heirs has yet been identified.

His profile should therefore use:

* birth probably before 1671, based on adult status by 1689, with birthplace unknown; and
* death after 25 November 1695, place unknown.

The year 1670 and County Donegal should not be presented as a certain birth date and place without an independent source.

== Locations Associated ==

* '''Lifford, County Donegal''' — Thomas’s stated residence or association in the 1689 attainder list.
* '''Ballindroight, Barony of Raphoe, County Donegal''' — his stated residence in the May 1693 lease and release.
* '''Shannon, Barony of Raphoe, County Donegal''' — his stated residence in the May 1694 bond.
* '''Drumloane, Glencosh, Glancosh, Teroneal and Drumlane''' — lands named in the Creighton transactions.
* '''Crom, County Fermanagh''' — residence of Colonel Abraham Creighton, Thomas’s principal associate in the surviving deeds.

The place-name Ballindroight may represent Ballindrait or another historical spelling. The original deeds and contemporary maps should be consulted before standardising the location.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current evidence assessment ===

The complete deeds and court bills may contain witnesses, signatures, property recitals or family language omitted from the indexes and catalogue descriptions. They remain the best sources for testing Thomas's family and tracing his estate after 1701.

The PRONI catalogue summaries may omit details contained in the original documents. Full copies could include:

* witnesses;
* seals and signatures;
* endorsements;
* former owners;
* inheritance recitals;
* adjoining tenants;
* trusts;
* marriage settlements;
* occupations;
* residences; or
* statements of family relationships.

The complete documents should therefore be inspected before concluding that they contain no genealogical evidence.

Particular attention should be given to phrases such as:

* “son and heir”;
* “natural and lawful son”;
* “brother”;
* “kinsman”;
* “heirs of the body”;
* “in consideration of marriage”;
* “for the advancement of”; and
* “remainder to”.

Further research should concentrate on:

* complete copies of PRONI D1939/18/8/1, D1939/18/1/3, D1939/18/3/25, D1939/18/7/1 and D1939/18/11/16;
* indexes to Irish prerogative and Raphoe diocesan wills and administrations;
* Betham will and administration abstracts;
* Donegal deeds involving the Creighton estate;
* Registry of Deeds memorials created after 1708;
* Raphoe parish and diocesan records;
* Lifford corporation and court records;
* Donegal Grand Jury records;
* records concerning the 1728 Killybegs James Glasgow; and
* later conveyances showing who inherited or occupied the lands after Thomas disappeared from the record.

== Research Conclusion ==

Thomas Glasgow was a genuine adult Donegal figure documented at Lifford in 1689 and in the Ballindroight and Shannon property network from 1692 to 1695.

He was styled an esquire and participated in substantial legal and financial transactions with Abraham and James Creighton. The documents do not establish that he owned every property named.

His birth date and place are unknown. His adult status in 1689 supports a probable birth before 1671, and the records show that he was alive after 25 November 1695.

No inspected record identifies his wife, children, parents, heirs or siblings. No relationship to Archibald Glasgow of Ramelton, Nathaniel Glasgow of Golan or Fintona, the later Killybegs James Glasgow, or the Scottish Thomas baptised in 1612 has been proved.

== Biography ==
William Glasgow's birth before 1690 at Cavers is an estimate retained in the structured fields as uncertain. The identified marriage record does not state his age, birthplace or parents.

William “Glasgon” married [[Scott-69166|Margaret Scott]] at Hummelknows on 4 March 1708/09.<ref>FreeREG transcription, Cavers marriage register, William Glasgon and Margaret Scott, 4 March 1708/09, “Married in Hummelknows”; see also “Scotland, Marriages, 1561-1910,” FamilySearch database, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQG-3XD record XYQG-3XD].</ref> The structured date is entered as 4 March 1709, with Hummelknows retained together with the Cavers parish context.

== Research Notes ==
The attached [[Glasgow-1605|William Glasgow]] is retained only as an uncertain father. The marriage record names no parents.

[[Glasgow-4138|William Glasgow]], a Cavers/Ormistoun servant documented in 1679–84, is a possible earlier identity for this 1708/09 groom. The earlier records and this marriage are compatible in locality and chronology, but neither identifies the groom by age, occupation or relative; they do not yet prove one man. The attached Glasgow-1605 father is a separate, unproved Polwarth baptism hypothesis.<ref>Findmypast, Scottish Covenanters 1679–1688, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028558&tab=this 1679 Cavers deposition] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPR%2FCOVENANT%2F028560&tab=this 1684 Ormistoun servant list].</ref>

An Isabel Glasgon, daughter of a William and of Humble Knows, was baptised on 27 August 1710.<ref>FreeREG transcription, baptism of Isabel Glasgon, 27 August 1710, father William, abode Humble Knows; mother not named.</ref> She is a strong candidate child of William and Margaret because of the name, date and place, but the record does not name her mother. She should not be attached as their proved child without corroboration.

47207788.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

Margaret Glasgow married William Hardie, a cordiner, at Edinburgh on 16 July 1611.<ref>“Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910,” FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYMK-1QM : accessed 11 February 2020), William Hardie and Margaret Glasgow, 1611.</ref><ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700'', p. 267, [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 16 July 1611], naming William as a cordiner.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

No reviewed record identifies Margaret's parents or birthplace. Her structured birth before 1595 is only an uncertain adult-status estimate from the 1611 marriage.

The same published-register page records Barbara Glasgow marrying cordiner George Johnstoun in 1616 and Isobel Glasgow marrying tailor William Symountoun in 1619. This craft-marriage cluster is a useful kinship lead, not proof that the women were sisters.

=== William Hardie's identity ===
The Edinburgh marriage register lists a William Hardie, cordiner, with Eupham Wauchope on 1 September 1608, Margaret Glasgow on 16 July 1611, Catharine Leslie on 27 August 1641 and Catharine Angus on 17 November 1643.<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=317 printed p. 307], entries under Hardie (Hardy).</ref> The repeated name and trade make these entries useful for tracing Margaret's husband, but they do not establish that all four marriages involved one man. The later entries could concern a younger namesake. Original parish and cordiner records are needed before inferring Margaret's death or additional relatives.

=== Possible family placement ===
Margaret is best placed as a possible daughter or niece of [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]. Her husband William Hardie was a cordiner.<ref>Henry Paton, ed., ''The Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595-1700'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 printed p. 267], 16 July 1611.</ref> Ninian's proved son Robert was also a cordiner, while his probable son [[Glasgow-3075|William]] moved into Leith and William's son was apprenticed to a cordiner.

This direct craft and Edinburgh-Leith pattern makes Ninian's household or immediate collateral circle the leading branch, but the marriage register names no parent. The possible daughter-or-niece relationship remains uncertain.

The structured 'before 1629' date is an uncertain adulthood estimate based on children baptised from 1646; it is not a baptism or proved birth date. The former exact 18 February 1626 date and attachment as a son of [[Glasgow-1087|William Glasgow]], christened in 1609, had no cited record and were removed on 26 September 2026. ** Marriages for a '''John/Johne Glasgow''' in Kirknewton and East Calder in the two decades before 1649.  
** Additional baptisms to a father named '''Johne/John Glasgow''' in the same parish, 1635–1665, to identify siblings.  
** Testaments and sasines in Midlothian that mention a John/Johne Glasgow of Kirknewton or East Calder.

47271170.Name: Glasgow-3613
47271170.bio:
== Biography ==

⚠️ '''Palaeographic Note'''

This profile uses only information supported by the manuscript images or by the supplied testament index. Original spelling and physical lineation are retained in the diplomatic transcription.

* Expanded abbreviations appear in ⟨angle brackets⟩.
* Doubtful or index-supplied readings appear in [square brackets].
* [....] marks wording that has not been read securely.
* No names, sums or clauses have been silently reconstructed from standard legal formulae.

=== Deceased ===

'''Margaret Glasgow''' was described in the supplied testament index as sometime spouse to '''John Edstoun in Croftmalloch'''.<ref>''Scotland, Will and Testament Index 1481–1807'', Margaret Glasgow, 1580; supplied index entry describing her as “sometime spouse to John Edstoun, in Croftmalloch”.</ref>

Her testament dative states that she died intestate in the month of '''November 1578'''. The manuscript gives no birth date, age or place of birth.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/8, image 355, testament dative and inventory of Margaret Glasgow.</ref>

=== Executor-Dative and Court Action ===

The testament and inventory were given up by a man named '''[[Edstoun-4|Cuthbert]]'''. The manuscript describes him as Margaret’s '''son''' and as executor-dative. The existing profile label Edstoun-4 is retained for continuity, but the manuscript does not securely establish his surname.

Wording following Cuthbert’s forename is not sufficiently clear to establish a surname. It should therefore not be assumed that he was Cuthbert Edstoun, Cuthbert Glasgow, Cuthbert Calder, Cuthbert Wrycht, or any other similarly named person without separate evidence.

Cuthbert was surrogated in place of the Procurator Fiscal by decree of the Commissaries of Edinburgh. The decree is dated '''17 October 1580'''.

A marginal annotation beside the entry reads:

:''margaret glasgw''
:''ultimo nouember 1580''

The second annotation means “the last day of November 1580”. It is a court or register annotation and is not Margaret’s date of death.

=== Inventory and Estate Accounting ===

The manuscript contains an inventory followed by the usual estate-accounting sections. The following headings or accounting descriptions are securely identifiable:

* ''Summa of the inventar'' — total of the inventory.
* ''Dettis awand to the deid'' — debts owed to Margaret.
* ''Summa of the dettis awand to the deid'' — total debts owed to Margaret.
* ''Dettis awand be the deid'' — debts owed by Margaret.
* ''Summa of the dettis awand be the deid'' — total debts owed by Margaret.
* ''Restis of frie geir the dettis deducit'' — free estate remaining after deduction of debts.
* A following division and quota calculation.

The individual inventory articles, debtor and creditor names, and right-margin monetary figures are not sufficiently secure in this copy to publish as facts. They have therefore not been included.

=== Diplomatic Transcription ===

''Image 355: opening block''

:1  The testament dative & inventar of the guidis geir sowmes
:2  of money & dettis pertening to vmq⟨uhi⟩le Margaret glasgw
:3  spous to Johne [Edstoun] in [Croftmalloch] the
:4  tyme of hir deceis quha deceist ab intestat in the
:5  moneth of nouember the zeir of god Jaj vc lxxviij zeiris
:6  faithfullie maid & gevin vp be Cuthbert [....] in
:7  [Croftmalloch] hir sone ex⟨ecutou⟩r dative surrogat & in
:8  place of the procuratour fiscall be decreit of the
:9  commissaris of Edinburgh as the samyn decreit of the dait the
:10 xvij day of october the zeir of god Jaj vc fourscoir zeiris
:11 at lenth proportis

''Beginning of the inventory''

:i1 In the first the said vmq⟨uhi⟩le woman had the guidis geir
:i2 sowmes of money & dettis of the availlis & pryces [....]
:i3 pertening to hir the tyme of hir deceis foirsaid viz [....]

''Image 356: securely identifiable accounting headings''

:a1 Summa of the inventar — [sum not securely read]
:a2 Dettis awand to the deid
:a3 Summa of the dettis awand to the deid — [sum not securely read]
:a4 Dettis awand be the deid
:a5 Summa of the dettis awand be the deid — [sum not securely read]
:a6 Restis of frie geir the dettis deducit — [sum not securely read]
:a7 [division and quota calculation not securely transcribed]

=== Modern Rendering ===

This is the court-appointed testament and inventory of the late Margaret Glasgow, spouse of John Edstoun in Croftmalloch.

Margaret died without leaving a will in November 1578. Her son Cuthbert presented the inventory and was made executor-dative in place of the Procurator Fiscal under a decree of the Commissaries of Edinburgh dated 17 October 1580.

The remainder of the record accounts for Margaret’s property, money and debts. It distinguishes between money owed to her and money owed by her, then calculates the free estate remaining after the debts were deducted.

The manuscript has a marginal annotation dated the last day of November 1580. This is later court or registration information, not the date of Margaret’s death.

== Research Notes ==

* Margaret’s entry begins in the lower portion of manuscript image 355 and continues on image 356. Text belonging to the preceding entries must not be incorporated into her profile.
* The supplied index has a separate date field of '''8 November 1580'''. This has not been treated as Margaret’s death date. The manuscript itself gives:
** November 1578 — Margaret’s death.
** 17 October 1580 — date of the decree appointing or surrogating the executor-dative.
** ''ultimo November 1580'' — marginal court or register annotation.
* The records-site wording supplied by the researcher is '''John Edstoun in Croftmalloch'''. The former readings “Johne Eastoun”, “Crost Mylnis” and “Cross Mills, Glasgow” are not retained.
* No birth year can be derived from this testament.
* The earlier proposed readings “Cuthbert wrycht”, “Johne Browne”, “1583”, “funeral expenses”, “kirk and bell”, and “to the poor” have not been retained. They are not sufficiently supported by these images.
* Cuthbert’s surname remains unresolved. The manuscript contains writing after his forename, but it has not been read securely enough to identify him further.
* [[Edstoun-4|Cuthbert]] is attached to Margaret as his confirmed mother because the testament directly calls him her son. [[Edstoun-3|John Edstoun]] is Margaret's record-proved husband and a natural father candidate, but the clause does not identify him as Cuthbert's father; that father relationship is retained as uncertain pending another record.

== Sources ==

* National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, '''CC8/8/8''', images '''355–356''', testament dative and inventory of Margaret Glasgow.
* ''Scotland, Will and Testament Index 1481–1807'', Margaret Glasgow, 1580; supplied index entry: “sometime spouse to John Edstoun, in Croftmalloch”.

50923069.Name: Glasgow-3908
50923069.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

Matthew Glasgow was born before 1542, probably in Scotland. The year is an estimate based on his being at least 18 years old when he appeared as a tenant in a record dated 1559–60.

In the Cunninghame teind lists of 1559–60, Matthew Glasgow and John Mathie were listed under Ardeer Nether in the parish of Stevenston, Ayrshire.<ref>Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', ''Ayrshire Collections'', vol. 14, no. 8 (Ayrshire Archaeological and Natural History Society, 1987), appendix "The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559–60," [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331], Ardeer Nether entry. Sanderson identifies the underlying record as Scottish Record Office, Register of Acts and Decreets, vol. 22, fols. 102v–167v.</ref> Sanderson explains that those named were tenants responsible for crop teinds and that the list does not necessarily identify the holding on which a family lived.

=== Research Notes ===

* Birth: before 1542, Scotland, uncertain.
* Death: after 1558, place unknown, uncertain.

No reviewed source identifies Matthew's parents, spouse, children, precise birthplace, residence, or death. Ardeer Nether should therefore not be entered as his birth or death place.

=== Wider Mathie–Glencairn connection ===

The Ardeer pairing belongs to a wider documented association. On 10 May 1554 David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were named together among the Glasgow burgesses witnessing the same sasines.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref> David had a recorded son John. A John Mathie was admitted as a burgess with James, Earl of Glencairn, James Cunningham and the earl’s servant William Cochrane in 1583.<ref name="MathieGlencairn">James R. Anderson, ed., Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750 (Scottish Record Society, 1925), [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf entry for 8 February 1582/83].</ref>

Tutory retours entered on 20 January 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother as Matthew Mathie, burgess of Glasgow, and name John’s lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref> Ibert lay in Kilmaronock within the Glencairn estate network. This gives the Mathie household a direct link back to Glasgow burgh society, although it does not identify [[Glasgow-3908|Matthew Glasgow]] as a relative.

[[Mathie-159|Jonet Mathie]] married [[Glasgow-1030|John Glasgow]] in Glasgow on 25 January 1618.<ref name="Mathie1618">FamilySearch, “Scotland Marriages, 1561–1910,” John Glasgow and Jonet Mathie, 25 January 1618, Glasgow, Lanark, Scotland; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYWK-WM3 permanent record].</ref> Her marriage may continue this association between the families.

This Matthew is not [[Glasgow-3538|Matthew Glasgow]], who was named at Pyperheugh in the same parish in 1665. No evidence currently establishes a relationship between the two men.

=== Possible family placement ===
[[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow elder of Corsankell]] is Matthew's leading possible father or uncle. Matthew at Ardeer Nether and James elder at Corsankell were separately named as tenant or householder figures in the same 1559-60 Stevenston teind list.<ref>Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', appendix “The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559-60,” [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331].</ref> A 1571 writ expressly names James elder's sons James and John, but does not purport to list every child.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Charter Chest of the Earls of Glencairn, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F5%2F59 GD39/5/59], 9 February 1571.</ref>

The locality and generation make Matthew a possible son, nephew or younger collateral, but no record states the relationship. James is therefore attached only as an uncertain working father. [[Glasgow-3911|Michael Glasgow]] is a distinct man and is better treated as an older collateral in the same estate network.

== Sources ==
<references />

Helen was born in 1609.  She passed away before 1627.

== Biography ==

'''Helen Glasgow''' was the spouse of Peter Broun of Thankerton, Lanarkshire. Her testament was recorded in the Lanark Commissary Court on 8 January 1627.<ref name="LanarkIndex">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''The Commissariot Record of Lanark: Register of Testaments, 1595–1800'' (Edinburgh: Scottish Record Society, 1903), printed p. 38, entry “Glasgow, Helen, spouse to Peter Broun, in Thankertoun,” [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=50 digital copy].</ref> She had died by that date.


=== Research Notes ===

Suggested creation data:
* Birth: before 1609, Scotland, uncertain.
* Death: before 8 January 1627, place unknown.
* Spouse: Peter Broun; create or attach him only after a duplicate search.
* Parents and children: unknown; leave unconnected.

The wording associates Peter Broun with Thankerton; it does not state that Helen was born or died there.

The `glasgow-one-tree.xlsx` snapshot and live WikiTree searches found no matching early Helen Glasgow of Thankerton. The Helen Glasgow profiles found in the snapshot were born in the 1650s and are too late to be this decedent.

== Biography ==

'''James Glasgow''' was a weaver at Quothquan (written “Quodquen”) in the parish of Libberton, Lanarkshire. His testament was recorded in the Lanark Commissary Court on 26 July 1624.<ref name="LanarkIndex">Francis J. The same index refers to Margaret Threipland, widow of a James Glesgow at Quothquan, whose testament was recorded on 27 October 1626.<ref name="ThreiplandIndex">Grant, ''Commissariot Record of Lanark'', printed p. 99, entry “Threipland, Margaret, relict of James Glesgow, in Quodquen,” [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/the_commissariot_record_of_lanark__register_of_testaments__1595-1800_~_1903.pdf#page=111 digital copy].</ref> She may have been this James's widow, but the index does not uniquely identify the two same-name Quothquan references as one man.

50926830.Name: Glasgow-3911
50926830.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}
== Biography ==

Michael Glasgow was probably born about 1525, perhaps in Ayrshire. The date and place are uncertain estimates based on his documented appearance as a witness at Stevenston in 1549.

On 28 January 1549 Michael Glasgow witnessed an instrument of sasine in favour of Janet Cunningham, daughter of John Cunningham of Caprington, and the heirs to be born between her and her husband Alexander, Earl of Glencairn, in the lands and barony of Stevenston and other lands. William Cunningham of Legland and Adam Mure were among the other witnesses.<ref name="NRS1549">National Records of Scotland, Charter Chest of the Earls of Glencairn, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F1%2F59 GD39/1/59], instrument of sasine in favour of Janet Cunningham and Alexander, Earl of Glencairn, 28 January 1549. The official catalogue entry was inspected; no manuscript image is available online.</ref>

In the Cunninghame teind lists of 1559–60, Michael Glasgow was listed with John Sparling, John Wilson, and Robert Wilson under Brakpleuch Over and Nether in the parish of Stevenston, Ayrshire.<ref name="Teinds1559">Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', ''Ayrshire Collections'', vol. 14, no. 8 (Ayrshire Archaeological and Natural History Society, 1987), appendix "The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559–60," [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331], Brakpleuch Over and Nether entry. Sanderson identifies the underlying record as Scottish Record Office, Register of Acts and Decreets, vol. 22, fols. 102v–167v.</ref>

The uncommon name and the repeated Stevenston/Glencairn estate setting make it probable that the witness of 1549 and the tenant of 1559–60 were the same man. The records do not supply an occupation, patronymic, or exact property chain, so this identification remains an evidence-based inference.

=== Mathie–Glencairn network ===

The Stevenston records show a broader association rather than an isolated cluster. The 1559–60 list also names John, Margaret and William Mathie, [[Glasgow-3908|Matthew Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow elder]] with his son [[Glasgow-3921|James]], across neighbouring holdings.<ref name="Teinds1559"/> In Glasgow, David Mathy and [[Glasgow-1096|Robert Glasgow]] were fellow burgesses witnessing the same sasines in 1554.<ref name="Mathie1554">Robert Renwick, ed., Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow, vol. 1, protocols 183–184, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc07robegoog/page/n90/mode/2up 10 May 1554, printed p. 63].</ref>

David’s son John is a plausible match for a later writer in the Earl of Glencairn’s circle. Tutory retours entered in 1607 identify the deceased John Mathie of Ibert’s full brother Matthew as a Glasgow burgess and name John’s lawful children James, David, Agnes and Margaret.<ref name="Ibert1607">Inquisitionum ad Capellam Domini Regis Retornatarum ... Abbreviatio, vol. 2, tutory retours 100–101, 20 January 1607, [https://books.google.com/books?id=PiVDAAAAcAAJ digitised volume]; underlying register, National Records of Scotland, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browsetreeview.aspx?reference=C22 C22/3].</ref> This gives Michael’s estate circle a documented route into Glasgow burgh society, although it does not state how the Glasgow tenants were related.

=== Research Notes ===

The same teind-list page also names a Michael Glasgow with Finlay Brown and James Morton under Dubbs.<ref name="Teinds1559"/> Sanderson warns that one tenant could hold more than one property. The Brakpleuch and Dubbs entries may therefore describe one Michael Glasgow or two contemporaries.

No reviewed source identifies Michael's parents, spouse, children, precise birthplace, or death. [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-3908|Matthew Glasgow]], and the other Glasgow surname bearers in the 1559 Stevenston rental form a local record cluster, but co-tenancy and locality do not prove kinship. No parent has therefore been attached.

This Michael is not [[Glasgow-1406|Michael Glasgow]], whose estimated birth was more than a century later.

=== Possible family placement ===
Michael is best placed as a probable brother or cousin, rather than a son, of [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow elder of Corsankell]]. Michael was already an adult legal witness in the Glencairn estate network on 28 January 1549,<ref>National Records of Scotland, Charter Chest of the Earls of Glencairn, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD39%2F1%2F59 GD39/1/59], 28 January 1549.</ref> and both men were present in the Stevenston-area tenancy landscape in 1559-60.<ref>Margaret H. B. Sanderson, ''The People of Sixteenth Century Ayrshire'', appendix “The Cunninghame Teind Lists of 1559-60,” [https://aanhs.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/people-of-ayrshire.pdf#page=36 p. 331].</ref>

The generation and repeated microregion support close collateral kinship, but no source identifies either man's father or the exact degree. No structured father should be inferred from this cluster.

== Sources ==
<references />

50931016.Name: Glasgow-3913
50931016.bio:
{{Estimated Date}} {{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}} == Biography == '''John Glasgow''', recorded as '''Jo Glascho''', was a taxed householder at Kilwaughter Demesne in Kilwaughter parish, upper Glenarm barony, County Antrim, in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll, T/307/A; W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf transcription], records 5347–5348, PDF p. 36. He is probably the same man who appears repeatedly in the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregational records about 1699–1700/1 as '''John Glasgow, senior''', representing Kilwaughter. If this identification is correct, his documented career extended for more than thirty years. The designation ''senior'' is genealogically significant: it strongly suggests that another, younger John Glasgow was then known within the local community. That younger man's identity and relationship remain unknown. === Kilwaughter in 1669 === The 1669 Hearth Money Roll records: :'''Jo. Glascho''' :'''James Glascho''' as immediately consecutive householders at Kilwaughter Demesne. The abbreviation ''Jo.'' most probably represents John. The exact co-location and uncommon surname make a close relationship between John and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] probable, although the tax roll gives no ages, household members or relationship. === John Glasgow senior, c. 1699–1700 === Classon Porter later published substantial extracts from an early record of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation. Porter stated that he had been unable to locate the original in his day and was working from a transcript made or procured for Rev. D. Davison, portions of which had already been published in 1826. Porter arranged his quotations by subject rather than strict chronology.Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 2 (1863–1864), pp. 410–415; [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0002unse Internet Archive]. Porter describes the provenance of the transcript on p. 410. On 3 March 1699/1700 the congregational record appointed four men to approach the Presbytery concerning Rev. William Ogilvie. One was:
"John Glasgow, sen."
Porter immediately reproduced the Presbytery's minute for the same deputation. It names the same four men — Samuel Smealley, William Hare, John Glasgow and James Callwell — but calls him simply '''John Glasgow'''. This is useful identity evidence. ''Senior'' was a contextual qualifier; the same man could be recorded without it in another record of the same transaction. On 17 May, John again appears as:
"John Glasgow, sen., for Kilwochter"
He and Patrick Agnew bound for Kilwaughter's £8 share of the minister's stipend, together with obligations for firing, ploughing and harrowing. John was also among the heads of families entrusted with considering the rebuilding of the meeting house. These entries establish that he was a substantial member of the Kilwaughter congregation and a representative of its householders. They do not establish that he held the office of elder. The following year's material again records plain '''John Glasgow''' acting for Kilwaughter. On 27 February 1700 in the record's dating, John Glasgow and Robert White were chosen for Kilwaughter to inspect the minister's land. In the same meeting, Patrick Agnew and John Glasgow were selected for Kilwaughter to consider repairs to the minister's house.Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), pp. 15–18; [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive]. The date falls in the period conventionally written 1700/1 when double-dating pre-1752 records. The recurrence of: * the same uncommon name; * the same Kilwaughter locality; * John being explicitly styled ''senior''; * plain John being paired again with Patrick Agnew; * and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] also appearing in Kilwaughter affairs about 1700; makes it more probable that the congregational John was the '''same man''' as Jo Glascho, householder at Kilwaughter in 1669, rather than an undocumented son of that man. The identification remains inferential because no surviving entry explicitly says that the 1669 and c.1700 men were identical. === Family === [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] was recorded immediately beside John at Kilwaughter in 1669. About 1700 a James Glasgow was appointed overseer for Kilwaughter during work on the minister's house. The repeated John-and-James presence in the same small district strengthens the case that they belonged to one close family cluster. Their exact relationship remains unknown. John is currently placed as an uncertain son of [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]], the Robert ''Glaskow'' associated with Larne during the period of the 1641 rebellion.Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 153r, examination of Con O'Sheale, 21 April 1653, identifier 838153r210; Robert is described as "one Robert Glaskow liuing in Larne"; [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42821.html 1641 Depositions Project transcription]. That parentage remains a reconstruction from chronology, locality and surname continuity. No record names Robert as John's father. John's wife is unknown. == Research Notes == === The younger John implied by "senior" === The repeated designation '''John Glasgow, sen.''' strongly suggests that another, younger John Glasgow was known to the congregation by about 1700. The same group of congregational extracts uses other age qualifiers, including ''Robert Mea, jun.'' and ''John Kerr, sen.'', showing that such distinctions were actively used in the source. No located published extract explicitly names a '''John Glasgow junior''', however, and ''senior'' does not itself prove a father-son relationship. The younger namesake could have been: * John's son; * a nephew; * a cousin; * another younger member of the same Glasgow cluster. '''A son is a plausible hypothesis, but not yet a relationship suitable for attachment without further evidence.''' The important distinction is therefore: :'''Probable:''' Jo Glascho of Kilwaughter in 1669 = John Glasgow senior of Kilwaughter c.1700. :'''Possible:''' the younger John implied by ''senior'' was his son. :'''Unknown:''' the younger John's identity and later history. No reliable WikiTree profile has yet been identified for this younger namesake. === Could the c.1700 senior have been a son of the 1669 John? === It is chronologically possible but presently less likely. A male householder in 1669 could readily still have been active about 1700. Even if John had been only about twenty-one in 1669, he would have been about fifty-two by 1700 — entirely compatible with being the established ''senior'' John, a head of family and congregational bondsman. Making the c.1700 senior a son instead requires an additional same-name generation for which no record has yet been found. It would also require some other younger John to explain why that second-generation John was himself called ''senior''. The simpler reconstruction fits all presently located evidence without adding an undocumented generation. '''Current assessment: same person probable; father-son replacement possible but unsupported.''' === Parentage and Scottish hypothesis === The current uncertain father hypothesis should distinguish two separate questions. [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]] is the Robert ''Glaskow'' associated with Larne in the 1653 examination. He is a plausible earlier member of the Larne–Kilwaughter Glasgow family and is currently attached as John's uncertain father. A separate [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] was recorded in Glasgow, Scotland, in 1618. That Scottish Robert has been proposed as identical with the Larne Robert, but no documentary migration or identity bridge has been found. The two hypotheses should not be collapsed: * Robert of Larne → John of Kilwaughter: '''possible; unproved'''. * Scottish Robert → Robert of Larne: '''possible identity; unproved'''. John's mother remains unknown. === Record survival === Porter's nineteenth-century publication is derivative: he stated that the original early congregational record could not then be found and that he was using a transcript. There is now a more concrete archival route. Modern scholarship identifies surviving Larne and Kilwaughter session material for 1699–1701 and 1720–1769 and cites '''PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B'''.Robert Whan, ''The Presbyterians of Ulster, 1680–1730'' (Boydell Press, 2013), introduction and bibliography, identifying Larne and Kilwaughter session records for 1699–1701 and 1720–1769 and citing PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B; [https://resolve.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/C038A358FF15C0285190286F12E951A4/9781782041894bib_p202-230_CBO.pdf/bibliography.pdf Cambridge bibliography]. The early section should be inspected directly to determine its precise relationship to the transcript used by Porter and, more importantly, whether entries omitted from his topical extracts identify the younger John Glasgow. === Suggested structured data === * '''First name:''' John * '''Last name at birth:''' Glasgow * '''Recorded spelling:''' Glascho * '''Birth:''' before 1651, place unknown, uncertain * '''Death:''' after about 1700, place unknown, uncertain, if the 1669 and c.1700 records are accepted as the same man * '''Residence:''' Kilwaughter Demesne, County Antrim, 1669 * '''Later residence/association:''' Kilwaughter, c.1699–1700/1, probable same person * '''Father:''' [[Glasgow-3970|Robert Glasgow]], uncertain * '''Mother:''' unknown * '''Relationship to [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]]:''' probable close relative; exact relationship unknown * '''Spouse:''' unknown * '''Children:''' none proved * '''Possible child:''' an unidentified younger John Glasgow implied by the designation ''John Glasgow, sen.'' === Priority Research === * '''PRONI MIC1B/6A/1B — Larne and Kilwaughter session book, 1699–1701 and 1720–1769.''' ** Inspect the complete early section rather than Porter's selected extracts. ** Search every occurrence of Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascho, John, ''sen.'', ''jun.'', younger and elder. ** Concentrate on the entries surrounding 3 March 1699/1700, 17 May and 27 February 1700/1. ** Determine whether the implied younger John is named, and whether any relationship to John senior is stated. * '''Presbyterian Historical Society of Ireland — Antrim Presbytery minutes, 1697–1713.''' ** Inspect the original minute for the Larne deputation of 3 March 1699/1700 and subsequent Larne/Kilwaughter business. ** Porter quotes the Presbytery minute as naming plain "John Glasgow"; surrounding entries may contain a qualifier, residence or relationship omitted from the published extract. * '''PRONI D282 and NRS GD154/505–534 — Kilwaughter estate material, approximately 1665–1710.''' ** Search for John Glasgow, Jo Glascho and variants, explicitly watching for simultaneous senior and junior tenants. ** Trace any holding occupied by John from the 1669 hearth roll into the early eighteenth century. ** A lease, renewal or succession entry naming a son, heir, widow or former tenant could distinguish the same-man and father-son hypotheses. * '''PRONI T/808/14889 — 1666 County Antrim subsidy roll.''' ** Search John/Jo, James and Robert Glasgow under Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascho, Glaskow and Glascow. ** An earlier appearance of John in the same Kilwaughter tenancy cluster would further strengthen continuity into 1669 and c.1700. == Sources ==

50940874.Name: Glasgow-3915
50940874.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==

Elizabeth Glasgow was the widow of [[Kaine-91|Alexander Kaine]] by 19 December 1552. On that date a Great Seal confirmation described the lands of Easter Corswood in Edinburghshire as occupied by Elizabeth Glasgow, relict of Alexander Kaine.<ref name="RMS739">John Maitland Thomson, ed., ''Registrum Magni Sigilli Regum Scotorum'', vol. 4, A.D. 1546-1580 (Edinburgh, 1886), no. 739, [https://archive.org/details/registrummagnisi04scot/page/164/mode/1up p. 164], 19 December 1552: ''per Elesabeth Glasgow relictam Alesandri Kaine occupatas''.</ref>

Alexander is confidently identified with the Alexander Kano named immediately after [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] in a royal remission to Sir James Sandilands of Calder's group on 2 July 1526.<ref name="Remission1526">National Records of Scotland, Papers of Lord Torphichen, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseDetails.aspx?reference=GD119%2F193 GD119/193], remission, 2 July 1526. The official catalogue reads ''Alexander Kano''; ''Registrum Secreti Sigilli'', vol. 1, no. 3412, p. 516, prints ''Alexandri Kame''.</ref> James V dined with Sandilands at Calder that day, placing the remission in an immediate estate-household setting.<ref name="Treasurer1526">Thomas Dickson and James Balfour Paul, eds., [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/accountslordhig05offigoog.pdf ''Accounts of the Lord High Treasurer of Scotland'', vol. 5, A.D. 1515–1531], preface p. xxvii, citing account p. 275.</ref> The identification rests on the uncommon name and on Elizabeth's later occupation of Easter Corswood within the same Sandilands barony of Calder.<ref name="Corswood1625">National Records of Scotland, Papers of Lord Torphichen, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseTreeview.aspx?reference=GD119 GD119/299], 1 July 1625, describing Corswoodburne alias Easter Corswood in the barony of Calder.</ref>

=== Research Notes ===

=== Possible relationship to William Glasgow ===

William is presently attached as Elizabeth's father, but the relationship must remain uncertain. The 1526 association between William and her husband, followed by Elizabeth's 1552 occupation in their patron's Calder estate, strongly suggests close kinship. It does not distinguish daughter from sister, niece or another female relative. No source names Elizabeth's parent.

Elizabeth's birth is estimated about 1525 from her marriage and widowhood; no record gives her age. The 1552 act proves that she was alive on 19 December 1552, so her structured death should be recorded as after that date, not on it. Easter Corswood is a residence, not a proved birth or death place. No reviewed record identifies a child.

== Sources ==
<references />

Spouses.Name: Kaine-91
Spouses.bio:
== Biography ==

Alexander Kaine was an associate of Sir James Sandilands ofCalder. On 2 July 1526 Alexander Kano was named immediately after [[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] among the men receiving a royal remission for the premeditated killing of James Somervile and other past offences.<ref name="Remission1526">National Records of Scotland, Papers of Lord Torphichen, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseDetails.aspx?reference=GD119%2F193 GD119/193], remission sealed at Edinburgh, 2 July 1526. The official catalogue reads ''Alexander Kano''; ''Registrum Secreti Sigilli'', vol. 1, no. 3412, p. 516, prints ''Alexandri Kame''.</ref> James V dined with Sandilands at Calder that day, and the Calder household servants received gratuities, placing the remission in an immediate estate-household setting.<ref name="Treasurer1526">Thomas Dickson and James Balfour Paul, eds., [https://electricscotland.com/history/records/accountslordhig05offigoog.pdf ''Accounts of the Lord HighTreasurer of Scotland'', vol. 5, A.D. 1515–1531], preface p. xxvii, citing account p. 275.</ref>

He is confidently identified with Alexander Kaine, husband of [[Glasgow-3915|Elizabeth Glasgow]]. A Great Seal confirmation dated 19 December 1552 described Easter Corswood as occupied by ''Elesabeth Glasgow relictam Alesandri Kaine''—Elizabeth Glasgow, widow of Alexander Kaine.<ref name="RMS739">John Maitland Thomson, ed., ''Registrum Magni Sigilli Regum Scotorum'', vol. 4, A.D. 1546-1580 (Edinburgh, 1886), no. 739, [https://archive.org/details/registrummagnisi04scot/page/164/mode/1up p. 164], 19 December 1552.</ref> Easter Corswood belonged to the Sandilands barony of Calder, independently linking the 1526 Kano and 1552 Kaine records to the same estate.<ref name="Corswood1625">National Records of Scotland, Papers of Lord Torphichen, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseTreeview.aspx?reference=GD119 GD119/299], 1 July 1625, describing Corswoodburne alias Easter Corswood in the barony of Calder.</ref>

The record proves that Alexander died before 19 December 1552. His birth year and parents are unknown; about 1520 is only an estimate.

== Research Notes ==

The forms ''Kano'', ''Kame'' and ''Kaine'' should be retained as spelling controls until GD119/193 is inspected. The rare name, William Glasgow association and continued Calder-estate context make this a confident same-person identification, but no record states Alexander's relationship to William. Elizabeth may have been William's daughter, sister, niece or another close kinswoman.

50941012.Name: Glasgow-3916
50941012.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

Isobella Glasgow was married to [[Herbison-475|Archibald Herbisoune]], a fisher. On 27 January 1562/3 the spouses sold a Glasgow tenement on the street leading from the South Port to the bridge over the Clyde. Isobella appeared before a bailie and judicially ratified the transaction.<ref name="Iso1563">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 3, 1561–1568 (Glasgow, 1897), protocol 719, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n41/mode/2up p. 29], 27 January 1562/3.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

The consolidated Brady/Brade research relevant to this profile is maintained at [[Space:Brady Family of Sauchie, Stirling & Easter Kennet — Research Notes|Brady Family of Stirling and Easter Kennet — Research Notes]].

=== Probable parentage ===

[[Glasgow-1098|William Glasgow]] and [[Brade-232|Isobel Brade]] are probable parents on strong circumstantial evidence, but both relationship links remain uncertain because no act expressly calls Isobella their daughter.

On 28 October 1564 [[Glasgow-1093|John Glesgw]] received sasine as heir of William Glesgw, explicitly his father, in a fore tenement between the lands of the late John Rankin and Robert Young.<ref name="JohnHeir1564">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 3, protocol 805, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n69/mode/2up p. 57], 28 October 1564.</ref> Only nineteen days later John sold that same inherited fore tenement to William Craig. Isobella's husband Archibald Herbisoune witnessed the sale.<ref name="Archibald1564">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 3, protocol 810, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n71/mode/2up pp. 58–59], 16 November 1564.</ref>

This is a direct association between Isobella's proved husband and William's proved son during disposal of paternal inheritance. A close in-law relationship is the simplest explanation, especially because Isobella repeats the forename of proposed mother Isobel Brade and fits the generation. Nevertheless, the witness clause does not call Archibald John's brother-in-law; a trusted neighbour or occupational associate remains possible. The evidence therefore supports ''probable'', not proved, parentage.

The birth date is estimated from Isobella's married property ownership in 1563. She was alive on 27 January 1562/3; that transaction is not a death record.

=== Later Bridgegait evidence ===

On 18 January 1581/2 a neighbouring property's boundaries included the tenement of Archibald Herbertsoun, fisher, on the south side of Bridgegait, with Ninian Schyre's land to the east and the little common green to the south.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 8, protocol 2370, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00scogoog/page/n60/mode/2up pp. 36–37], 18 January 1581/2; Archibald Hegate's protocols, vol. 1, fol. 31.</ref> The name, occupation and street make this a probable later reference to Isobella's husband. It extends the family's property evidence, although the entry does not name Isobella or a Glasgow relative. The particular tenement has not yet been joined to the 1563 title, and this boundary reference supplies no new parentage statement.

== Sources ==
<references />

Spouses.Name: Herbison-475
Spouses.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==
'''Archibald Herbesoun''' was a fisher in Glasgow and the husband of
[[Glasgow-3916|Isobella Glasgow]]. On 27 January 1562/63 the spouses sold a
Bridgegait tenement; the record directly names Archibald's occupation and their
marriage.<ref name="Herbesoun1563">Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 3, protocol 719, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc06scogoog/page/n41/mode/2up p. 29], 27 January 1562/3.</ref>

Archibald was still alive on 19 December 1573, when Robert Glasgow, Archibald
Herbertsone and John Glasgow were collectively described as fishers in a
Bridgegait conveyance. His death is therefore after that date, with no proven
place.<ref name="Herbesoun1573">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2002, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n52/mode/2up p. 36], 19 December 1573.</ref> A 1575 conveyance refers to a tenement formerly belonging to Archibald Herbertsoun, fisher; that corroborates the property identity but does not prove that he had died.<ref name="Herbesoun1575">Renwick, ''Abstracts of Protocols'', vol. 7, protocol 2151, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc00robegoog/page/n114/mode/2up p. 98], 25 March 1575.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
The 1573 association with Robert and John Glasgow supports a close network
around Isobella, but no record calls either man Archibald's brother-in-law. An
Archibald Herbesoun described as a barker in 1559 and an Archibald Herbertsoun,
baker, in 1574 remain distinct candidates. No parent should be attached until a
record bridges the fisher to an earlier Herbesoun household.

== Sources ==

50941042.Name: Glasgow-3917
50941042.bio:
== Biography ==

Jonet Glasgow was married to William Pady. On 19 March 1582/3 the spouses acquired eight ells of land in Bridgegait, Glasgow.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 8, 1581-1585 (Glasgow, 1899), protocol 2478, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsofproto08glas/page/78/mode/1up p. 78], 19 March 1582-3.</ref>

The same couple remained together on 20 June 1598, when William Pady and Jonet Glasgow received an equal pro indiviso feu portion in St Teneu Street.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 11, 1597-1600 (Glasgow, 1900), protocol 3459, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc04renwgoog/page/74/mode/1up pp. 74-75], 20 June 1598.</ref>

On 17 July 1599 William Padyne, carter, was admitted a burgess and freeman of Glasgow as the husband of a burgess's daughter.<ref>James R. Anderson, ed., ''The Burgesses and Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573-1750'', Scottish Record Society 43 (1925), [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso43scotuoft/page/27/mode/2up p. 27], 17 July 1599.</ref> This is consistent with Jonet being a burgess's daughter, but the abstract names neither the wife nor her father. It therefore does not prove that her currently attached uncertain father, [[Glasgow-3522|William Glasgow]], was that burgess.

On 5 November 1600 William Pady conveyed property in favour of himself and Margaret Playfair, his future spouse.<ref>Robert Renwick, ed., ''Abstracts of Protocols of the Town Clerks of Glasgow'', vol. 11, protocol 3706, [https://archive.org/details/abstractsprotoc02scogoog/page/n207/mode/2up p. 170], 5 November 1600.</ref> Jonet's marriage to William had therefore ended by that date, but the record does not say whether Jonet had died or the marriage ended in another way.

=== Research Notes ===

* Birth: before 1565, Scotland, uncertain.
* Death: after 20 June 1598, place unknown, uncertain. William Pady's future marriage in November 1600 is not proof of Jonet's death.
* Spouse: William Pady.

The birth estimate assumes that Jonet was at least 18 at the 1583 purchase. The records do not identify her parents or children. The 1599 burgess entry supports only the broad proposition that William Pady had married a burgess's daughter; it does not name her father. She is not [[Glasgow-3183|Jonet Glasgow]], estimated born about 1600 at Mid Calder, who was not alive for the 1583 transaction. 

* the subject's given name Jonet recurs below 2 independent child branches of candidate's child George Glasgow (Jonet (Glasgow) Stewart branch: Jonet (Glasgow) Stewart; William Glasgow branch: Jonet Glasgow) (+26; catalogue rarity 12, Jonet in 14 profiles; grandchild-level echo, supports investigating the subject as that child's missing sibling)
