51164916.Name: Glasgow-3938
51164916.bio:
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

== Biography ==

'''Robert Glasgow''' was a cordiner in Edinburgh during the mid-seventeenth century. His date and place of birth have not been identified.

=== Marriage and occupation ===

Robert married '''[[Thomsone-50|Jonet Thomsone]]''' at Edinburgh, Midlothian, Scotland, on '''1 July 1652'''. The published Edinburgh marriage register prints her given name as Janet and describes Robert as a cordiner.<ref name="Marriage1652">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Robert, cordiner; Janet Thomsone 1 July 1652.” Scotland's People, Edinburgh marriages 685/1, reference 440/13.</ref>

In Older Scots, a cordiner was a cordwainer or shoemaker.<ref name="CordinerDefinition">Dictionaries of the Scots Language, [https://dsl.ac.uk/entry/dost00057534 “Cordiner(e), n.”], ''Dictionary of the Older Scottish Tongue'', accessed 4 August 2026.</ref>

No inspected record identifies Robert's parents or any children.

Robert's date and place of death have not been identified. He was alive on 1 July 1652.

== Research Notes ==

=== Possible Edinburgh burgess in 1666 ===

On '''4 July 1666''' a Robert Glasgow, also described as a cordiner, was admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh by right of his wife Euphame, daughter of the late Andrew Lorimer, beltmaker and burgess.<ref name="Burgess1666">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208: “Glasgow, Robt., B., cordiner, by r. of w. Euphame, dr. to late Andrew Lorimer, beltmaker, B. 4 July 1666.”</ref>

Scotland's People indexes four children of a Robert Glasgow and Euphame Lorimer or Laurimer: Eupham, 8 May 1651 at Edinburgh (685/1 50/395); Kathrin, 3 February 1659 at St Cuthbert's (685/2 30/28); William, 29 November 1662 at St Cuthbert's (685/2 30/53); and Magdalene, 14 August 1664 at Edinburgh (685/1 60/377).<ref name="LorimerChildren">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms: Eupham Glasgow, 8 May 1651, Edinburgh 685/1 50/395; Kathrin Glasgow, 3 February 1659, St Cuthbert's 685/2 30/28; William Glasgow, 29 November 1662, St Cuthbert's 685/2 30/53; Magdalene Glasgow, 14 August 1664, Edinburgh 685/1 60/377. Parents indexed as Robert Glasgow and Euphame Lorimer/Laurimer.</ref>

This persistent Lorimer household brackets the separate 1 July 1652 marriage of a cordiner Robert Glasgow to Jonet Thomsone. Combined with the 1666 burgess admission through Euphame, it makes the burgess very probably the father in the Lorimer household and strongly supports treating him as a different Robert from the 1652 bridegroom. The original images and cordiner records remain needed for proof, but the former “strong candidate” identification should no longer be preferred.

=== Birth, death and suffix ===

The former birth estimate of about 1612 is unsupported. No inspected record states Robert's age, birthplace or parentage.

For database purposes, his birth should be left unknown rather than estimated from compiled family trees. The only presently certain life range is that he was living on 1 July 1652. If the 1666 burgess is accepted as the same man, a death date after 4 July 1666 may be used, but should remain uncertain.

The former death estimate of about 1690 in Virginia is also unsupported. No burial, testament, probate record or other contemporary evidence has been supplied for that date or place.

The suffix “II” is a database label and does not appear in either inspected record. It should not be treated as part of Robert's name.

=== Parentage ===

'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' and '''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' have previously been attached as Robert's parents.

No inspected Scottish record identifies either person as his parent. The 1652 marriage entry names no parents. The possible 1666 burgess entry identifies Robert's wife and father-in-law, but not Robert's father or mother.

The elder Robert associated with Wester Duddingston in 1641 belongs to a separate record cluster. Shared surname, compatible chronology and residence in Midlothian do not establish a father-and-son relationship.

No Scottish record inspected identifies Deborah Ivey as the wife of the Wester Duddingston Robert or as the mother of this Robert. Both parental relationships should be removed unless contemporary evidence is found.

=== Children ===

No baptism, apprenticeship, burgess entry, testament, sasine or other inspected record identifies a child of Robert Glasgow and Jonet or Janet Thomsone.

The profile should not retain children merely because they appear in FamilySearch, Geni, Pedigree Resource File or other submitted family trees. Any proposed child requires an independent contemporary record linking that person to this couple.

=== Distinct from Robert Glasgow baptised in 1655 ===

This Robert was not '''[[Glasgow-1374|Robert Glasgow]]''', who was baptised at Edinburgh on 5 May 1655 as a son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.<ref name="Robert1655Baptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRSV-T1T Robert Glasgow, baptised 5 May 1655, Edinburgh], son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>

The present Robert married in 1652, nearly three years before that child's baptism. The two men must remain on separate profiles.

=== Unsupported Virginia identity ===

No inspected contemporary record establishes that this Edinburgh cordiner:

* emigrated to Virginia;
* married Ann Johnson;
* resided in Accomack, James City or Lower Norfolk County;
* was identical with Robert Glascocke or Glasscock;
* was the father of Daniel Glasco;
* was the father of Robert, Mary, Daniel or William Glasgow; or
* had descendants in Virginia or North Carolina.

The 1652 Edinburgh marriage record should not be combined with colonial Glasco, Glascocke or Glasscock material without a direct migration, probate, land or parentage record.

Ann Johnson and the attributed colonial children should be removed from this profile.

=== Name of spouse ===

The published Edinburgh register prints the bride's name as '''Janet Thomsone'''. The attached WikiTree profile uses '''Jonet Thomsone'''.

The original parish-register image should be inspected before preferring one form over the other. The differing forms should not be treated as evidence for two separate wives.

=== North Leith namesake, 1694 ===

A poll-tax page for North Leith dated 3 October 1694 lists '''Robt Glasgow''' among four servants in the household of Alexander Ainslie, clerk to the glass manufactory.<ref name="NorthLeith1694">National Records of Scotland, E70/4/10, North Leith poll tax, 3 October 1694, image 11, ''Scotland's People Virtual Volumes'', [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/virtual-volumes/volume-images/volume_data-E70-4-10/REX01666?image_number=11 original image].</ref> A later history dates the entry to 1695 and describes Robert as a glassmaker, but the original says only "servant". On 16 July 1694 a Robert Glasgow gave a receipt in Ainslie's name for bottles supplied to the Earl of Breadalbane.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Breadalbane Muniments, GD112/15/59, item 24, 16 July 1694, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD112%2F15%2F59 catalogue description].</ref> The shared employer and year make him almost certainly the October servant and prove a functional glassworks-business role, though not that he was a skilled glassmaker.

This profile's Robert was an adult in 1652 and could have been alive in 1694, but no record connects the North Leith servant to Jonet or Janet Thomsone or to the cordiner trade. The occurrence is therefore an unresolved same-name candidate, not a continuation of this biography.


[[Glasgow-3011|Robert Glasgow]], baptised at Glencorse in 1676, is a stronger younger chronological candidate for the 1694 servant: he was seventeen, is the sole exact-name Robert baptism returned for Glencorse from 1640 through 1690, and a same-name man married there in 1704. There is no direct Ainslie or glassworks link.

Exact Scotland's People OPR searches found no Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glaskow or Glassgow baptism in the Leith parishes from 1694 to 1730, and no exact Robert Glasgow marriage there from 1694 to 1710 or burial from 1694 to 1730. Register survival and spelling limit those negative results.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original Edinburgh parish-register entry for the marriage on 1 July 1652;
* Edinburgh baptismal registers for possible children of Robert Glasgow and Janet or Jonet Thomsone;
* Edinburgh burial registers for Janet or Jonet before July 1666;
* a marriage record for Robert Glasgow and Euphame Lorimer;
* the original burgess admission dated 4 July 1666;
* records of the Edinburgh Incorporation of Cordiners;
* Edinburgh apprentice records;
* Edinburgh Commissary Court testaments;
* sasines, deeds and burgess records identifying Robert's relatives;
* a burial or testament for Robert;
* evidence establishing whether the 1652 bridegroom and 1666 burgess were the same man; and
* any contemporary record identifying Robert's parents or children.

== Sources ==

* “Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XY9M-F56 Robert Glasgow, marriage dated 1 July 1652], record XY9M-F56.

51175040.Name: Glasgow-3942
51175040.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''Katherin Glasgow''' was buried in the Church of Ireland parish of St
Audoen, Dublin, on 3 November 1713. Her age, address, occupation and relatives
are not supplied in the cited entry.<ref name="DublinBurial">IrishGenealogy.ie,
Church of Ireland burial register, St Audoen, Dublin, p. 96, Katherin Glasgow,
3 November 1713, record identifier DU-CI-BU-25141,
[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/church/d-116-1-1-098.pdf register image].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible Saltcoats identity ===

A testament dative for John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats within Ardrossan
parish, names '''Katherine and Agnes Glasgow''' as his lawful children. John
died in December 1636, and the estate proceedings followed in April 1637. The
record also names Isobell Gray as John's widow but does not expressly call her
The girls' mother.<ref name="Saltcoats1637">National Records of Scotland,
Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/27, register pp. 478–480, testament dative and
inventory of John Glasgow, sailor in Saltcoats; original register working
transcription. Locate by reference through the
[https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills
Scotland's People wills search].</ref>

The Dublin woman was compared with John's daughter Katherine because her birth
and parents are unknown and a person alive in 1637 could have been buried in
1713. No inspected record carries the
Saltcoats residence, sailor household, Isobell Gray, Agnes Glasgow or a
Scotland-to-Dublin migration into the St Audoen burial. The two documentary
identities are not presently matched; name and theoretical longevity are not
enough. A separate Saltcoats profile is appropriate, with a later merge only if
positive evidence bridges the records.

The Dublin profile should not be assigned John as father or an estimated
Saltcoats birth without a bridging record.

The Dublin date is a burial date. It should not be described more precisely as
The date of death unless the register wording establishes that distinction.

== Sources ==
<references />

51184376.Name: Glasgow-3961
51184376.bio:
== Biography ==

{{Estimated Date}}
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

'''Elizabeth Glasgow''', recorded as '''Eliz Glascho''', was named in the 1669 Hearth Money Roll for Glenarm Town, Tickmacrevan parish, Lower Glenarm barony, County Antrim.<ref name="Antrim1669">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll, T/307/A; W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf surname transcription], record 5730, PDF p. 36 (accessed 17 July 2026).</ref>

Her appearance in the roll indicates that she was the person associated with a taxable hearth or household at Glenarm Town. The record does not state whether she owned or rented the property, nor does it identify her as a wife or widow. She may have been the head of the household, but that remains an inference.

The entry provides no age or birthplace. Elizabeth was therefore born before 1669, although the more specific estimate of before 1651 assumes that she was at least about eighteen when recorded and should be treated as uncertain.

The same return records James and Jo ''Glascho'' at Kilwaughter Demesne, in neighbouring Upper Glenarm barony.<ref name="Antrim1669" /> Their shared surname, close date and east-Antrim locations make membership of the same extended family possible. The hearth roll, however, records no relationship between them.

No parents, spouse, children or later records have been identified for Elizabeth with confidence.

=== Research Notes ===

'''Suggested profile data:'''

* '''First name:''' Elizabeth.
* '''Name as recorded:''' Eliz.
* '''Last name at birth:''' Glasgow.
* '''Other surname or spelling:''' Glascho.
* '''Birth:''' before 1651, place unknown, uncertain.
* '''Death:''' after 1669, place unknown, uncertain.
* '''Residence:''' Glenarm Town, Tickmacrevan parish, County Antrim, Ireland, in 1669.
* '''Parents, spouse and children:''' unknown; leave unconnected.

The birth estimate is based only on presumed adulthood in 1669. The source does not provide her age, and a less specific date of ''before 1669'' would also be defensible.

Glenarm was Elizabeth's recorded residence, not her stated birthplace.

Do not identify her as the wife of Archibald Glasgow or attach her to James or John Glascho of Kilwaughter without a record establishing the relationship.

A workbook search conducted on 17 July 2026 found no compatible WikiTree profile for an Elizabeth or Eliz Glasgow or Glascho born before 1700 with an association to Glenarm or Tickmacrevan.

== Biography ==

{{Estimated Date}}
{{One Name Study|name=Glasgow}}

'''George Glasgow''' was a Presbyterian ruling elder associated with the congregation at Keady, County Armagh, Ireland, in 1713.

He appears in material derived from the records of the General Synod of Ulster as:

: '''George Glasgow, R.E., 1713 — Keady, County Armagh'''

Here, ''R.E.'' denotes '''ruling elder''', a lay office within the Presbyterian church. The entry indicates that George represented or was associated with the Keady congregation at the Synod in 1713.

George’s date and place of birth are not recorded. An estimated birth before '''1693''' is used here only to allow for him being an adult by 1713. He may have been born considerably earlier.

The Synod entry does not identify his parents, wife, children, occupation outside the church, or exact place of residence. Keady identifies the congregation with which he was associated and should not automatically be treated as his birthplace.

No evidence has yet been found connecting George with the earlier George Glasgow recorded in Dublin, who died in 1676. The chronology demonstrates that they were different men.

=== Research Notes ===

* May be a grandson of [[Glasgow-1099|George Glasgow]]

'''Suggested profile data:'''

* '''First name:''' George.
* '''Last name at birth:''' Glasgow.
* '''Birth:''' before 1693, place unknown, uncertain.
* '''Residence or church association:''' Keady, County Armagh, Ireland, in 1713.
* '''Occupation/status:''' Presbyterian ruling elder.
* '''Death:''' after 1713, place unknown, uncertain.
* '''Parents:''' unknown.
* '''Spouse:''' unknown.
* '''Children:''' unknown.

The birth estimate is not based on a recorded age. It assumes only that George was an adult when serving as a ruling elder in 1713.

Keady should be treated as George’s recorded congregational association rather than a proved birthplace or precise residence. Synod lists commonly identify elders by the congregations they represented.

George should not be confused with '''George Glasgow of Dublin''', who died in 1676.

No relationship has yet been established between George and the Glasgow families recorded elsewhere in Ulster.

=== 1724 probate occurrence ===
An Irish probate index records a George Glasgow in 1724 without a usable residence or family description. The date is compatible with this George, but the name-only entry cannot identify the Keady elder.<ref>[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx Underlying record source: george glasgow].</ref>

51188450.Name: Glasgow-3967
51188450.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was a Presbyterian ruling elder associated with William
Taylor's Randalstown or Drummaul congregation at the end of the seventeenth
century. He was recorded beside Taylor at the General Synods of Ulster in
'''1698''' and '''1703'''. A ruling elder of the same name appeared beside
James Scott, minister of Duneane, in '''1705'''.<ref name="Synod">Presbyterian
Church in Ireland, ''Records of the General Synod of Ulster, from 1691 to
1820'', vol. 1 (Belfast, 1890), Synod records for 1698, 1703 and 1705;
[https://archive.org/details/recordsofgeneral01pres Internet Archive scan]
and [https://archive.org/stream/recordsofgeneral01pres/recordsofgeneral01pres_djvu.txt
searchable OCR text].</ref>

The close chronology, identical name and identical church office make the
1705 occurrence a probable further appearance of the same man. The published
entries pair ministers with elder representatives, however; they do not give
James's residence or say that he moved from one congregation to another.

=== Ruling elder for Randalstown or Drummaul ===

The 1698 Synod record pairs William Taylor with James Glasgow as ruling elder.
The same pairing occurs again in 1703.<ref name="Synod" /> William Taylor was
minister of the Presbyterian congregation associated with Randalstown and
Drummaul. Randalstown was not written as a residence beside James's name; the
association is derived from the known charge of the minister whom he
accompanied.

The repeated pairing establishes an enduring connection with Taylor's
congregation rather than a single incidental appearance. As a ruling elder,
James held a lay office in Presbyterian church government and represented his
congregation in the courts of the church.

{| class="wikitable" style="background:#e6ffe6;"
! Year !! Minister !! Ruling elder !! What the entry establishes
|-
| 1698 || William Taylor || James Glasgow || James represented Taylor's congregation.
|-
| 1703 || William Taylor || James Glasgow || The earlier minister-and-elder pairing was repeated.
|-
| 1705 || James Scott || James Glasgow || Probably the same elder, now representing beside the minister of Duneane.
|-
| 1705 || William Taylor || Robert King || Taylor had a different elder representative at the same Synod.
|}

=== Association with Duneane in 1705 ===

In 1705 James Glasgow appeared beside James Scott, minister of Duneane, while
William Taylor appeared with Robert King.<ref name="Synod" /> This change was
once interpreted as evidence that James had transferred from Randalstown or
Drummaul to Duneane. A move, a congregational boundary change or a formal
transfer could explain the pattern, but none is stated in the record.

Taylor also appeared with different elders in later Synods. Rotation or
substitution of congregational representatives is therefore a sufficient
explanation for the changed pairing. The evidence supports a probable
Duneane congregational association in 1705, but it does '''not''' prove that
James changed residence or permanently transferred congregations.

It remains possible that the Duneane elder was a second contemporary James
Glasgow. No independent record of another western County Antrim ruling elder
of that name has been found, and the identical name, office, neighbouring
congregational setting and two-year interval make one man the more economical
working identification.

=== Birth ===

James's date and place of birth are unknown. He was already serving as a
ruling elder in 1698 and must have been an adult by then. A conservative
working estimate is:

:'''born before 1678'''

That estimate allows him to have been at least about twenty in 1698; it is not
derived from a recorded age, and he may have been born considerably earlier.
Randalstown, Drummaul and Duneane are documented or inferred congregational
associations and do not establish his birthplace.

=== Family ===

No inspected Synod, land, probate or congregational record names James's
parents, wife or children. His occupation outside the church, exact residence
and place of origin are also unknown.

[[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]] is presently attached as an
uncertain father. No record identifies him as this James's father, so the
attachment remains a research hypothesis. The resulting links to
[[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-1499|Hugh Glasgow]] are likewise
uncertain rather than documented sibling relationships.

No descendant line from James has yet been proved. Uncertain attachments can
be retained as working links when clearly marked, but the surviving records do
not presently establish a wife or child.

=== Death ===

No death record has been identified. James was living in 1705, so the only
date supported by the evidence is:

:'''died after 1705'''

His place of death is unknown.

=== Distinction from James Glasgow of Kilwaughter ===

The ruling elder is distinct from [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of
Kilwaughter]]. The Kilwaughter man was recorded as James ''Glascho'' in the
1669 Hearth Money Roll and was active in the Larne and Kilwaughter
Presbyterian congregation by 1700. He became an overseer in that congregation
and was recorded as deceased in 1726.<ref name="Hearth1669">W. MacAfee,
[https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf
transcription of the 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll], Drummaul and
Kilwaughter entries, including records 5347–5348.</ref><ref name="Porter">Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and
Kilwaughter," ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864),
[https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

The strongest evidence for two identities is the 1703 Synod roll. This James
represented William Taylor's Randalstown or Drummaul congregation, while
James Caldwell separately represented William Ogilvie, minister of Larne and
Kilwaughter.<ref name="Synod" /> At about the same time, the other James was
active in the affairs of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregation, although he
does not appear in its surviving early roster of ruling elders.

Combining the men would require the same James to represent Taylor's
congregation at Synod while being established in the affairs of another
congregation whose own minister attended with a different elder. That is
possible in theory, but no evidence supports it. The records favour separate
identities. Separation of the two men does not itself rule out kinship; it
only prevents their records from being combined.

== Research Notes ==
=== Identity assessment ===

The strongest reconstruction of James's recorded appearances is:

:'''1698''' — James Glasgow, ruling elder paired with William Taylor.
:'''1703''' — James Glasgow, ruling elder again paired with William Taylor.
:'''1705''' — James Glasgow, ruling elder paired with James Scott of Duneane.
:'''1705''' — William Taylor separately paired with Robert King.

The 1698 and 1703 entries are near-certainly the same man. The 1705 Duneane
occurrence is probably the same man, but no surviving entry explicitly states
continuity of identity.<ref name="Synod" />

=== Why the Randalstown and Duneane occurrences are combined ===

The published Synod records pair each ruling elder with a minister. The place
is derived from the known charge of that minister:

* William Taylor — Randalstown or Drummaul.
* James Scott — Duneane.

The source evidence is therefore not literally "James Glasgow of
Randalstown" in 1698 and 1703 and "James Glasgow of Duneane" in 1705. More
precisely, it is:

:William Taylor — James Glasgow, 1698.
:William Taylor — James Glasgow, 1703.
:James Scott — James Glasgow, 1705.

This distinction explains why the three occurrences are combined under one
probable identity without turning the ministerial associations into exact
residences. Later indexes can obscure that distinction by presenting the
minister's congregation as though it had been written beside James's name.

=== Alternative explanation and possible residence ===

A second James Glasgow could theoretically have served Duneane in 1705. Under
that reconstruction, one James represented Taylor's congregation in 1698 and
1703 and another represented Scott's congregation in 1705. There is no
independent evidence for the second elder, so a single identity remains the
stronger hypothesis.

The Synod records do not reveal where James lived. He may have resided within
Drummaul parish, in or near Randalstown, within the district served by the
Duneane congregation, or in a locality between the congregational areas. A
move between 1703 and 1705 remains possible, but no tax, lease, estate or
other land record has been found to demonstrate it.

=== Possible descendants ===

No child of James has been identified from a contemporary record. The later
Bannside and Clough family of [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] and
[[McClure-6341|Jane McClure]] includes [[Glasgow-1780|Rev. James McClure
Glasgow]] and several documented siblings. It is a substantial later Glasgow
family in the wider western or mid-Antrim area, but no record connects John to
This elder.

Rev. A. R. Crawford compiled two histories of the Glasgow family, and later
typescript copies and additions survive in the Crawford and Glasgow family
papers at PRONI, reference D2003/MIC128. The publicly available introduction
begins the later household with John Glasgow of Bannside and Jane or Jean
McClure rather than identifying John's parents.<ref name="Crawford">PRONI,
D2003/MIC128, Crawford and Glasgow family papers;
[https://www.sommemidulster.org/dwd/pdfs/02002.pdf public introduction].</ref>
The manuscript histories may preserve an earlier generation, but they are not
publicly digitised and have not been inspected for this profile.

=== Similar surnames in western County Antrim ===

Seventeenth- and eighteenth-century records contain established families
named '''Glass''' as well as spellings resembling Glasgow. These names should
not be normalised automatically.

The 1669 Hearth Money Roll records John Glass at Andraid and John and Neile
Glass at Coolsythe in Drummaul. The same transcription separately renders Jo
and James ''Glascho'' of Kilwaughter as Glasgow.<ref name="Hearth1669" /> The
distinction shows that a Glass population was already established in
Drummaul before the first known Synod occurrence of this James.

The 1740 Protestant Householders' Return continues that pattern with Adam
Glass, John Glass and two Glass widows in Drummaul.<ref name="Householders1740">W. MacAfee,
[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf
1740 County Antrim Protestant Householders' Return], Drummaul and Duneane
entries.</ref> They may descend from the earlier Glass households and cannot
be treated as James Glasgow's children or grandchildren merely by changing
The surname.

Henry ''Glads'' appears separately in Duneane in the 1740 return.<ref name="Householders1740" /> The unusual form and locality make him the most
interesting unresolved spelling candidate for a son or younger relative of
James, but the return supplies no relationship evidence and does not establish
that his surname was Glasgow.

Useful search variants include:

* Glasgow.
* Glasgo.
* Glascho.
* Glaskow.
* Glask.
* Glass.
* Glads.

A variant should be assigned to this family only when chronology, locality,
associates or another record support the identification.

=== Relationship to the Kilwaughter family ===

No relationship has been proved between this western elder and the Glasgow
family established around Larne and Kilwaughter. They could belong to a wider
Scottish or Ulster family, and County Antrim Presbyterian migration patterns
make a connection plausible in general terms. No baptism, will, deed,
congregational minute or family record presently identifies a common ancestor.

The uncertain attachment to [[Glasgow-1081|James of Kilwaughter]] therefore
records a working theory, not a proved parent-child relationship. Evidence
belonging to the two men should remain separated unless a direct bridge is
found.

=== Record coverage and archive leads ===

Ordinary local church registers do not reach James's likely child-bearing
period. Old Randalstown Presbyterian baptisms begin in 1853; Randalstown First
marriages in 1845; Randalstown Second baptisms and session minutes in 1850;
and Duneane Presbyterian baptisms in 1864 and marriages in 1845. Broad searches
of those surviving registers cannot identify children born about 1695–1720.

The most important church source is the Presbyterian Historical Society
material catalogued by the Irish Manuscripts Commission as '''"Antrim
Presbytery: Parcel of minutes, 1697–1713"'''. The collection also includes an
earlier volume for 1671–1691 and Connor Presbytery minutes covering
1693–1735.<ref name="PHSIManuscripts">Irish Manuscripts Commission,
[https://irishmanuscripts.ie/womenshistorysources/index.php?whp_function=1&whp_identifier=6204
Presbyterian Historical Society collection description].</ref> The 1697–1713
parcel spans every known appearance of James and may record lay commissioners,
elder appointments, calls or congregational business not preserved in the
published Synod volume.

The archive's label needs care. The Presbyterian Historical Society's modern
timeline dates the Presbytery of Belfast to 1697 and the later, doctrinally
distinct Presbytery of Antrim to 1726.<ref name="PHSITimeline">Presbyterian
Historical Society of Ireland,
[https://presbyterianhistoryireland.com/history/timeline-for-presbyterianism-in-ireland/
"Timeline for Presbyterianism in Ireland"].</ref> The catalogue wording should
be retained when ordering the manuscript, but it should not be assumed to
describe precisely the same institution as the post-1726 Presbytery of Antrim.

A National Archives of Ireland packet concerning the Drummaul and Duneane
tithe dispute contains a return naming seventeen tithe payers at Coolsythe.
The online description does not transcribe those names.<ref name="CSO1833">National
Archives of Ireland, [https://csorp.nationalarchives.ie/search/index.php?browse=true&browseresults=true&category=27&offset=6060&subcategory=204
CSO/RP/1833/6068, original reference 1833/6354], 11 items and 27 pages.</ref>
Although much later than James, the return could test whether the local Glass
surname continued at Coolsythe.

The Registry of Deeds Index Project reports that its County Antrim townland
index transcription is complete for 1708–1820. The original Antrim index films
are 100382 for 1708–1738 and 100395 for 1739–1810.<ref name="DeedsIndex">Registry of Deeds Index Project,
[https://blog.irishdeedsindex.net/index.php/major-townland-index-update County
Antrim townland-index update], [https://irishdeedsindex.net/guides/townland_films.htm
townland-index film guide], and [https://www.irishdeedsindex.net/ project
database].</ref> A search of the public surname and townland indexes on 13
August 2026 found no early Glasgow, Glascho or Glads party at Andraid,
Coolsythe, Drummaul, Duneane or Randalstown. The indexed Andraid and Coolsythe
deeds were dated 1811–1820, while the two earlier Duneane entries named other
parties. This is a bounded negative result, not proof that James or his family
held no land: registered deeds were never a complete population record and the
volunteer person index remains incomplete.

=== Profile data supported by the records ===

* '''First name:''' James.
* '''Last name at birth:''' Glasgow.
* '''Birth:''' before 1678, uncertain estimate.
* '''Birthplace:''' unknown.
* '''Parents:''' no parents proved; the attached father is uncertain.
* '''Spouse:''' unknown.
* '''Children:''' unknown.
* '''Religion:''' Presbyterian.
* '''Office:''' ruling elder.
* '''Congregational association:''' William Taylor's Randalstown or Drummaul congregation, 1698 and 1703.
* '''Probable additional association:''' James Scott's Duneane congregation, 1705.
* '''Death:''' after 1705.
* '''Death place:''' unknown.

=== Research priorities ===

'''Original Synod and presbytery material'''

* Recheck the manuscript or highest-quality facsimile for the 1698, 1703 and 1705 entries, recording exact spelling, marginal notes and the order of ministers and elders.
* Inspect the PHSI parcel catalogued as "Antrim Presbytery: minutes, 1697–1713," especially Taylor's call and ordination business and the years 1697–1705.
* Look for elder ordinations, commissioner lists, substitutions, transfers, discipline cases or a description of James as formerly serving another congregation.

'''Randalstown, Drummaul and Duneane records'''

* Search any surviving session minutes, communion rolls, estate rentals and tax lists for James's residence, occupation or family.
* Determine whether the records explain when Robert King represented Taylor's congregation and whether James Glasgow joined or represented Duneane.
* Inspect the closest surviving 1740 return for Henry ''Glads'' and the seventeen-name Coolsythe return in NAI CSO/RP/1833/6068.

'''Land and probate'''

* Inspect the original Registry of Deeds townland-index images and relevant memorials for Andraid, Coolsythe and Duneane, checking spelling and parties omitted from the public index.
* Search County Antrim and Diocese of Connor probate material after 1705.
* Keep the 1727 probate entry for James Glasgow of Kilwater separate unless its contents prove otherwise; it probably belongs to the Kilwaughter man.

'''Family histories'''

* Inspect both Glasgow-family histories and the later typescript additions in PRONI D2003/MIC128 for the parents of [[Glasgow-1657|John Glasgow]] of Bannside and for copied records extending the family before the nineteenth century.

Later index to ruling elders; useful as a finding aid, while the published Synod records above remain the principal source. [https://archive.org/details/scotchirish00boltrich Internet Archive].

* '''MacAfee, W.''' [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll transcription], used to distinguish the Drummaul Glass households and the separate Kilwaughter Glasgow family.

51189069.Name: Glasgow-3970
51189069.bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date}} == Biography == {{YDNA 700 Earliest Known Ancestor|R-FT20271}} '''Robert Glasgow''', recorded as '''Robert Glaskow''' and '''Robert Glascow''', was associated with Larne, County Antrim, in four examinations taken in 1653 concerning the earlier death of Teige O'Sheale. The evidence establishes that a man of this name was locally remembered in connection with events following the outbreak of the 1641 rebellion. It does not establish his parentage, marriage, children or ultimate fate.Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 153r, examination of Con O'Sheale, Lisnagarvy, 21 April 1653, identifier 838153r210; 1641 Depositions Project, [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42821.html online transcription].Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 208r, examination of Captain James Collogh, 1 June 1653, identifier 838208r259; 1641 Depositions Project, [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/36082.html online transcription].Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 131r, examination of John Hill, 1 June 1653, identifier 838131r192; 1641 Depositions Project, [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42803.html online transcription].Trinity College Dublin, MS 838, fol. 218r, examination of William Willson, 1 June 1653, identifier 838218r266; 1641 Depositions Project, [https://1641dep.abdn.ac.uk/items/show/42875.html online transcription]. === The 1653 examinations === {| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding:20px; width:100%;" |+ '''Statements concerning Robert Glasgow''' ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Date ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Deponent ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Statement ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Evidential value |- | '''21 April 1653''' | Con O'Sheale | He had heard that James Browne and “one Robert Glaskow liuing in Larne” encountered Teige O'Sheale in a cottage. He attributed the fatal shot to James Browne. | Hearsay, but it supplies Robert's only explicit association with Larne. |- | '''1 June 1653''' | James Collogh | Jennett Woodsyde, wife of Robert Browne, had told him that Robert Glasgow shot Teige with a horseman's piece. | Second-hand testimony through a named informant. |- | '''1 June 1653''' | John Hill | He had heard it generally reported that Robert Glascow killed Teige O'Sheale. | Unattributed local report. |- | '''1 June 1653''' | William Willson | After returning to Islandmagee, he heard that Robert Glasgow had killed Teige but could not remember who told him. | Hearsay from an unidentified source. |} The four statements are not four independent confirmations. All are hearsay, and Con O'Sheale's version attributes the fatal shot to James Browne rather than Robert. The genealogically useful wording is:
one Robert Glaskow liuing in Larne
This identifies Robert with Larne in the account. It does not name a wife, child, sibling, parent, occupation or property holding. The wording also need not mean that Robert was still alive or resident there when the examination was taken in April 1653; it may describe him at the time of the reported incident. No examination of Robert, indictment against him or recorded judicial outcome has been located. === Date and origin === Robert's age and birthplace are unknown. The reported event occurred during the early rebellion period, when he was apparently old enough to travel in company with James Browne. A birth before about 1625 is therefore only a broad working estimate. No evidence yet connects him with the separate [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] baptised at Glasgow High Kirk in 1618, or with any other Scottish Glasgow family. == Research Notes == === Browne–McCullogh network and the 1653 transplantation list === Robert's only documented connection to this circle comes through the 1653 examinations: Con O'Sheale associated him with James Browne, while Captain James McCullogh repeated Jennett Woodsyde's accusation. Robert Browne's own examination named sons Hugh and James, and identified Hugh as a lieutenant in McCullogh's company, but it did not call Robert Glasgow a soldier, servant, tenant or relative. A government declaration dated 23 May 1653 survives as British Library 816.m.17[74], Wing I341. In the Islandmagee, Magheramorne and Ballynure quarter, the surviving print names Hugh Hoomes and James Lawder, together with Captain James McCullogh; it does not name James Browne or Ensign William Stephenson.Ireland, Commissioners for the Settling and Securing the Province of Ulster, ''By the Commissioners for the settling and securing the province of Vlster'' (Dublin: William Bladen, 1653), British Library 816.m.17[74], Wing I341; [https://catalog.folger.edu/record/538557 catalogue record describing the British Library original]. Robert M. Young's publication of William Pinkerton's manuscript-derived text instead places James Browne and Ensign William Stephenson in those two positions.Robert M. Young, ''Historical Notices of Old Belfast and its Vicinity'' (Belfast, 1896), pp. 80–86; [https://archive.org/details/historicalnotice00youn/page/80/mode/2up Internet Archive]. Young also printed a contemporary commissioners' letter saying that a local paper had been circulated before the declaration arrived and that the print was withheld because of “the great mistake of the printing the names.” The letter does not identify the mistaken names. Browne's absence from the surviving print is therefore real, but his inclusion in an intended or working schedule remains disputed rather than disproved. The contemporary administrative dossier survives in Trinity College Dublin MS 844, formerly F.3.18. Henry Jones's draft material of 14 June 1653 is at fol. 841, with further proposals dated 30 June; the relevant folios and enclosures have not yet been collated against the two list states.Judith Mary Carroll, “The papers of Henry Jones” (MSc thesis, Aberystwyth University), p. 82; [https://pure.aber.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/26062006/Carroll_Judith_Mary_MSc.pdf online PDF]. This is supporting network evidence only. Robert appears in neither list state; no record places him in McCullogh's company; and nothing connects McCullogh or the Brownes with either Jonet Cunningham. The result does not materially strengthen the proposed identification with [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow baptised in 1618]]. === Connection with the Kilwaughter Glasgows === The closest later Glasgow records occur at Kilwaughter, immediately inland from Larne. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="padding:20px; width:100%;" |+ '''Glasgow records in the Larne and Kilwaughter district''' ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Date ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Person ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | Place ! style="background-color:#E1F0B4;" | What the record establishes |- | '''c. 1641; recorded 1653''' | Robert Glaskow | Larne | Named in hearsay accounts concerning Teige O'Sheale. No relative is named. |- | '''1669''' | [[Glasgow-3913|Jo. Glascho]] | Kilwaughter Demesne | Liable householder in the County Antrim Hearth Money Roll.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, T/307/A, 1669 County Antrim Hearth Money Roll; W. Macafee, [https://www.billmacafee.com/1660shearthmoneyrolls/1669hearthmoneyrollsantrim.pdf surname-sorted transcription], records 5347–5348 and 5730. |- | '''1669''' | [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho]] | Kilwaughter Demesne | Separate liable householder entered immediately after Jo. Glascho. The roll states no relationship. |- | '''1669''' | [[Glasgow-3961|Elizabeth Glascho]] | Glenarm Town, Tickmacrevan parish | Same-surname householder elsewhere in east County Antrim. No relationship is stated. |- | '''1700''' | [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] | Kilwaughter | Represented Kilwaughter in arrangements for the Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian congregation.Classon Porter, “Congregational Memoirs—Larne and Kilwaughter,” ''The Christian Unitarian'', vol. 3 (1864), pp. 16–18 and subsequent extracts from the older congregational records; [https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive]. |- | '''1700''' | [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] | Kilwaughter | Separately named as an overseer for Kilwaughter. |- | '''1700''' | [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] | South side of Larne Water | Represented a different part of the congregation. His relationship to John and James is not stated. |} These records establish a continuing Glasgow presence within the Larne–Kilwaughter district. They do not establish that the 1653 Robert was father of [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-3961|Elizabeth Glasgow]]. The present WikiTree attachment of [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] as Robert's son is based on surname, chronology and neighbouring locations. No located record states that relationship. Robert could instead have been an uncle, brother, cousin, other collateral relative or an unrelated namesake. '''Conclusion: possible family connection; unproved. Jo/John and James Glascho were consecutive Kilwaughter Demesne householders in 1669, then recur in the same district's congregational business about 1700, when John represented Kilwaughter and James served as an overseer. This repeated association makes [[Glasgow-3913|John]] and [[Glasgow-1081|James]] probable close relatives, but no record states an exact kinship or proves either man was Robert's son.''' === A documented later Kilwaughter family === A later family can be established more securely. The surviving Larne and Kilwaughter Presbyterian register records the baptism of [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]], born 24 May 1731, as a son of [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] and Rachel Wilson.Larne and Kilwaughter Non-Subscribing Presbyterian congregation, baptismal register beginning 1720, baptism of James Glasgow, son of Robert Glasgow and Rachel Wilson, born 24 May 1731; Public Record Office of Northern Ireland microfilm and congregational register series. The original register image should be cited when available. A lease dated 13 February 1738, registered in 1742, was granted by William Agnew of Kilwaughter to [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]]. It named three lives: * Robert Glasgow; * Rachel Glasgow alias Wilson, his wife; * “James Glasgow junior”. The property comprised land at Ballykeel and Upper Ballykeel, Kilwaughter.Registry of Deeds, Ireland, memorial 74015, book 105, p. 301, deed dated 13 February 1738 and registered 12 April 1742; William Agnew of Kilwaughter to Robert Glasgow of Kilwaughter, naming Rachel Glasgow alias Wilson and James Glasgow junior as additional lives. The lease does not itself call James their son. Read with the 1731 baptism, however, the identification of “James Glasgow junior” as [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]], son of Robert and Rachel, is strongly supported. Sworn inheritance pleadings made in 1817 and 1818 by James's eldest son, also Robert Glasgow, state that Rachel Wilson married Robert Glasgow and left two children, James Glasgow and Ann Glasgow. The deponent identified James as his father and Rachel as his paternal grandmother. The pleadings arose from claims to the Wilson estate and included reference to a Ballykeel interest.South Carolina equity pleadings and associated Wilson–Glasgow inheritance papers, 1817–1818, sworn answers concerning the estate of Archibald Wilson. The pleadings identify Rachel Wilson as wife of Robert Glasgow; James Glasgow as their son; and the deponent Robert Glasgow as James's eldest son and Rachel's paternal grandson. Surviving online transcriptions should be checked against the original court papers. The resulting documented chain is: :'''[[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]]''' married Rachel Wilson :* '''[[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]]''', born 24 May 1731 :** later Robert Glasgow, James's eldest son, who gave sworn evidence in 1817 This is a genuine documentary family connection, but it begins several generations after the 1653 Robert. === The later Robert was not the 1653 man === [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] was married to Rachel Wilson, fathered a child in 1731, held the Ballykeel lease in 1738 and was still appearing in congregational business in the 1740s. The Robert associated with the early-1640s incident was already old enough to accompany James Browne. Even at an implausibly young age of about fifteen in 1641, he would have been about 112 in 1738 and about 121 in 1747. The two Roberts therefore should not be merged. The later Robert could have been a son, grandson, great-grandson, nephew or other relative of the 1653 Robert. No record yet specifies which, if any, relationship applied. === The missing generational bridge === The evidence currently produces two separate groups: :'''Early group''' :* Robert Glaskow of Larne, associated with events about 1641 :* [[Glasgow-3913|Jo. Glascho]] and [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho]], householders at Kilwaughter in 1669 :'''Later documented family''' :* [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] and Rachel Wilson :* their son [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]], born in 1731 The missing evidence is a record identifying the parentage of the later [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]], or naming the heirs or children of [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]]. A 1727 probate index entry exists for “James Glasgow, Kilwater”. The underlying pre-1858 probate file appears not to survive, so the index cannot establish his heirs.Diocese of Connor probate index, 1727, entry for James Glasgow of Kilwater. The entry establishes that probate proceedings once existed but does not preserve the will's contents or name beneficiaries. Later Y-DNA results reportedly place descendants of [[Glasgow-1144|James Glasgow]] in the same close paternal cluster as descendants attributed to another early-eighteenth-century northern Irish Robert Glasgow. This supports a shared paternal Glasgow ancestry among those later branches. It cannot determine whether the common ancestor was the 1653 Robert or identify the missing parent-child links.Glasgow surname Y-DNA project results and published project grouping for tested descendants of northern Irish Glasgow lines. DNA evidence supports paternal relatedness among the tested later branches but does not identify the seventeenth-century connecting ancestor. === Scottish candidate === A separate [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] was baptised at Glasgow High Kirk on 17 November 1618, a son of [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]] and [[Cunningham-20923|Jonet Conynghame]].National Records of Scotland, Glasgow High Kirk Old Parish Register 644/1, reported reference 10/272, baptism of Robert Glasgow, 17 November 1618. The reported entry names Robert Glasgow and Jonet Conynghame as parents. A derivative FamilySearch index also records a James Glasgow in Glasgow in November 1645, with parents named as Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunningham.“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” FamilySearch database, James Glasgow, November 1645, parents Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunningham, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK record VQHK-VMK]. This is a derivative index rather than an independent original record. No record places the Scottish [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] in Larne, names him as the man in the 1653 examinations or identifies the Scottish child James with [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]] of Kilwaughter. The profiles should remain separate. === 1666 shipmaster candidate === The Argyll Estates Archives catalogue identifies a receipt made in 1666 by a '''Robert Glasgow, master of the ''John of Portrush''''', for transporting barrels of coal for the earl of Argyll.Argyll Estates Archives, Campbell family, dukes of Argyll papers, “Various accounts and receipts,” 1666–1678, GB 3452 ARG-04-03-67-78, former reference PFV 67, catalogue p. 149, [https://www.argyll-papers.com/downloads/campbell-family-dukes-of-argyll-papers.pdf catalogue description]. The original receipt has not yet been inspected. A shipmaster working between the Scottish west coast and an Ulster-named vessel is chronologically compatible with both this Larne man and [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow baptised in 1618]]. The catalogue gives no age, residence, birthplace, kin or Larne connection, however, and the vessel name does not prove that its master lived at Portrush. He is therefore a relevant same-name candidate, not an identity bridge. The surviving customs records do not presently supply an easy substitute for the receipt. National Records of Scotland guidance explains that early customs books may name masters and merchants, but the E72 port-book series begins in 1668 and no Ayr or Irvine customs book for 1666 has been located in the fragmentary E71 material.National Records of Scotland, [https://nrscotland.gov.uk/learning-and-events/research-guides/customs-and-excise-records/ “Customs and excise records” research guide], accessed 31 August 2026. The original Argyll receipt is consequently the priority record for identifying this man. An NRS catalogue search found a possible later west-coast occurrence. An instrument of resignation and sasine at Ayr dated 6 August 1688 was written by '''Robert Glasgow, servitor to the notary''' Alexander McDermeit, depute clerk of the burgh.National Records of Scotland, GD86/741, instrument of resignation and sasine, 6 August 1688, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/browseDetails.aspx?reference=GD86%2F741 catalogue record]. A literate former shipmaster might later have worked for a notary, but the records are twenty-two years apart and neither gives age, kin or origin. The hand and signature should be compared with the 1666 receipt before treating them as one man; neither occurrence is identified with Robert of Larne. The original North Leith poll-tax page records another adult namesake on 3 October 1694. '''Robert Glasgow''' was one of four servants in the household of Alexander Ainslie, who was explicitly styled clerk to the glass manufactory.National Records of Scotland, Scottish Exchequer poll tax, North Leith parish, E70/4/10, image 11, 3 October 1694; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/virtual-volumes/volume-images/volume_data-E70-4-10/REX01666?image_number=11 original image], Scotland's People Virtual Volumes. A modern study describes Robert as a glassmaker and dates the tax to 1695, but the original page itself calls him only a servant and is dated 1694.Jill Turnbull, “The Scottish Glass Industry, 1610–1750” (PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh, 1999), pp. 171, 202, 324 and 350, [https://era.ed.ac.uk/server/api/core/bitstreams/fe29343e-a341-412e-85bd-96afca6214e5/content PDF]. A second contemporary record almost certainly concerns the same man: on 16 July 1694 Robert Glasgow gave a receipt in Ainslie's name for bottles supplied to the Earl of Breadalbane.National Records of Scotland, Breadalbane Muniments, GD112/15/59, item 24, 16 July 1694, [https://catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk/nrsonlinecatalogue/details.aspx?reference=GD112%2F15%2F59 catalogue description]. This proves a functional and probably trusted role in the glassworks business, though not the skilled occupation of glassmaker. Employment around the glassworks is plausible; a skilled trade and identity with the Larne, shipmaster or Ayr men are not proved. A stronger younger chronological alternative now exists: [[Glasgow-3011|Robert Glasgow]] was baptised at Glencorse in 1676, was seventeen in 1694, and is the sole exact-name Robert Glasgow baptism returned for that parish from 1640 through 1690. A same-name man married at Glencorse in 1704. This makes him a plausible candidate for the North Leith servant, although no record links him to Ainslie or the glassworks. It further reduces the 1694 entry's value as continuity evidence for this much older Larne man. Exact Scotland's People OPR searches found no Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow, Glaskow or Glassgow baptism in the Leith parishes from 1694 to 1730, and no exact Robert Glasgow marriage there from 1694 to 1710 or burial from 1694 to 1730. Register survival and spelling limit those negative results. === Priority Research === * Inspect the original 1666 Argyll Estates receipt, GB 3452 ARG-04-03-67-78, for its date, route, signature, endorsements, residence and associates. * Compare its hand and signature with the 1688 Ayr sasine, NRS GD86/741. * Inspect the 1666 County Antrim subsidy roll, PRONI T/808/14889. ** Search all forms including Glasgow, Glasgo, Glaskow, Glascow, Glascho and possible Glass entries. ** Determine whether Robert, James or John was recorded under the Kilwaughter estate before the 1669 hearth roll. * Search the Agnew of Kilwaughter estate papers. ** PRONI D282 contains leases, rentals and estate papers extending into the seventeenth century. ** NRS GD154/505–534 contains related Agnew and Kilwaughter material. ** Priority should be given to leases reciting former tenants, inherited interests, named lives or succession from one Glasgow tenant to another. * Inspect the archive-only records most capable of supplying the missing generational bridge. ** PRONI T/808/14889: the 1666 County Antrim subsidy roll. ** PRONI D/282/2–160 and NRS GD154/505–534: Kilwaughter estate leases, rentals, assignments and tenant succession. ** PRONI MIC/1B/6, including MIC1B/6A/1B: Larne and Kilwaughter congregational originals. ** MIC331 concerns William Ewart Gladstone papers and is unrelated to this family. T1762 and D2003/MIC128 are substantially later and lower-priority collections. * Reconstruct the complete title history of Ballykeel and Upper Ballykeel before the 1738 lease. ** Determine whether Robert and Rachel's holding had previously been occupied by [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]], [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] or another Glasgow. * Inspect the original Larne and Kilwaughter baptismal, marriage and session registers from 1720 onward. ** Record every Glasgow entry, witness, elder, townland and stated relationship. ** Seek an entry naming the father of [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]]. * Search the surviving Connor administration bonds, grant books and related probate indexes for [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow]]. ** Although the 1727 will itself appears lost, a collateral bond, grant entry or later estate proceeding may identify an administrator or relative. * Search the complete 1641 Depositions corpus and related Commonwealth judicial papers for Robert Glasgow and variants. ** Include James Browne, Robert Browne, Jennett Woodsyde, Teige O'Sheale, Larne, Islandmagee and Kilwaughter. ** A separate examination naming Robert's residence, occupation or household would be more useful genealogically than another repetition of the accusation. * Do not merge the 1653 Robert with [[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]] or [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]] without a documentary bridge. === Focused FamilySearch full-text search === A focused search of FamilySearch full-text material, restricted to seventeenth-century Larne and Kilwaughter, found no matching record for Robert Glaskow, James Glascho or John Glascho. The useful deed results begin in the later William Glasgow generation. A 1736 lease names William and Hugh Glasgow jointly,Registry of Deeds, memorial of lease dated 10 March 1736, Earl of Antrim to William and Hugh Glasgow of Larne. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSN1-FXR2 FamilySearch image]. and another record carries an adult William of Larne from witnessing a deed in 1744 to proving it in 1775.Registry of Deeds, memorial of deed dated 19 April 1744, with affidavit of William Glasgow at Larne on 6 January 1775. [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3Q9M-CSJW-C674 FamilySearch image]. Neither record bridges Robert to the proposed children or grandchildren. === Belfast maritime collateral candidate === [[Glasgow-3172|Captain James Glasgow of Belfast]] is a possible son or younger relative of Robert and a possible collateral of the later Kilwaughter householders. A Belfast-associated shipmaster active by 1667 fits the next generation after Robert's 1653 Larne occurrence, and Belfast, Larne and Kilwaughter form a plausible north-east Antrim maritime and estate corridor.Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, MIC19/2, maritime material naming Captain James Glasgow or Glascow as a Belfast-associated shipmaster in the late 1660s and 1670s; T/828/15, will extract for James Glasgow of Belfast, 1686. This is locality and chronology, not a stated relationship. Captain James must also remain distinct from [[Glasgow-1081|James Glascho of Kilwaughter]], who was still active in the 1720s and was apparently deceased only about 1726. == Sources ==

51189160.Name: Glasgow-3971
51189160.bio:
== Biography ==

James Glasgow was recorded at Glasgow on 25 November 1645 as the son of Robert Glasgow and Jonet Cunynghame. The register names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers.<ref name="SP1645">Scotland's People, Church of Scotland Old Parish Registers, births and baptisms, Glasgow parish 644/1, reference 40/56, James Glasgow, male, 25 November 1645, parents indexed as "Rot. Glasgow/Jonet Cunnyngham". Original register image inspected 31 August 2026; it names James Cunynghame and Johne Muir as godfathers but gives no occupation, residence, age or birthplace for Robert.</ref>

The attached father, [[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised at Glasgow in 1618, is chronologically compatible but is not identified by the index. That relationship remains uncertain. The attached mother, [[Cunningham-22604|Jonet Cunningham]], represents the woman named in the 1645 record.

This Scottish child has been proposed as identical with [[Glasgow-1081|James Glasgow of Kilwaughter]], County Antrim, first securely recorded there in 1669. No inspected record supplies migration, residence, occupation or family evidence joining them, so they must remain separate profiles.

== Research Notes ==

=== Godfather identification ===

The obvious James Cunningham, merchant and burgess admitted in 1629, had a testament confirmed on 31 January 1642 and therefore cannot have been the living godfather in 1645. Other men of the name—including James Cunningham of Easter Garden and later burgess entrants associated with Dunoon and Cobblehaugh—remain possible, but none has been connected to this baptism.<ref name="Indexes">James R. Anderson, ed., [https://www.electricscotland.com/history/records/scottishrecordso43scotuoft.pdf ''Burgesses & Guild Brethren of Glasgow, 1573–1750'']; Scottish Record Society, [https://archive.org/stream/scottishrecordso07scotuoft/scottishrecordso07scotuoft_djvu.txt ''The Commissariot Record of Glasgow: Register of Testaments, 1547–1800''], surname entries for Cunningham and Muir.</ref>

The same-name problem is greater for Johne Muir. The testament index excludes a Glasgow tailor whose testament was confirmed in 1640 and a mariner whose testament was confirmed in 1642. Men described in later entries as a maltman, weaver, doctor and of Langside could have been alive in 1645. An early John Muir in the cordiner membership material dates from 1585 and cannot be selected merely because James's possible grandfather was a cordiner. Both godfathers therefore remain unidentified.

== Sources ==
<references />

* "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQHK-VMK), James Glasgow, 1645. Derivative index to the same event.

51197795.Name: Glasgow-3974
51197795.BirthLocation: Kirknewton and East Calder, Midlothian, Scotland
51197795.bio:
== Biography ==

'''William Glasgow''' was baptised on 24 September 1671 in Kirknewton parish, Midlothian, Scotland. The parish index names his father as '''Andro Glasgow'''.<ref name="Baptism1671">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, William Glasgow, baptised 24 September 1671, son of Andro Glasgow; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-F2B FamilySearch record] (accessed 11 February 2020).</ref>

His father is represented on WikiTree by [[Glasgow-1319|Andrew Glasgow]].

No later record has yet been securely identified as belonging to this William.

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

This profile represents the William Glasgow baptised at Kirknewton on 24 September 1671, son of Andro Glasgow.<ref name="Baptism1671" />

He is distinct from [[Glasgow-1026|William Glasgow]], husband of [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]].

[[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]] was recorded on 21 April 1682 as a daughter of William Glasgow and Ann McCook.<ref name="Bessie1682">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch, Bessie Glasgow, 1682; [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4K-ZQN FamilySearch record].</ref>

The William baptised in September 1671 was only ten years old when Bessie was recorded. He therefore cannot reasonably have been the William who was married to Ann McCook and fathered Bessie.

The marriage to Ann and the family associated with her belong to [[Glasgow-1026|William Glasgow]], not this profile.

=== Birth and baptism ===

The indexed record establishes William's baptism on 24 September 1671.<ref name="Baptism1671" />

A birth date of 9 September 1671 has appeared in derivative material. The original Old Parish Register should be inspected before that date is treated as established.

The event occurred in Kirknewton parish, Midlothian. Later catalogue descriptions may call the parish "Kirknewton and East Calder", but that should not be interpreted as evidence that William was born at East Calder.

=== Father ===

William's baptism names his father as '''Andro Glasgow'''.<ref name="Baptism1671" />

The father is currently identified on WikiTree as [[Glasgow-1319|Andrew Glasgow]].

The original parish entry should be examined for residence, occupation, witnesses or other details capable of strengthening the identification of Andro with Glasgow-1319.

=== Later life ===

No reliable evidence has yet established William's marriage, children, adult residence, occupation, migration or death.

He should not inherit claims formerly attached to the conflated profile concerning:

* marriage to [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]];
* parentage of [[Glasgow-1545|Bessie Glasgow]];
* parentage of [[Glasgow-1318|William Glasgow]];
* the middle name "Walter";
* an association with Drummore;
* migration to County Tyrone;
* death in 1716;
* descent of later Irish or American Glasgow families.

Those claims either belong to [[Glasgow-1026|William Glasgow]] or remain independently unproved.

=== Priority Research ===

* '''Priority 1 — inspect the original 1671 baptism.'''
** Obtain the original Kirknewton Old Parish Register image corresponding to the FamilySearch index.
** Transcribe the complete entry.
** Record any separate birth date, residence, father's occupation, witnesses or other relatives.

* '''Priority 1 — reconstruct the Andro Glasgow household.'''
** Search Kirknewton parish registers for all children of Andro/Andrew Glasgow.
** Search surname variants including Glasgow, Glasgo, Glascow and Glassgow.
** Compare residences and witnesses across the entries to determine whether they belong to one household.

* '''Priority 2 — trace William after childhood.'''
** Search Kirknewton and neighbouring Midlothian parishes from approximately 1687 onwards.
** Prioritise records giving a residence, occupation, spouse, father or recurring witnesses.
** Distinguish these records from the older [[Glasgow-1026|William Glasgow]] and [[McCook-217|Ann McCook]] household.

* '''Priority 2 — test possible adult identities rather than assuming them.'''
** Compare any later William Glasgow candidate by age, parish, associates and family structure.
** Do not attach the Drummore, County Tyrone or "Walter" traditions without an independent documentary bridge.

== Sources ==

<references />

51221104.bio:

== Biography ==

'''John Glasgow''' was recorded in an Irish pre-1858 wills and administrations index in 1685. His residence was written '''Maghrebegg'''.<ref name="JohnProbate1685">Public Record Office of Northern Ireland, ''Pre-1858 Wills and Administrations'' index, entry for John Glasgow, index date 1685, residence "Maghrebegg"; transcription supplied to the project in July 2026. The public index can be searched through the [https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search]. The available transcription supplies no occupation, relatives, type of instrument or surviving original reference.</ref>

The record proves a same-name Irish resident and an estate or probate-related index event. It does not establish what the year represents, identify the place of death, or name a parent, spouse, child, executor, beneficiary or heir.<ref name="JohnProbate1685" />

The project map provisionally identifies the historical residence with '''Magherabeg''' in the Arboe and Loughinsholin area of County Londonderry. That modernisation is a close spelling and locality match, not a relationship record or proof of John's birthplace.

== Research Notes ==

[[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] was already an adult householder at Kilwaughter Demesne, County Antrim, in 1669 and had no known death date. He could have been the man indexed at Maghrebegg sixteen years later, but no record links the two localities. [[Glasgow-1498|John Glasgow of Cavers]] was an adult of the right generation, but no reviewed record places him in Ireland. [[Glasgow-551|John Glasgow]], estimated born about 1681, and [[Glasgow-2475|John Glasgow]], estimated born in 1685, were too young to be ordinary adult probate subjects in 1685.

51230723.Name: Glasgow-3990
51230723.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}

[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' represents an unidentified younger namesake implied by the
description of [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]] as "John Glasgow, senior" in
published extracts of the Larne and Kilwaughter congregational records.<ref name="Porter">Classon Porter, "Congregational Memoirs: Larne and Kilwaughter,"
''The Christian Unitarian'' 3 (1864), extracts from the congregational records;
[https://archive.org/details/christianunitari0003unse Internet Archive].</ref>

The word "senior" distinguishes an older John from a younger contemporary. It
does not state that the younger man was his son. [[Glasgow-3913|John Glasgow]]
is therefore attached as an uncertain working father, not a proved parent.

John's birth about 1680 is an estimate. No record has been found giving his
age, birthplace, wife or death, or proving a child.

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible identities ===

A '''John Glasgow of Killroot''' appears in the 1733 Connor diocesan administration-bond index.<ref name="Killroot">[https://apps.proni.gov.uk/ProniNames_IE/SearchPage.aspx PRONI Name Search], Pre-1858 Wills and Admons, sub-index Connor Diocesan Administration Bonds: John Glasgow, Kilroot, 1733; official detail inspected 21 September 2026. Occupation, notes and reference fields are blank. PRONI states that the original documents do not exist and no further information survives in this index. Individual result links are session-bound.</ref> He is the strongest record-defined
candidate for the younger namesake, but the index does not identify his father
or establish that he was the man represented by this profile.

[[Glasgow-3959|John Glasgow of Ballyboggy]] is currently attached as an uncertain son, not as a proved descendant or an identified same person. A 1740 return
records `Joh Glask` in the Ballyboggy locality, and a three-life lease from the
same year names John Glasgow and James Wier as joint lessees of one-third of
Ballyboggy.<ref>W. MacAfee,
[https://www.billmacafee.com/1740returns/1740protestantreturnsantrim.pdf 1740 County Antrim Protestant Householders' Return], Dunaghy entries; PRONI
`D2223/15/56`, Ballyboggy title-deed bundle.</ref> No record connects that John
to the older Kilwaughter man or proves the attached father-son relationship. If the 1733 administration-bond entry belongs to this profile, its deceased-estate chronology conflicts with identifying him as the man personally co-leasing Ballyboggy in 1740. An earlier relative remains possible, but unproved.

[[Glasgow-551|John Glasgow]] is associated with a separate traditional County
Tyrone family reconstruction. Similar name and estimated age do not establish
that the profiles are duplicates.

=== Family and descendants ===

No wife or descendant has been proved. [[Glasgow-3959|John Glasgow of Ballyboggy]] is attached as an uncertain working son; the attachment is a hypothesis, not historical proof. The word "senior" supports
only the existence of a younger namesake. The relationship could have been
father and son, but could also have been uncle and nephew, cousins or unrelated
men distinguished by age.

The decisive records are the complete Larne and Kilwaughter session material
at PRONI `MIC1B/6A/1B`, independent Kilroot estate or church material identifying the John in
the 1733 administration-bond index, and the three named lives in the 1740 Ballyboggy lease.

== Sources ==

51308553.Name: Glasgow-4009
51308553.bio:
{{Estimated Date}}

== Biography ==

== Research Notes ==

A live WikiTree person search and the creation-time duplicate check were repeated on 19 August 2026. No existing profile carried this exact 1685 Belfast event.

[[Glasgow-1078|Robert Glasgow]], baptised in Glasgow in 1618 and associated in the project research with Robert ''Glaskow'' living at Larne in 1653, is the leading candidate. Larne, Kilwaughter and Belfast form a workable east-Antrim and Belfast corridor, and the profile has no proved death date. The probate index nevertheless supplies no age, origin, occupation, spouse or relative capable of carrying that identity into Belfast.

[[Glasgow-3338|Robert Glasgow]], recorded before 28 May 1665 at St Cuthbert's, Edinburgh, was surfaced by WikiTree's creation-time comparison. He is chronologically possible, but no reviewed record carries that Scottish man to Belfast.

[[Glasgow-1502|Robert Glasgow]], estimated born about 1678 and later active in the Kilwaughter congregational records, would have been only about seven in 1685 and is not a credible ordinary adult probate subject without contrary evidence.

This profile therefore represents the Belfast record separately and remains unconnected. Do not merge it with [[Glasgow-1078|Robert of the Larne–Kilwaughter reconstruction]] or another namesake unless a surviving abstract, administration bond, diocesan index or estate reference supplies an identifying bridge.

== Biography ==

'''Robert Glasgow''' was recorded in the parish register of Holkham, Norfolk, England, in March 1559/60.<ref name="NRO-PD608-1">Norfolk Record Office, Holkham parish register, archive reference '''PD 608/1''', entry for Robert Glasgow, 23 March 1559 (Old Style); digital image and index, Findmypast, ''Norfolk Burials'', [https://search.findmypast.co.uk/record?id=GBPRS%2FNORFOLK%2FPD_608-1%2F01702&parentid=GBPRS%2FNORFOLK%2FBUR%2F004320950 Robert Glasgow, Holkham, Norfolk] (accessed 3 September 2026).</ref>

The register entry is in Latin and appears to read:

:''Robertus Glasgow[e] obijt''

that is, "Robert Glasgow died".<ref name="NRO-PD608-1" />

Findmypast indexes the event as a burial on '''23 March 1559''' at Holkham. The manuscript wording itself uses ''obijt'' ("died"), rather than an explicit form meaning "was buried".<ref name="NRO-PD608-1" />

Nothing presently identified in this record establishes Robert's age, birthplace, occupation, parents, wife or children.

=== Date ===

The register uses the English Old Style year, in which the new year began on 25 March. Robert's entry occurs on 23 March under the year 1559, immediately before the register changes to 1560 after 24 March. The date can therefore be expressed as '''23 March 1559/60'''.

For the WikiTree date field, which uses modern year numbering, the corresponding date is '''23 March 1560'''.

=== Research Notes ===

The surname is indexed by Findmypast as '''Glasgow'''. The handwriting in the original register is difficult, but the surname is consistent with ''Glasgow'', possibly written with a final ''-e''. Until a clearer image or another contemporary record is found, ''Glasgow'' is retained as the Last Name at Birth.

The Findmypast collection describes the event as a burial. Because the original entry appears to use the Latin ''obijt'' ("died"), this profile treats 23 March 1560 as Robert's death date rather than assuming that death and burial occurred on the same day.

No relationships should presently be attached to Robert solely from this record.

== Biography ==

'''William Glasgow''' was a servant to John Eastoun in Ormistoun, Roxburghshire, and was among the Covenanters taken at Cavers. Examined before Lord Elphinstone at the end of June 1679, he declared that he had been with the rebels eight days and had carried a gun.<ref name="FMP1" /> He is also listed among the banished who survived the shipwreck at the Moul Head of Deerness, and appears again as a servant at Ormistoun in a list of October 1684.<ref name="FMP2" /><ref name="FMP3" /> The records place him at Cavers and Ormistoun between 1679 and 1684; no birth, family or death is stated, so his birth is placed before 1679 and Cavers is inferred from the record.

== Research Notes ==

The 1679 deposition, the shipwreck-survivor list and the 1684 servant list are compatible stages in one man's record trail rather than three independently evidenced men. This documented Cavers man is also discussed as a same-name hypothesis on [[Glasgow-1605]], which represents a child baptised at Polwarth in 1658. No reviewed record connects that child with the Cavers man. Their identification remains unproved.

[[Glasgow-3587|William Glasgon]], who married Margaret Scott at Hummelknows in Cavers parish on 4 March 1708/09, is another possible later identity for this Cavers man. The marriage follows the 1684 servant record by about 24 years, but gives no age, occupation, parents or other link to the Covenanter. The two adult records remain separate pending a direct bridge.<ref name="Cavers1709">FreeREG transcription, Cavers marriage register, William Glasgon and Margaret Scott, 4 March 1708/09, “Married in Hummelknows”; FamilySearch, “Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910,” record [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYQG-3XD XYQG-3XD].</ref>

== Research Notes ==

They may represent two women, a remarriage, or a register/transcription discrepancy. Both named women and all three child entries remain recorded; no marriage, death or surname change is asserted without further evidence.

Compare the original 1718, 1720 and 1726 register pages, then search Libberton marriages and burials for Katherin Gibson and Katherine Watson.
